tasks.brief:
I'm the product lead on a metering node and I need a 10 MHz timing block built around a fixed small AT-cut crystal. It must start fast, stay settled, and follow an external 10 MHz disciplining tone that wanders by tens of ppm. Power is scarce, but a block that settles late or slips lock corrupts field timestamps.

Fixed inputs:
- Supply: 3.0 V DC through 1 ohm source resistance.
- Crystal: parameters and corner multipliers are in /app/input_assets/crystal.json. It connects between pins xa and xb.
- Load on pin out: 10 kohm in parallel with 5 pF to ground.
- Reference tone on pin ref: 150 mV peak sinusoid through 1 kohm source resistance, frequency 10 MHz plus or minus 20 ppm.
- Allowed parts and parameter ranges: /app/input_assets/allowed_devices.json. Nothing else may be used.

Topology, gain, loading, injection point and strength, bias and start-up arrangement are yours to choose.

Deliverable: /app/output/osc.cir, a SPICE netlist containing one subcircuit named osc with ports in the order vdd gnd xa xb out ref.

Every requirement must hold at all crystal corners: Rm x0.75 to x1.25, C0 x0.9 to x1.1, series resonance -8 to +8 ppm. Every simulated case is observed from supply application (t=0) to t = 1.5 ms.

Definitions: a window is 50 consecutive cycles; the window envelope change is (max-min)/mean of the per-cycle peak amplitude in it. Settling time is the earliest time t_s such that every 50-cycle window starting at or after t_s, up to 1.5 ms, has envelope change under 1 percent.

Requirements:
1. Cold start from zero stored energy, reference off: settling time at most 400 microseconds after supply application.
2. Free-run, nominal crystal, after settling: amplitude of consecutive 100-cycle windows differs by at most 0.5 percent and frequency by at most 5 ppm.
3. Output RMS amplitude at out is 0.8 to 1.4 V in every settled state, free-run or locked.
4. Crystal drive power (motional-branch RMS current squared times that corner's Rm) is at most 100 microwatts in every settled state.
5. Average supply current is at most 1.2 mA in every settled state.
6. Locked state, reference anywhere in 10 MHz plus or minus 20 ppm, supply and reference applied together: over the 2000 cycles starting 600 microseconds after application, the output phase against the reference has no cycle slip (unwrapped excursion under 180 degrees) and, after linear detrending, peak-to-peak phase spread of at most 3 degrees.
7. After a 2 microsecond total supply dropout from a settled locked state, with observation running 1.5 ms from the supply returning: settling time (as defined, measured from the supply returning) is at most 600 microseconds, and requirement 6 holds over the 2000 cycles starting 600 microseconds after the supply returns.
8. Numerical resolution independence: halving the base time resolution moves the requirement 1 settling time by at most 20 microseconds and the requirement 6 phase spread by at most 1 degree.
9. The netlist uses only allowed parts, within their ranges and placement rules.
tasks.handbook:
Handbook (reference data and conventions)

Crystal. Series Rm-Lm-Cm branch in parallel with C0. Series resonance fs = 1/(2 pi sqrt(Lm Cm)), about 10.000 MHz here. Motional Q = 2 pi fs Lm / Rm is about 12,600 for the unloaded part. Parallel resonance sits above fs by about fs*Cm/(2 C0) (roughly 0.35 percent). A load capacitance CL in series with the crystal pulls frequency by about Cm/(2 (C0+CL)^2) per farad, of the order of 20 ppm per pF for CL near 20 pF. Series resistance in the crystal branch lowers loaded Q to 2 pi fs Lm / (Rm+Rext).

Envelope dynamics. The amplitude envelope follows a first-order law with time constant about 2 Lm / (Rm + Rext + Rneg), where Rneg is the negative resistance presented by the active circuit (Rneg is negative in sign for gain, so the denominator shrinks as gain rises). Near-unity loop gain and high loaded Q make this time constant long (hundreds of microseconds). Large excess gain shortens start-up but raises crystal current and distortion. Limiter recovery also slows as loop gain approaches unity.

Injection locking (Adler). Lock range as a fraction of frequency is roughly (1/(2 Q_L)) * (I_inj / I_osc), with Q_L the loaded Q and I_inj / I_osc the injected-to-oscillating current ratio at the injection point. Lock-in time constant scales as the inverse of the lock range. Phase offset in lock is asin(detuning/lock range), so detuning near the lock-range edge makes phase sensitive to disturbances. Strong injection also pulls amplitude and frequency.

Drive level. P = Irms^2 * Rm with Irms the current in the motional branch (through Lm). Small AT-cut crystals are typically rated 10 to 200 microwatts.

Measurement definitions.
- Envelope: peak amplitude per cycle of the out-node fundamental.
- RMS amplitude: over whole cycles in the stated window.
- Frequency: from interpolated zero crossings over the 100-cycle window.
- Phase against the reference: per-cycle phase of the out-node fundamental minus reference phase, unwrapped; detrending removes a least-squares straight line over the window.
- Supply current: time-average current delivered by the 3.0 V source over whole cycles in the settled window.
- Settled state: any state after the settling time defined in the brief.
- Timestep change: the same case simulated at the base step and at half that step.

Test conditions. Supply application is a 1 microsecond ramp from zero with all node voltages and inductor currents starting at zero. A 10 microamp, 10 ns current pulse is applied across xa-xb at the start for numerical seeding. The reference is off for free-run tests and on from time zero in locked tests. The supply dropout takes the supply source to 0 V for 2 microseconds with 0.1 microsecond edges. Reference offsets are sampled anywhere inside the declared band, including between band edges. Corners are combinations of the multipliers in crystal.json. Time integration uses tight tolerances.

Practical ranges. Saturating tanh transconductors self-limit amplitude near Isat times the load impedance. Supply current is dominated by active-source current. A 3 V supply with 1 ohm source has negligible droop at 1 mA.
tasks.review:
### 10-10mhz-crystal-clock-block-settled-and-locked · Crystal clock block that settles and locks across corners — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "Topology, gain, loading, injection point and strength, bias and start-up arrangement are yours to choose"; deliverable is a SPICE subcircuit netlist.

Forge task: Design a <=40-element SPICE subcircuit (R, C, L, linear VCCS, tanh current source, up to 4 D1 diodes; only vdd as current-sourcing terminal) implementing a 10 MHz crystal-referenced oscillator that settles within 400 us cold, delivers 0.8-1.4 V RMS into 10 kohm || 5 pF, keeps motional drive <=100 uW and supply current <=1.2 mA, locks to a 150 mV-pk 10 MHz +/-20 ppm reference with no cycle slip and <=3 deg detrended phase spread, at all corners (Rm x0.75-1.25, C0 x0.9-1.1, fs +/-8 ppm), and recovers within 600 us after a 2 us supply dropout.

Why it fits:
- The deliverable is a design artifact (chosen topology and component values), not analysis; the checker builds its own bench and runs headless ngspice transients plus a Python static parse (element types, ranges, count, port order, placement rule).
- Genuine coupled trade-off: excess loop gain shortens the envelope time constant but raises crystal drive and supply current; injection strength buys Adler lock range but pulls amplitude and frequency; robustness across corners, held-out reference offsets and a halved timestep forces deliberate margin rather than a knife-edge nominal tuning.
- Bounded design space: <=40 ideal elements from a closed allowed list, fixed crystal model, explicit numeric limits.

What stops it:
- Structural: nothing. As written it is a design decision, doable in principle and script-checkable.
- Unresolved feasibility risk: no passing design has been demonstrated. The reference outline is a proposed solution and the author states "thresholds are provisional until a reference passes"; whether R1 (<=400 us settling), R4 (<=100 uW at Rm x0.75) and R6 (<=3 deg at +/-20 ppm detuning) are simultaneously satisfiable at 1.2 mA is an author claim, not verified evidence.
- Unresolved runtime risk: 1.5 ms at 10 MHz is ~15,000 cycles per transient; 27 corner combinations plus undisclosed reference offsets, cold-start/locked/dropout cases and half-step reruns could exceed both the agent budget and the grader budget. Unmeasured.
- Spec ambiguity (not a missing number per se): the phase metric "per-cycle phase of the out-node fundamental minus reference phase" needs a pinned extraction formula and window alignment, since R6/R8 margins are ~1-3 degrees.

How to check it:
- ngspice (headless transient): checker-built bench (3.0 V + 1 ohm, Rm-Lm-Cm || C0 with corner multipliers from crystal.json, 10 kohm || 5 pF load, 150 mV-pk 10 MHz +/-20 ppm sine through 1 kohm, 10 uA/10 ns seeding pulse, 2 us dropout with 0.1 us edges); numpy computes 50-cycle envelope settling, waveform RMS over whole cycles, Irms^2*Rm in the motional branch, mean supply current, interpolated zero-crossing frequency, unwrapped fundamental phase and detrended peak-to-peak.
- Python static parse of osc.cir against allowed_devices.json: element set, parameter ranges, <=40 elements, .subckt osc vdd gnd xa xb out ref, G/B first node at vdd, forbidden directives absent.

Simulation gaps:
- Ideal elements: no parasitics, no PCB/package capacitance, no transconductor output conductance or headroom limits beyond the tanh form, no noise sources (phase jitter, AM noise, reference amplitude noise), no temperature drift.
- Crystal model is fixed and linear; drive-level dependence of Rm, activity dips, and shunt-path nonlinearity are not modeled, so passing drive-power limits in simulation does not guarantee safe drive in hardware.
- Numerical: R8 probes only two step sizes; convergence of tanh B-sources and diodes at startup, and the sensitivity of the settling-window definition to integration method, remain uncertain.
- Robustness to held-out reference offsets near band edges and to the undisclosed dropout instant depends on the checker's sampling; corner coverage in the agent's own loop is likely sparser than the grader's.

Why frontier models fail: hypothesis, not demonstrated. The plausible difficulty is real engineering coupling — envelope time constant, drive level, injection lock range, amplitude and supply current move in opposite directions, and corner/wander/timestep variation punishes a nominal-point optimum. Predicted failures of the named public topologies (Pierce settling ~1 ms, Colpitts drive >100 uW, near-unity-gain loops slipping at band edges) are author claims pending reproduction.

Real-world risks:
- A tanh transconductor and ideal D1 diodes are abstractions; real 3 V implementations face headroom, output swing and loading not represented here.
- Passing the checks establishes simulated functionality at declared corners only; jitter/phase noise, temperature, aging, supply ripple and layout parasitics are unassessed.
- The measurement conventions (fundamental projection, zero-crossing interpolation) can move R6/R8 results by a non-trivial fraction of their margins.

Milestones (if split is desired; not required):
1. Free-run oscillator meeting R1-R5 at all corners: grader checks settling, RMS, drive power, supply current.
2. Injection-locked variant meeting R6 at held-out offsets: grader checks slip count and detrended phase spread.
3. Dropout recovery and step-independence meeting R7-R8: grader checks re-settling and half-step deltas.

What to change (reshape): nothing. The brief already fixes one process/medium (SPICE netlist), one deliverable and one bench; pinning the phase-extraction formula and the numerical settings belongs in "Numbers to supply next".

Evidence status: draft-only input. Requirements text, crystal.json and allowed_devices.json contents are supplied text; I have not inspected /app/input_assets or run any simulation. The reference outline, distinct_valid_designs list, public-design failure claims, mechanism-survival narrative and the "thresholds are provisional" note are author claims. Named asset paths are specified dependencies, not verified assets. Feasibility of the joint limits and all runtimes are unverified.

Checks before full-task readiness:
- Produce and run at least one reference netlist through the full grader set (cold start, free-run, locked at held-out offsets, dropout, half-step reruns) and record pass margins; or reproduce the claimed baseline failures to confirm the tests discriminate.
- Measure ngspice runtime for a 1.5 ms transient at the intended tolerance and total sweep cost across 27 corners x offsets x cases x 2 steps; trim the sweep if it does not fit.
- Pin the phase-extraction formula, window alignment and zero-crossing interpolation so R6/R8 are reproducible across implementations; state the trap/gear choice and maxstep.
- Confirm ngspice accepts the specified tanh B-source form and .model D1 exactly as the static parser expects, and that seeding pulse and dropout are applied deterministically.
- Verify /app/input_assets/crystal.json and /app/input_assets/allowed_devices.json exist and load.

Numbers to supply next:
- Requirement (spec): base time resolution and tolerance set — e.g. maxstep 0.5 ns, reltol 1e-6, trap integration; halved step = 0.25 ns.
- Requirement (spec): exact phase metric — e.g. least-squares projection of out onto cos/sin at the reference frequency over each 100-cycle window, phase = atan2 of coefficients, unwrapped across windows.
- Requirement (spec): dropout instant range and reference phase at t=0 — e.g. dropout between 1.0 and 1.2 ms after application; ref phase 0 at t=0; reference offset sampling list policy (e.g. 5 fixed held-out offsets drawn by seed).
- Requirement (spec): grading runtime budget and case count — e.g. <=30 min CPU per netlist, 27 corners x 5 offsets max.
- Interface (specified, assets unverified): inputs /app/input_assets/crystal.json and /app/input_assets/allowed_devices.json (contents supplied); output /app/output/osc.cir (schema supplied); still needed: the checker bench netlist template and the exact numpy measurement functions used for R1-R8.
- Handbook data (spec): crystal drive rating used for R4 justification — e.g. 10-200 uW typical for small AT-cut; transconductor Isat and Vs usable ranges already given in allowed_devices.json.
- Verification still needed (not spec): a demonstrated passing design, reproduced failure of at least one listed public topology, and measured simulation runtimes/noise at the two timesteps.

tasks.brief:
I need a 12 V to 5.0 V power block for our mixed-signal sensor board. The 12 V digital rail is noisy. A 16-bit converter sampled at 250 kS/s, asynchronous to the block's clock, reads the 5.0 V analog rail, and anything that aliases into 0-20 kHz shows up as reading noise. The board clock driving the block is spread-spectrum, so the block must hold across the whole wander, not only at nominal.

Fixed interfaces
- Subcircuit `abk` with ports in this order: vin12 vout5 clk dgnd a b c.
- Ground copper dgnd-a-b-c is in /app/input_assets/ground_network.cir (subcircuit GNET, 8 mohm + 6 nH per segment). The converter reference and the load return are at node c. Your block may connect its returns to any of dgnd, a, b, c.
- The 12 V source returns to dgnd through 0.5 ohm + 100 nH in series, with twelve noise tones of 10 mV each between 0.1 and 5 MHz.
- clk is a 0/3.3 V logic input: triangular spread 0.9-1.1 MHz at 30 kHz rate, 3 ns edges, 0.3 ns rms jitter. The whole spread profile may sit anywhere from 0.97x to 1.03x of nominal.
- Load 10-60 mA, resistive, from vout5 to c.
- Power path uses only the parts in /app/input_assets/parts.cir (SWX switches, INDQ inductors, CAPX capacitors) plus plain resistors. Capacitors vary +/-15% and inductors +/-10%. Control circuitry (behavioral sources, small R/C) may sense any node but may only drive switch control pins, may not use time or any clock other than clk, and its own power is covered by a fixed 1 mW added to input power.

Definitions
- Rail = V(vout5) - V(c).
- In-band noise = rms of the 0-20 kHz content of the rail, sampled by an ideal unfiltered 250 kS/s sampler at any sampling phase, mean removed, over a record of at least 2 ms after 1 ms of settling.
- Efficiency = mean load power / (mean power from the 12 V source + 1 mW), over whole 33.3 us clock-modulation periods.

Requirements (all with loads of 10, 35 and 60 mA, any clock offset in range, any component corner, unless stated)
1. Mean rail 4.90 V to 5.10 V.
2. In-band noise <= 20 uV rms.
3. In-band noise <= 25 uV rms with an additional 150 mA peak, 1.013 MHz sine current injected between node a and dgnd.
4. Efficiency >= 80% at 35 mA and >= 70% at 10 mA.
5. Load step 10 -> 60 mA in 1 us: rail inside 4.90-5.10 V within 40 us and stays inside for the next 160 us.
6. Start-up at 35 mA with 12 V ramping 0 -> 12 V in 20 us: rail enters 4.90-5.10 V within 300 us, never exceeds 5.5 V, and stays inside afterwards.
7. Switch area sum(0.15 ohm / ron) <= 4.0 over all SWX instances, ron between 0.15 and 2 ohm; total inductance <= 10 uH.
8. The in-band noise result must be numerically converged: it changes by no more than 20% or 2 uV, whichever is larger, when the time resolution of the evaluation is made twice as fine.

Deliver /app/output/abk.cir: a SPICE netlist defining subcircuit abk. Do not include the parts file; it is loaded for you.
tasks.handbook:
Parts file (parts.cir): SWX is a binary switch: closed resistance ron when V(c,r) > 1.65 V, 100 Mohm otherwise. INDQ has series resistance 2*pi*1 MHz*L/30 (Q = 30 at 1 MHz). CAPX has ESR = 0.02/sqrt(C in uF) ohm. Each has tolerance parameters (kc, kr, kl, default 1) that are scaled for corners. Usable capacitance range is about 10 nF to 100 uF.

Noise tones on the 12 V source: 0.105, 0.43, 0.6, 0.82, 1.255, 1.7, 2.35, 3.0, 3.76, 4.4, 4.99 MHz and one additional tone at 0.27 MHz, each 10 mV peak with zero phase.

Sampling background: a tone at f aliases to |f - k*250 kHz| for the nearest integer k. Anything whose alias lands within 0-20 kHz counts as in-band, and a fold to exactly 0 Hz is removed with the mean. Under a 30 kHz triangular spread of +/-100 kHz, a switching fundamental and its harmonics sweep their alias frequency across the band instead of sitting on one value. Tuned notches and traps have a bandwidth of a few percent, and a +/-15% capacitor or +/-10% inductor tolerance moves their center by 5-8%.

Practice: ripple of a buck-type stage is about (1-D)*Vo/(8*L*C*f^2) peak-to-peak before ESR. LC corner attenuation is 40 dB/decade per stage above the corner. Inductor DCR, ESR and switch Ron set conduction loss. Return current in a ground segment produces a voltage of about I*(R + j*2*pi*f*L). A 6 nH segment is 38 mohm at 1 MHz, so about 8 mohm + 38 mohm per segment. Anything that shares the analog reference path with pulsed current appears directly in the rail as the converter sees it. Sensing the output at the converter reference removes drops in the return from the regulated quantity.

Simulation practice: edge transitions of 3 ns need time steps of about 0.5 ns or finer near edges and 5-20 ns elsewhere. Start-up ramps and load steps need the return to settle before the stay-inside window is evaluated.

Sampling phase: the sampler is asynchronous, so its phase relative to clk is arbitrary. Test with several offsets within one 4 us sample period.
tasks.review:
### 11 · Quiet 5 V analog rail with spread clock and ground-return partition — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "I need a 12 V to 5.0 V power block for our mixed-signal sensor board" with "Deliver /app/output/abk.cir: a SPICE netlist defining subcircuit abk". The agent chooses the converter topology, filter staging, where each return ties into the dgnd-a-b-c copper, switch ron/area, inductor/capacitor values, and the control law built from `clk` alone.

Forge task: design a subcircuit `abk vin12 vout5 clk dgnd a b c` (SWX/INDQ/CAPX + resistors in the power path; behavioral control only on switch pins) that delivers 4.90–5.10 V into 10–60 mA from a noisy 12 V rail with a spread-spectrum 0.9–1.1 MHz clock, holding ≤20 µV rms aliased 0–20 kHz rail noise at 250 kS/s (≤25 µV with a 150 mA / 1.013 MHz burst into a→dgnd), ≥80% / ≥70% efficiency at 35 / 10 mA, load-step and start-up band entry, sum(0.15/ron) ≤ 4.0 and Ltotal ≤ 10 µH, plus timestep-converged noise numbers.

Why it fits:
- It is a design decision (a circuit), not analysis: the deliverable is a netlist the agent must synthesize; the simulation is the grader's instrument.
- Every requirement maps to a scripted check: ngspice transients for R1/R2/R3/R5/R6, waveform-integrated power for R4, a statement parser for R7, and a re-run at half timestep for R8. No human-in-the-loop measurement is needed.
- The core engineering tension is real and survives translation to simulation: spread spectrum plus component tolerance kills tuned traps, so attenuation must be broadband; broadband filtering plus a 12→5 V step-down fights the efficiency and area limits; and the ground-return partition plus Kelvin sensing at node c is exactly the classical quiet-rail problem.
- The aliasing definition (tone at f folds to |f − k·250 kHz|, DC folds removed) is stated precisely enough to implement deterministically.
- Multiple valid architectures are plausible (cascaded buck + LC, interleaved, switch-cap front end), so the task does not secretly encode one reference topology.

What stops it:
- Structural objections: none. The idea as written is a bounded single-deliverable design task.
- Unresolved feasibility risks (not yet demonstrated): (a) the reference outline is an author proposal, not a passing design — no run showing ≤20 µV rms at all corners exists in the payload; (b) full-grid verification cost is unknown: ~3 loads × several clock scales × corner sets × burst on/off × several sampling phases × two timesteps is on the order of 50+ transients of 2–3 ms each with 0.5 ns steps near 3 ns edges; if each run takes minutes, the grader sweep and an agent's iteration loops may exceed a two-hour run; (c) the corner scaling of kc/kr/kl is not quantified anywhere in the payload; (d) the parts library's behavioral expression `V(d,s)/(V(c,r) > 1.65 ? {ron} : 1e8)` and the `8m` / `6n` suffixes must be confirmed to parse and behave as intended in the pinned ngspice version; (e) R8 as written (change ≤20% or 2 µV when halving the step) can be satisfied trivially if the base step is already fine — the discriminator depends on how the checker picks the base step and how it handles the 3 ns edges.

How to check it:
- ngspice (transient, variable timestep): mean rail, rail waveform during the 10→60 mA step and the 20 µs input ramp, source and load currents/periods for efficiency, burst case.
- numpy (FFT of the 250 kS/s resampled `V(vout5)-V(c)`, mean removed) + the stated fold rule: in-band 0–20 kHz rms for R2/R3 and the R8 convergence comparison.
- A netlist parser (Python) for R7: element types, ron/l parameter evaluation, control-source drive nodes, and a ban on `time` and on any source other than parts + behavioral control.
- Wrapper the checker owns: 0.5 Ω + 100 nH source with the twelve 10 mV tones, the GNET ground copper, triangular spread clock with jitter, resistive loads, burst injector, ideal sampler at several phases within the 4 µs sample period.

Simulation gaps:
- Ideal binary switch (instantaneous state change at 1.65 V, fixed 100 MΩ off-state) has no body-diode / dead-time / gate-charge loss and no dv/dt coupling; real switch loss and shoot-through are not modeled.
- INDQ is a fixed-Q-30-at-1 MHz series-R model: no saturation, no core loss spectrum, no frequency-dependent winding capacitance. CAPX is a lumped ESR model: no ESL, no dielectric absorption, no DC-bias derating — and real MLCC capacitance loss with bias would move the filter corners.
- No PCB parasitics beyond the fixed 8 mΩ + 6 nH/segment chain; real plane spreading, via arrays, and component-loop inductance are absent, so the delivered noise margin in sim will be optimistic relative to hardware.
- Ideal 250 kS/s sampler with no aperture jitter or ADC reference noise; the real converter's own reference/decoupling noise is out of scope by construction.
- Numerical: FFT leakage with a 2 ms record (500 Hz bins) and a swept 0.9–1.1 MHz switching fundamental is the dominant measurement error; the declared 1 µV allowance is an author assertion to be validated, and R8's base/half-step pair is sensitive to how the checker handles 3 ns edges.

Why frontier models fail:
- The naive move is a tuned trap at 1.000 MHz or a ground tie that cancels at one frequency: it looks far under limit at the nominal clock and one sampling phase, but the ±10 % spread, ±15 %/±10 % part tolerance and held-out clock scales swing the alias into 0–20 kHz. Seeing that requires reasoning about the fold |f − k·250 kHz| over a continuously moving f, not at one frequency.
- Coupled constraints: ripple attenuation (multi-stage LC, DCR/ESR resistance, output impedance) trades directly against R4 efficiency and R7 area/inductance, and against R5 load-step recovery (stiffer filtering = slower loop), while R3 forces the ground-return partition and Kelvin sensing at node c to be right — these cannot be satisfied one requirement at a time.
- The control-law constraints (no `time`, no clock other than `clk`) rule out textbook compensators and force a clk-derived PWM/PFM scheme that must also be light-load efficient for R4 at 10 mA.
This is a hypothesis about model behavior; it is not trial-supported.

Real-world risks:
- Even a design passing every simulated check would face real PCB parasitics, capacitor DC-bias/temperature drift, inductor saturation, and switch/thermal behavior the models omit.
- Spread-spectrum clock generation, jitter and edge-rate in hardware may differ from the wrapper's ideal triangle.
- EMC (radiated/conducted) is entirely outside the check set; a quiet 20 µV rail in sim can still fail system-level EMC.

Milestones (contingency, if measured runtime exceeds one run):
1. Regulation + efficiency + structure (R1, R4, R5, R6, R7) at nominal parts and nominal clock: grader checks band entry, efficiency, area/inductance and structural rules on `abk.cir`.
2. Aliased-noise design (R2, R3) at nominal and worst-case corners: grader runs the sampler/FFT sweep plus burst.
3. Robustness and numerics (R8 + held-out clock scales/phases): grader re-runs the full sweep at base and half timestep.
Each milestone keeps the same device and deliverable file; only the check set is staged.

What to change (reshape): Nothing substantive. Pin down the open details under "Numbers to supply next"; if runtime measurement shows the full sweep cannot be run inside the budget, stage the checks as the three milestones above rather than shrinking the requirements.

tasks.brief:
We are adding a 48 V to 12 V auxiliary supply to a telecom shelf and I need the power-stage values from you. The drive clock drifts with temperature and ageing, and production parasitics will differ from the bench. A supply that loses lock or rings without settling browns out the downstream rail. The fixed stage (source, input capacitor, half-bridge, series resonant tank, transformer, rectifier, output capacitor, load, parasitics) is described in the handbook. Device models are in /app/input_assets/models.lib.

You choose Lr (2 to 100 uH), Cr (10 to 500 nF), Lm (20 to 500 uH), n (1.5 to 4), extra gate resistor per switch Rgate (0 to 20 ohm), a damping resistor Rd in series with the tank (0 to 2 ohm), and an optional snubber across the transformer primary (Rsn 1 to 100 ohm in series with Csn 0 to 2 nF).

Unless stated, every requirement must hold at loads of 2, 3.5 and 5 A, at any drive frequency from 174.6 to 226.6 kHz (the 180 to 220 kHz band plus 3 % drift), with both parasitic capacitances at 0.7x to 1.3x nominal, and from any initial state with output capacitor 0 to 12 V, resonant capacitor -10 to +10 V and inductor currents within +/-2 A. Steady state means switching cycles 151 to 200 after a run starts or after a load step.
1. Mean output voltage between 10.5 and 13.5 V.
2. Efficiency at least 88 % at 3.5 A and at least 86 % at 2 A and 5 A (gate-drive power excluded).
3. Output ripple at most 0.15 V peak to peak.
4. Start-up from zero state at 3.5 A: output within 2 % of its final value within 400 switching cycles.
5. Load step 2 A to 5 A and 5 A to 2 A: output within 2 % of its final value within 150 cycles after each step.
6. No sub-harmonic operation: tank-current component at half the drive frequency at most 2 % of the fundamental.
7. Periodicity: mean output voltage and RMS tank current in the two consecutive 20-cycle windows ending at cycle 180 and 200 differ by at most 1 %.
8. Switching-phase spread: after removing any linear trend, standard deviation of tank-current zero-crossing phase relative to the drive edge over the 50 steady-state cycles at most 1.5 degrees.
9. Convergence from different initial states: mean output voltage within 0.5 % and efficiency within 0.3 points of the zero-state result at the same condition.
10. Numerical robustness: refining the time resolution of the simulation as defined in the handbook changes efficiency by at most 0.3 points and mean output voltage by at most 0.5 %.
11. Peak current in either switch (channel plus body diode) at most 8 A.

Deliver /app/output/design.json with numeric fields Lr_H, Cr_F, Lm_H, n, Rgate_ohm, Rd_ohm, Rsn_ohm, Csn_F (use Csn_F = 0 for no snubber).
tasks.handbook:
FIXED STAGE (all values nominal)
- Source: ideal 48 V in series with 20 mohm, then 20 uF input capacitor with 5 mohm ESR across the half-bridge. Input power is measured at the ideal source terminal, so the 20 mohm counts as loss.
- Half-bridge: two identical switches, subcircuit SWM in models.lib (terminals drain, gate, source). Each contains a 2 ohm gate resistor, Ron about 12 mohm at 10 V gate drive, 400 pF output capacitance, about 20 nC gate charge, and a body diode. Your extra Rgate is in series with each gate outside the subcircuit. Gate drive is an ideal 0/10 V source with 1 ns edges. Each switch is on for half a period minus a 40 ns dead time at each edge (high side on first). Duty is nominally 50 %. Gate-drive power is excluded from efficiency.
- Tank: half-bridge midpoint -> Rd -> Lr -> Cr -> transformer primary. Lr and Lm each carry a series ESR R = 2*pi*200 kHz*L/80 (inductor Q of 80 at 200 kHz). Cr has 5 mohm ESR. The snubber (Rsn in series with Csn) is across the primary.
- Transformer: magnetising inductance Lm across the primary, plus an ideal transformer with primary:secondary ratio n:1 (Vsec = Vpri/n, Isec = n*Ipri), no extra leakage (Lr is all the leakage).
- Parasitic capacitance: 150 pF x scale across the primary and 150 pF x scale across the secondary (rectifier input). Scale is a test condition from 0.7 to 1.3.
- Rectifier: full bridge of four DSCH diodes (models.lib) from the secondary.
- Output: 100 uF with 10 mohm ESR across the rectifier output, then an ideal current sink of 2, 3.5 or 5 A (load steps are instantaneous). The sink stays active for any output voltage above 0 V.
- Drive frequency is fixed per run (open loop); the drive does not track the tank.

DEFINITIONS
- Cycle = one drive period. Efficiency = mean (Vout x Iload) / mean source input power over whole drive cycles in the steady-state window. Final value for settling = mean output voltage over the steady-state window; settling is the last cycle where the cycle-mean output deviates by more than 2 % of final value.
- Ripple = peak to peak of output voltage over the 50 steady-state cycles after removing the cycle-mean trend is not applied; plain peak to peak over the last 10 cycles of the window.
- Tank current = current through Lr. Phase = time of each rising zero crossing of tank current relative to the preceding rising drive edge of the high-side gate, expressed in degrees of the drive period; ringing crossings inside 100 ns after a switching edge are ignored.
- Half-frequency component: DFT amplitude of tank current at f/2 over the 50-cycle window, divided by the amplitude at f.
- Periodicity windows: cycles 161-180 and 181-200.
- Switch peak current: drain-source branch current magnitude including Coss and body diode.
- Convergence comparison: same condition from the random initial states versus the zero-state run (zero-state steady state is also taken at cycles 151-200 for the 200-cycle runs; the start-up run is longer).
- Numerical check: maximum internal step 5 ns, then 2.5 ns, trapezoidal integration, tight relative tolerance, same initial state.

FACTS FOR SIZING
- Fundamental-mode estimates: Z0 = sqrt(Lr/Cr), fr = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(Lr*Cr)), Rac = (8/pi^2) * n^2 * Vout/Iload, loaded Q = Z0/(Rac + Rd + ESR). Rectifier clamping puts the primary near +/-n*(Vout + diode drops) while conducting; the half-bridge gives +/-24 V across the tank after the DC-blocking capacitor.
- Series-resonant stages operated below resonance have discontinuous tank current; above resonance the switch current lags the voltage and switch-node transitions can be soft.
- Voltage gain of a series-resonant stage depends on frequency relative to fr more strongly as loaded Q rises.
- The tank currents of a lightly damped tank take many cycles to decay; the decay time constant is about 2*L_total/R_total.
- Rectifier forward drop at these currents is about 0.3 to 0.5 V per diode, so two diodes in series cost roughly 4 to 7 % of the output at 12 V.
- Efficiency in this class is typically 85 to 93 % depending on damping, gate resistance and operating point. Series damping resistors dissipate Rd x I_rms^2.
- Parasitic capacitance with magnetising and leakage inductance rings at several MHz when current in the rectifier reaches zero; a snubber or gate resistance changes how this ring and the switching-edge timing behave.
- Checker test points: drive frequencies within 174.6 to 226.6 kHz (not disclosed, including values near both ends), loads 2, 3.5, 5 A, parasitic scales 0.7 and 1.3, and several random initial states drawn uniformly from the stated ranges.
tasks.review:
### 06 · 48 V→12 V resonant aux supply across drifting drive clock — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "I need the power-stage values from you... You choose Lr (2 to 100 uH), Cr (10 to 500 nF), Lm (20 to 500 uH), n (1.5 to 4), extra gate resistor... damping resistor Rd... optional snubber"; deliverable is one parameter vector `design.json` for a fixed physical half-bridge series-resonant converter stage.

Forge task: Select Lr, Cr, Lm, n, Rgate, Rd and optional Rsn/Csn for a fixed 48 V→12 V half-bridge series-resonant auxiliary supply so that a transient circuit simulation over drive frequencies 174.6–226.6 kHz, loads 2/3.5/5 A, parasitic scales 0.7–1.3 and random initial states satisfies mean-Vout, efficiency, ripple, start-up and load-step settling, sub-harmonic, periodicity, phase-spread, initial-state-convergence, timestep-robustness and 8 A peak-switch-current limits.

Why it fits:
• It is a parameter decision for a physical device (power stage of a real telecom-shelf supply), not analysis of a fixed design: the eight values are free within ranges and different vectors give different behaviour.
• Every requirement is measurable from a scripted ngspice transient plus Python post-processing: cycle-mean Vout and integrated source/output power (R1, R2, R9), peak-to-peak ripple (R3), settling cycle index (R4, R5), DFT amplitude ratio at f/2 (R6), window-difference of mean Vout and RMS Lr current (R7), detrended standard deviation of rising zero-crossing phase vs the high-side gate edge (R8), cross-run comparison (R9), paired 5 ns / 2.5 ns rerun comparison (R10), drain-source branch peak (R11).
• The device models needed are supplied as text (`models.lib` subckt SWM, DSCH/DBODY), so the netlist is fully constructible headless — checkable in principle, pending harness implementation.
• The difficulty is real engineering, not tedium: gain flatness across a 30% frequency drift versus an 88% efficiency floor at 3.5 A, with damping (Rd, Rgate, snubber) trading stability/settling against loss, plus sub-harmonic, phase-jitter and initial-state sensitivity under parasitic spread.

What stops it:
• Structural: none. The core decision is a design decision and all stated physics is inside a SPICE-class model set (open-source ngspice, listed tool).
• Unresolved feasibility risk (author claim, unverified): the draft states "No reference has been run; all limits are provisional estimates to be calibrated by the task owner" and that the mechanism depends on an existing narrow window between a sharp candidate failing R6–R10 and a damped candidate failing R2. If no parameter vector clears all 11 limits simultaneously, the task has no solution and must be recalibrated (limits retuned — not widened merely to force a pass).
• Unresolved budget risk (arithmetic on the stated plan, not measured runtime): G1 24 runs × ~200 cycles ≈ 1.06 ms sim time each, G2 6 × 420 cycles, G3 and G4 ~16 runs, G5 6 reruns at 2.5 ns — on the order of 14 million timesteps across ~60 long transients before any agent-side design exploration; at an assumed 0.1–1 ms per timestep in a nonlinear MOSFICE netlist this is plausibly tens of minutes to hours of solver time, which threatens the ~2 hour single-run budget for the agent's own iterations. Runtime per run must be measured, not assumed.
• Unresolved specification ambiguity: R3's sentence "after removing the cycle-mean trend is not applied; plain peak to peak over the last 10 cycles" is self-contradictory and must be pinned to one definition; likewise whether G4's random draws are per-condition or shared, and whether R11 applies to the start-up/step transients in G2/G3 only or to all runs.

How to check it:
• ngspice (headless, batch mode): build the handbook netlist (ideal 48 V + 20 mΩ, 20 µF/5 mΩ input cap, two SWM switches with external Rgate, 40 ns dead time, 50% duty, Rd+Lr+Cr+transformer with Lm and ESR terms, 150 pF×scale parasitics at primary and secondary, DSCH full bridge, 100 µF/10 mΩ output, ideal current sink), run 200-cycle (420 for start-up) trapezoidal transients at max step 5 ns.
• Python post-processing of the `.raw`/CSV waveforms: all R1–R11 metrics as defined in the brief, with the drive-edge reference and the 100 ns ringing-crossing rejection for R8.
• Paired runs at 5 ns and 2.5 ns max step on a held-out subset for R10; cross-run comparisons for R9.
• Range validation of `design.json` fields before simulation.

Simulation gaps:
• The models are deliberately simple: level-1 NMOS with constant Coss, no reverse-recovery dynamics for the body diode, ideal transformer with no core loss, no winding AC/proximity loss, no thermal coupling, ideal 0/10 V gate drive with 1 ns edges, ideal current-sink load. Simulated efficiency therefore has an optimistic bias (no core or AC copper loss) and switching-edge/ringing behaviour (R8, R6, R11) will differ on real hardware with a real gate driver and PCB layout.
• Continuum conditions are sampled at 4 undisclosed frequencies and a handful of parasitic/initial-state points; a design can pass the sample and fail inside the band. This is inherent to the stated grader, not fixable by more requirements.
• R10 measures the solver, not the design: a timestep-sensitivity pass says the reported numbers are converged, not that hardware behaves similarly.
• Numerical accuracy of zero-crossing phase at 1.5° (≈ tens of ns at 200 kHz) is close to the 5 ns step scale; detrended phase std must be shown to be insensitive to interpolation method before the limit is meaningful.

Why frontier models fail:
• Hypothesis, unverified. Plausible causes: the parameter space couples gain (Lr, Cr, Lm, n) to damping (Rd, Rgate, Rsn/Csn) so local optima on a coarse nominal grid clear the agent's own gates marginally and fail at held-out frequencies, loads or parasitic scales; the efficiency floor blocks the damping-heavy escape; subharmonic and phase-judge metrics (R6–R8) are emergent behaviours of a lightly damped nonlinear tank that analytic hand-sizing (the handbook's fundamental-mode facts) does not predict; and the agent must spend its run budget wisely on simulation iteration rather than analytic hope. Trials are needed before claiming models actually fail.

Real-world risks:
• Model-to-hardware gap listed above (core loss, AC winding loss, real MOSFET Coss(V) and gate charge, diode leakage, PCB and transformer parasitics beyond the two lumped capacitances) means an in-sim pass may under-deliver efficiency or exhibit different ringing.
• Tolerance/temperature drift of Lr, Cr and the magnetising inductance is not modelled; the 0.7–1.3× parasitic scale covers only two capacitances.
• Component ratings (capacitor ripple current, transformer saturation, MOSFET voltage stress at the ringing frequency) are not among the 11 requirements and are not checked; a passing design could still overstress parts. Peak switch *current* is checked (R11) but peak switch *voltage* is not.

Milestones (if measured runtimes exceed one run):
1. Baseline + calibration: build the checker netlist and reproduce the author's candidate (Lr 3 µH, Cr 330 nF, Lm 150 µH, n 2, Rgate 3 Ω, Rd 0.1 Ω, Rsn 10 Ω/Csn 0.5 nF) at a reduced grid; grader checks that the netlist runs, metrics extract, and measured runtimes are recorded.
2. Window demonstration: run one sharp (low-damping) and one heavily damped candidate across the full grid; grader checks that the sharp one fails R6–R10 (or R1/R5) and the damped one fails R2, establishing that a narrow window exists.
3. Full design task: deliver `design.json` meeting R1–R11 on the undisclosed grid, as originally specified.

What to change (reshape): none at this stage — nothing the idea says needs removing or splitting until runtimes and the passing window are measured. If the calibration shows no passing vector, reshape by retuning the R2 floor / R6–R8 limits against measured candidate behaviour (the author's own stated plan), not by widening limits to manufacture a pass.

Numbers to supply next:
• Requirement calibration (missing specification + verification still needed): a demonstrated passing parameter vector and a demonstrated sharp/damped failure pair, from which the R2 floor (88% at 3.5 A, 86% at 2/5 A) and R6/R7/R8 limits are confirmed — e.g. "candidate Lr=3 µH... passes all of R1–R11 on the 24-run grid; Rd=1.5 Ω variant measures 83.4% at 5 A".
• Requirement: exact R3 definition — e.g. "plain peak-to-peak of Vout over the last 10 cycles of the 151–200 window" (drop the contradictory detrend clause) or "detrended peak-to-peak over 50 cycles".
• Requirement: scope of R11 — e.g. "applies to every run including the 420-cycle start-up and the 200-cycle post-step runs".
• Requirement: R4/R5 settling definition tie-break — e.g. "last cycle whose cycle-mean Vout deviates > 2% of the final value (mean of cycles 401–420 for R4, mean of cycles 351–400 for R5)".
• Interface: checker harness — e.g. `/app/input_assets/topology.cir` template, `/app/output/design.json` schema as stated, plus a metric-output CSV schema (columns: check_id, value, limit, unit, condition_id) and the fixed RNG seed/number of random initial states (e.g. 4 draws, seed 12345).
• Interface: simulation settings — e.g. "ngspice batch, trapezoidal, reltol 1e-4, maxstep 5 ns (2.5 ns for R10), `.ic` from the stated initial-state ranges".
• Verification still needed: measured solver runtime per 200-cycle run at 5 ns and at 2.5 ns on the grader hardware, and total grid runtime, to establish the two-hour agent budget; measured phase-extraction noise (zero-crossing std on a synthetic waveform) to justify the 1.5° limit.
• Handbook data: confirm the model-derived quantities — e.g. DSCH forward drop at 3–5 A (IS=1e-4, RS=0.008), SWM Ron ≈ 12 mΩ and Qg ≈ 20 nC as used in the efficiency accounting, and whether core loss is intentionally excluded from the efficiency definition.

Evidence status: Draft-only input. The `models.lib` text is supplied (establishes the model equations given, not that the asset exists on disk or that the netlist runs). All stated limits, the reference outline, the "distinct_valid_designs" list, the public-design failure claims and the mechanism-survival narrative are author claims; no simulation, reference run or runtime measurement has been supplied or inspected, and the author explicitly states no reference has been run. Efficiency figures, loaded-Q estimates and expected failure modes are unverified engineering estimates. Arithmetic on the grader plan (≈60 long transients, ≈14M timesteps) is my own inference from the stated cycle counts and step limits, not a measured runtime.

Checks before full-task readiness: (1) implement the checker netlist and run the author's candidate once to confirm it executes and metrics extract cleanly; (2) demonstrate a passing design and a sharp/damped failure pair to prove the window exists and to calibrate R2/R6–R8; (3) measure per-run and total solver runtime and set the agent's own simulation budget accordingly; (4) resolve the R3/R11/settling-definition ambiguities in the written requirements; (5) validate that 1.5° zero-crossing phase std is numerically resolvable at 5 ns step; (6) confirm design.json schema and held-out test-point protocol.

tasks.brief:
I need the conditioning block between our resonant sensor (10 kHz class) and a phase-detecting ADC front end. The sensor tone wanders over 9.6 to 10.4 kHz as the sensor warms and ages, and the block's own parts drift too. The block has to give selective gain, limit large signals softly so the ADC is never overdriven, and settle and stay phase-coherent every time the tone starts or steps. I'm leaving the topology to you.

Fixed interfaces: the source is an ideal sine EMF with a 1 kOhm series resistance, amplitude 5 to 400 mVpk, at any frequency in 9.6 to 10.4 kHz. The load is 100 kOhm in parallel with 20 pF to ground. The supply is a single 5 V rail (4.75 to 5.25 V). Active parts are only the supplied op-amp subcircuit OPA (5 MHz gain-bandwidth, rail-to-rail, 0.5 mA quiescent from VCC) and diode model DLIM (Is 1e-14 A, n 1.8, Rs 10 Ohm), both in /app/input_assets/models.lib. Every R, L and C in your block may sit anywhere within +/-3 % of its value, independently or together. Diode Is may vary 0.5x to 2x, diode n 1.7 to 1.9, and op-amp GBW 4 to 6 MHz. All limits below must hold across all of these and across the whole frequency and amplitude range.

Requirements (Vout is the load voltage; gain is Vout amplitude over source EMF amplitude; the tone starts at t = 0 with the circuit at its DC operating point; cycles count at the drive frequency):
1. Small-signal gain at 5 mVpk: at least 38 dB at every frequency in the band.
2. Output amplitude about its mean: at most 1.8 Vpk at every amplitude and frequency, and Vout stays within 0.1 to 4.9 V at all times.
3. Settling: the per-cycle output amplitude at cycle 30 is within 2 % of its final value, for 5, 50 and 400 mVpk tones.
4. Periodicity: between the 10-cycle windows at cycles 40 to 50 and 50 to 60, the amplitude changes by at most 0.1 % and the phase relative to the input by at most 0.2 degrees, for 5, 50 and 400 mVpk.
5. THD at 400 mVpk, over an integer number of cycles in steady state, harmonics 2 to 9: at most 5 %.
6. Orbit return: starting from capacitor and inductor initial states perturbed up to +/-1 V and +/-1 mA, the output amplitude and phase after 80 cycles match the unperturbed start to within 0.5 % and 0.5 degrees, at 5 and 400 mVpk.
7. Amplitude step of +/-20 % (5 to 6 mVpk, 320 to 400 mVpk, 400 to 320 mVpk): output amplitude within 2 % of the new final value 30 cycles after the step, and sub-harmonic content at half the drive frequency at most 0.5 % of the fundamental.
8. Average supply current at 400 mVpk: at most 5 mA.

Deliverable: /app/output/block.cir, a SPICE netlist containing one subcircuit named BLOCK with ports VIN VOUT VCC GND, where VIN is the node after the 1 kOhm source resistance. It may contain only R, L, C, diode (model DLIM) and OPA instances, no sources, no .include and no definitions of OPA or DLIM, and no more than 40 elements. The source, load and supply are applied from outside.
tasks.handbook:
Reference data and conventions.

OP-AMP AND DIODE MODELS. OPA is a behavioural op-amp: transconductance into a single pole, DC gain 1e5, GBW 5 MHz, output clamped about 50 mV inside the rails, 0.5 mA quiescent current drawn from VCC. DLIM is a junction diode with the stated Is, n and Rs and no junction capacitance. Checks may use a different time step, minimum conductance or smoothing form for the exponential, so a design should not depend on numerical detail.

MEASUREMENT DEFINITIONS. Per-cycle amplitude: the magnitude of the fundamental, (2/T) times the integral over one drive cycle of vout(t) exp(-j w t). Phase: the argument of that fundamental minus the argument of the source EMF fundamental. Window amplitude and phase are averages over ten consecutive cycles. Final value: mean per-cycle amplitude over cycles 80 to 90. THD: RMS of harmonics 2 to 9 over the fundamental, from a DFT over an integer number of cycles in the window 60 to 70. Sub-harmonic content: DFT magnitude at half the drive frequency over a 20-cycle window, with the window length a multiple of two cycles. Gain is measured from the source EMF, so the 1 kOhm source and the block's input loading are included. Small-signal gain is taken from steady-state transients at 5 mVpk at 21 or more band points. Corner shifts apply to element values as multipliers between 0.97 and 1.03, per element or all together; extreme combinations such as all R high with all C high are included. Supply within 4.75 to 5.25 V. DC bias of Vout is part of the measured absolute voltage limits.

PRACTICE DATA. For a second-order resonant section of loaded quality factor Q and centre frequency f0, the envelope time constant is Q/(pi f0) and the 3 dB bandwidth is f0/Q. For a 10 kHz section, 1 cycle is 100 us. A residual of x percent after N cycles needs the time constant in cycles to be at most N / ln(100/x). Resonance frequency scales as 1/sqrt(LC) or 1/(RC), so independent +/-3 % shifts of R and C can move f0 by up to about +/-6 %. Peak gain of active resonant sections trades against Q and available op-amp loop gain: usable closed-loop gain of an op-amp stage drops as GBW divided by the noise gain, and the noise gain of high-Q single-op-amp sections rises with Q squared. Low-Q sections are insensitive to detuning but give lower selectivity per stage; cascaded sections multiply gain and combine delays. A silicon diode with n = 1.8 conducts noticeably from about 0.5 V and has dynamic resistance of about n Vt / I (Vt about 25.9 mV at 300 K). Diode conduction changes the effective damping and the resonance of any network it shares with, with amplitude-dependent effect. A limiter followed by a selective stage reduces harmonic content by roughly 1/(Q (h - 1/h)) at harmonic h. Amplitude-dependent soft limiting at 400 mVpk with 38 dB or more of small-signal gain compresses by more than 20x, so the limiter must sit where the following stages do not saturate or lose the gain needed at small signal. Single-supply op-amp stages need a mid-rail bias (about 2.5 V) and AC coupling, whose corner frequencies add phase shift and extra poles at the tone frequency. Large supply-current budgets are not a concern at 5 mA, since each OPA draws 0.5 mA.

EXAMPLES OF DEFINITION. A tone of 5 mVpk at 10 kHz producing 0.5 Vpk at Vout has gain 40 dB. A phase drift of 0.2 degrees at 10 kHz is a timing drift of about 56 ns.
tasks.review:
### 26 · Band-tolerant selective conditioning amp with soft limiting — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "I'm leaving the topology to you" and "Deliverable: /app/output/block.cir, a SPICE netlist containing one subcircuit named BLOCK with ports VIN VOUT VCC GND". The agent chooses the topology and component values of a physical circuit; the brief fixes only interfaces, models and limits.

Forge task: Design a ≤40-element single-supply BLOCK subcircuit (R, L, C, DLIM diodes, OPA instances only) between a 1 kΩ-source 5–400 mVpk tone wandering over 9.6–10.4 kHz and a 100 kΩ ∥ 20 pF load, giving ≥38 dB small-signal gain at 5 mVpk while softly limiting to ≤1.8 Vpk about the mean (Vout inside 0.1–4.9 V at all times), settling to 2% by cycle 30, window-drifting ≤0.1% amplitude and ≤0.2° phase, ≤5% THD at 400 mVpk, returning to the unperturbed orbit within 0.5%/0.5° after ±1 V / ±1 mA state perturbations, meeting ±20% amplitude-step and sub-harmonic limits, and drawing ≤5 mA from VCC — all across ±3% R/L/C corners, diode and GBW spread, and 4.75–5.25 V supply.

Why it fits:
• Physical design decision with a machine-checkable artifact: a SPICE netlist embedded by the checker and measured by transient simulation plus numpy DFT extraction; any topology is accepted.
• Every stated requirement maps to a headless computation: gain (fundamental/EMF), peak and absolute range (waveform scan), settling and window drift (per-cycle DFT over 100 cycles), THD (DFT, integer cycles), orbit return (re-run with .ic perturbations), step response and half-frequency bin, average VCC current.
• The difficulty is real engineering: the gain floor needs peak gain across an effective detuning range of roughly ±10% (band edges ±4% plus component-driven f0 shift up to about ±6%), while R3/R4/R6 force low envelope Q; the limiter must compress more than 20x at 400 mVpk without killing small-signal gain or producing >5% THD or a half-frequency limit cycle. Placing the limiter, staggering sections and filtering harmonics afterwards are coupled decisions.
• Plausible bounded deliverable: one netlist, ≤40 elements, ~5 OPA instances fit the 5 mA budget with margin for a bias divider.

What stops it:
• Structural: none identified; the task is a design task as written and its metrics are all computable in a circuit simulator.
• Unresolved feasibility risks (not structural objections): (a) the reference outline is explicitly "provisional, not yet simulated" — no passing design has been demonstrated, so achievability of R1 + R3/R4 simultaneously under corners is an assumption; (b) the behavioural OPA (single pole, hard min/max clamp at 50 mV from rails, no slew rate, no output impedance or current limit) and DLIM with zero junction capacitance may let designs pass that would misbehave with real parts or with a differently smoothed exponential; (c) the checker's corner strategy (named mixes vs number of random draws) and its tolerance for numerically fragile designs materially change pass rates; (d) total grader sweep (21+ band points × amplitudes × corners × two time steps) may reach hundreds of 100-cycle transient runs; runtime is unmeasured.

How to check it:
• ngspice: transient from DC operating point, 100 cycles at T/400 and T/800 steps, embedding block.cir with the supplied source (EMF + 1 kΩ), load and models.lib; per-cycle fundamental amplitude and phase via numpy DFT; peak/mean/min/max of Vout; THD from DFT over integer cycles in 60–70; sub-harmonic bin over a 20-cycle window; VCC source current averaged over steady-state windows.
• Corner handling: scale each R, L, C by multipliers in [0.97, 1.03] independently and in correlated mixes (all R high with all C high, etc.), plus GBW 4–6 MHz and diode Is 0.5–2x, n 1.7–1.9, supply 4.75/5.25 V.

Simulation gaps:
• OPA is idealised: no slew rate, no output current limit, no input capacitance/bias current, output clamped by a non-smooth min/max — solver behaviour at the clamp and under diode exponential smoothing (gmin variation) can change verdicts; the brief's request for step/smoothing independence is stated but not proven.
• DLIM has no junction capacitance, so THD and settling in a real limiter differ.
• Initial-state perturbations: ngspice .ic specifies node voltages; how ±1 mA inductor-current perturbations are applied is not specified and is simulator-dependent.
• Envelope/measurement definitions are well specified in principle, but window edge effects, DC bias drift during AC-coupled start-up, and amplitude extraction near band edges within 20 Hz are numerical corner cases.

Why frontier models fail:
• Hypothesis, not verified by trials: the constraints are genuinely coupled — per-section Q must be low enough for R3/R4/R6 yet high enough that the staggered cascade keeps ≥38 dB over ±10% effective detuning, under GBW limits (5 MHz op-amp at 10 kHz gives only ~54 dB open-loop, less at 4 MHz corner), while the limiter must hold ≤1.8 Vpk with ≤5% THD after filtering and must not introduce a half-frequency orbit. Nominal-only sweeps can look passing while corner draws and held-out band-edge points fail.

Real-world risks:
• A design validated only against this model set may not survive real op-amp slew, output impedance, supply rejection, noise, diode capacitance, or parasitic coupling; ±3% R/L/C is generous versus 1% parts but the diode spread and AC-coupling corner assumptions dominate.

Milestones (optional, if the single-run sweep proves too heavy): 1. Gain-and-bandwidth milestone: cascade of selective stages meeting R1/R2 at 5 mVpk across corners, checked by frequency-sweep plus short transients. 2. Limiter milestone: add soft limiting to meet R2/R5 at 400 mVpk. 3. Full-dynamics milestone: complete BLOCK meeting R3/R4/R6/R7/R8.

Numbers to supply next:
• Requirement: exact corner sampling — e.g. named corner list (all-low, all-high, R-high/C-high, R-low/C-low) plus N=20 random draws with a stated seed; and the rule for verdicts where coarse and fine time steps disagree.
• Requirement: application of initial-state perturbations — e.g. "inductor currents perturbed by inserting a 1 ns current-source pre-phase, or .ic on designated nodes", with the exact ngspice syntax; specify whether GND-referenced node voltages are perturbed only for capacitor states.
• Requirement: measurement windows — e.g. supply-current average over cycles 60–90; amplitude-step applied at a stated integer cycle (e.g. cycle 20) with the step magnitude carried into the transient source.
• Interface: input files (/app/input_assets/models.lib as given, checker harness) and output schema (block.cir; element-count convention — does an OPA instance count as one element?); max node count and whether .param/.func lines are forbidden alongside behavioural expressions.
• Handbook data: ngspice version and options (gmin value, reltol/abstol, exponential smoothing form), simulation temperature (300 K as stated), and the maximum number of OPA instances implied by the 5 mA budget at 0.5 mA quiescent each (e.g. ≤8 plus a divider ≤2.5 mA).
• Verification still needed (not a widened limit): demonstrate one passing design on the checker; reproduce a stated public-design failure (e.g. single MFB bandpass) to confirm discrimination; measure full-sweep runtime and the T/400 vs T/800 numerical noise floor; confirm the min/max behavioural clamp and diode smoothing variants give the same verdict.

Evidence status: draft-only. The embedded models.lib text establishes supplied model text, not simulator fidelity or asset presence on disk. The reference outline is author-declared "provisional, not yet simulated"; public-design failure claims, stated margins (Q ranges, dB drops, compression factors) and the mechanism-survival narrative are author claims and hypotheses, not verified evidence. No simulations were run and no filesystem inspected for this review. Stated requirement: the eight requirement rows and the netlist contract. Engineering inference: effective detuning up to roughly ±10%, per-stage envelope time constant Q/π cycles (so R3 tolerates Q up to ~24 per slowest stage and R6 up to ~47), and the 5 mA budget implying roughly ≤8 OPA instances.

Checks before full-task readiness: (1) demonstrate a passing design at nominal and at least the four named corner mixes; (2) reproduce at least one claimed-failing public design to confirm the metrics discriminate; (3) fix and document .ic semantics for inductor currents and validate perturbation application; (4) run the coarse/fine time-step pair and the gmin/smoothing variants on one candidate to confirm verdict stability; (5) measure checker runtime and decide the corner-draw count; (6) pin down element counting and forbidden constructs in the netlist grammar.

tasks.brief:
Hi, our system team is adding a pulsed ultrasonic transducer drive stage to the existing 12 V board, and I need the board-side network sized. The drive clock (3.3 V, 50 % duty, 2 ns edges) drifts anywhere in 4.8 to 5.2 MHz. The stage has to come up settled and phase-locked every time, with no retuning.

Fixed parts are in /app/input_assets/fixed_parts.cir: the 12 V harness and source, the half-bridge stage with its stacked low-side pair, and the resonant load tank (which contains the 1.2 ohm load resistor). Nothing in that file may change.

Deliver /app/output/design.json with these fields:
- rail_caps: list of at most 6 objects {c_uF 0.1 to 10, esr_mohm 3 to 300, esl_nH 0.5 to 4}. Each is a capacitor with its series ESR and ESL, from the rail node to ground.
- snubbers: list of at most 2 objects {node one of "rail","sw","tin","mid", r_ohm 0.1 to 100, c_nF 0.1 to 100}. Each is a series R-C branch from that node to ground.
- r_series_ohm (0 to 5): between the stage switch node sw and the tank input tin.
- r_gate_ohm (1 to 100): between the inverted-clock node clkb and the stack gate node gl.
- c_mid_nF (0 to 10): from the stack middle node mid to ground.

Every simulated run lasts 150 clock cycles from the start (or from the step, for R3, which is applied after 150 settled cycles and also run for 150 cycles). Every requirement below must hold at every clock frequency in the band, with rail 11 to 13 V, tank inductance and capacitance each within plus or minus 3 %, every rail capacitor at minus 30 % of its stated value, and for any start state described.

R1. Cold start (all tank and stack states zero, rail capacitors charged to the rail voltage): settling time at most 60 clock cycles.
R2. Perturbed start (tank inductor current and capacitor voltage set to a random state of either polarity holding up to 50 % of the final peak tank stored energy, 0.5*L*Ipk^2 + 0.5*C*Vpk^2 with the final clock-frequency amplitudes Ipk and Vpk): settling time at most 60 clock cycles, and the tank-current waveform over cycles 110 to 130 must match the cold-start waveform over the same cycles, i.e. RMS of the pointwise difference divided by RMS of the cold-start waveform at most 5 %.
R3. Clock step between any two frequencies in the band at least 250 kHz apart, applied after the design has settled: re-settling time at most 70 clock cycles, with no cycle slip, meaning exactly one sw falling 6 V crossing in every clock cycle from 10 cycles after the step to 60 cycles after it.
R4. Periodicity: sqrt(mean over time of (i(t) - i(t+20T))^2) over window 90 to 110 cycles, divided by sqrt(mean over time of i(t)^2) over that same window, at most 1 %. Here i is the tank inductor current and T the clock period.
R5. Phase lock: spread (max minus min, after removing a linear trend) of the sw falling-edge 6 V crossing time relative to the clock edge over cycles 110 to 150, at most 3 degrees of clock period.
R6. Rail ripple: peak-to-peak voltage at the rail node over cycles 110 to 150, at most 150 mV.
R7. Efficiency: mean power in the 1.2 ohm load resistor divided by mean power delivered by the 12 V source terminals, over cycles 110 to 150, at least 42 %.
R8. The file parses, respects the part counts and ranges above, and every simulation completes without non-convergence.

Definitions: the tank-current envelope is the amplitude of its clock-frequency component in each clock cycle. Settling time is the number of cycles after the start (or step) until the envelope stays within 5 % of its final value, where final is the mean over the last 10 simulated cycles (cycles 140 to 150). Cycle 0 begins at the clock start or step.
tasks.handbook:
Handbook: data and conventions

Tank. Series L (4.7 uH, +/-3 %), ESR 0.35 ohm, load resistor 1.2 ohm, series C 215 pF (+/-3 %). The nominal resonance is f0 = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(LC)), about 5.0 MHz. The loaded Q is X/Rtotal with X = 2*pi*f0*L, about 148 ohm. The tank time constant for the current envelope is tau = 2L/Rtotal. Rtotal is the sum of load, ESR, series damping resistance, average on-resistance of the half-bridge, harness and any resistive damping the added network contributes. Envelope decay to 5 % takes about 3 tau, so tau must be short compared with the cycle budget. The same number of cycles lasts less time at the top of the band (60 cycles is 11.5 us at 5.2 MHz and 12.5 us at 4.8 MHz) and the time constant grows with inductance.

Drive. With the supplied half-bridge, the fundamental of the switch-node square wave is about 4/pi times half the rail voltage in amplitude. With the clock 4 % away from resonance, the current is several times lower than at resonance, and a start-up transient at the tank natural frequency beats against the forced response. That transient decays only at tau.

Efficiency. In a series loop every resistance carries the same current, so the share lost in each resistance is roughly its fraction of Rtotal. Added damping reduces efficiency in proportion. Shoot-through current in the stage (high-side and low-side devices on together) and edge losses count as input power. The fixed stage delays the high-side turn-on by an RC delay of about 14 ns but turns it off immediately. A large gate resistance slows turn-off of the stack and can overlap the high-side turn-on.

Body effect. Threshold is Vt = VTO + GAMMA*(sqrt(PHI + Vsb) - sqrt(PHI)). The upper stack device has its source on mid, so its threshold rises, its on-resistance rises and its turn-on delay increases as mid rises. The mid node capacitance and the gate resistance set the timing of the stack edges. The on-resistance of each device is about 1/(KP*(W/L)*(Vgs-Vt)), about 0.09 to 0.12 ohm at a 3.3 V gate.

Rail. The harness is 50 mohm in series with 100 nH. A rail capacitor bank of total C forms a resonance with 100 nH at 1/(2*pi*sqrt(100nH*C)), tens to hundreds of kHz. It is damped by 50 mohm plus the capacitor ESR. Ceramic 10 uF parts at this voltage typically have ESR 3 to 20 mohm and ESL 0.5 to 2 nH. Parallel parts divide both. Ripple is set by the pulsed rail-current charge divided by C, the ESR times the current, and the ESL times di/dt of the edges. Ripple is measured at the rail node, after the harness.

Mapping from design.json to the circuit. The harness output is the rail node, with ground as reference. Each rail cap is a C in series with its ESR and ESL, from rail to ground. A snubber is R in series with C, from the named node to ground. r_series_ohm is a resistor between the stage port sw and the tank port tin. r_gate_ohm is a resistor between the stage port clkb and gl. c_mid_nF is a capacitor from mid to ground. The harness vin parameter is set to the rail voltage under test. The tank kl and kc parameters carry the +/-3 % spread.

Start states. Rail capacitors start at the rail voltage and all other nodes start at zero unless the perturbed start applies. Clock edges are 2 ns. The 6 V crossing is of the sw node falling through 6 V. Phase in degrees is the crossing time divided by the clock period times 360.

Numerics. Trapezoidal and Gear integration with steps of 1/200 and 1/400 of the clock period normally agree for these circuits. Disagreement between them signals a sharp, poorly damped or edge-sensitive design.
tasks.review:
### 06 · Resonant drive board network across a drifting clock band — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "Deliver /app/output/design.json with these fields: rail_caps ... snubbers ... r_series_ohm ... r_gate_ohm ... c_mid_nF" and "The stage has to come up settled and phase-locked every time, with no retuning."

Forge task: Size the board-side network for a pulsed half-bridge resonant ultrasonic drive — at most 6 rail capacitors (C/ESR/ESL), at most 2 RC snubbers, a series damping resistor, a gate resistor and a mid-node bypass — so that the fixed stage and tank settle within 60 cycles from cold and perturbed starts, re-lock without cycle slip after a clock step, meet periodicity and phase-lock limits, keep rail ripple ≤ 150 mV and deliver ≥ 42 % efficiency, at every clock in 4.8–5.2 MHz over rail 11–13 V and L/C ±3 % corners.

Why it fits:
• The deliverable is a set of component values that change real physical behaviour of a built circuit — not an analysis, not a solver, not a report.
• Every requirement is a deterministic output of a transient simulation of a fully specified netlist (fixed_parts.cir + design.json), so a script can check function, drive integrity and power balance with no human in the loop.
• The design tension is real engineering: damping shortens the envelope time constant (R1/R2/R4) but directly eats the Rl/Rtotal efficiency share (R7), and the added knobs (r_gate, c_mid, snubber placement, rail bank) couple stack edge timing to body effect and rail ringing.
• It is self-contained: one input netlist, one JSON output, ngspice as the only tool.

What stops it:
• Structural: none — the task is a bounded parameter-selection problem over a fully specified model.
• Unresolved feasibility risk (not verified): the claimed window of total series resistance ~2.5–2.85 ohm is author arithmetic from the handbook, and the handbook's own reference outline states "Thresholds are provisional until a reference simulation is run." The 1.2/Rtotal efficiency share ignores switching loss into Csw/Cgd, rail ESR/ESL loss, and edge loss, which are counted as input power in R7; at band edges where the handbook says current is "several times lower", fixed switching losses are a larger share of input power and could push R7 below 42 % precisely where the clock is most detuned.
• Unresolved runtime risk: 150 cycles at 5.2 MHz is ~29 us of transient at a forced max step of T/400 (~0.48 ns) — on the order of 6e4 accepted points per run, times ~5 held-out frequencies x both band edges x L/C ±3 % combinations x rail extremes x caps −30 % x two integrators x two step sizes x cold/perturbed starts, plus the R3 step runs. That is plausibly 100+ ngspice runs. Measured per-run wall time is unknown; if a run takes more than ~30–40 s the full self-check matrix will not fit a two-hour loop.
• Unresolved spec risk: R2's perturbed start says "a random state" — the number of seeds, the sampling distribution of the 50 %-energy state, and whether the orbit comparison is time-aligned are not stated.

How to check it:
• ngspice: build the netlist from fixed_parts.cir plus design.json; run 150-cycle transients and extract the per-cycle tank-current envelope (settling, R1/R2), perturbed-vs-cold RMS orbit mismatch (R2), clock-step re-settling and sw falling-6V-crossing counts (R3), the 20T periodicity ratio (R4), detrended sw crossing spread (R5), rail peak-to-peak (R6), and mean power in Rl vs mean source power (R7); repeat with trap and gear integration at T/200 and T/400 and across held-out frequencies and corners.
• Python: schema/part-count/range validation of design.json (R8).
What a simulation would get wrong: Level-1 MOSFET with no gate charge, no package or layout inductance, no temperature; ideal C+ESR+ESL capacitors with no DC-bias derating; behavioral sources that deliver gate-drive power from nowhere, so R7's denominator excludes gate-drive consumption that a real board would pay; the SHS ideal switch; discrete corner sampling is not proof over the continuous 4.8–5.2 MHz band; forced time steps can mask or manufacture edge-sensitive behaviour.

Simulation gaps: see above; additionally the envelope demodulation method (per-cycle DFT, Hilbert, or peak detect) is unspecified and changes settling counts near a 5 % boundary, and numerical noise between T/200 and T/400 must be characterized before a 1 % R4 or 3° R5 limit can be treated as resolvable.

Why frontier models fail: the damping window is narrow and efficiency moves opposite to settling, so a design tuned on nominal corners sits on the edge and fails held-out L +3 % / 5.2 MHz / caps −30 % cases (author hypothesis, not trial-verified); passing requires deliberately giving up efficiency margin for robustness, which an agent optimizing for R7 alone will not do. The start-up beat between the tank natural frequency and the clock only decays at tau, the same time constant the budget constrains; body-effect-dependent stack turn-off interacting with r_gate/c_mid can create edge glitches, cycle slips and rail spikes that only appear across corners; R2 additionally forces a unique converged orbit.

Real-world risks: ceramic capacitance loss under 12 V DC bias not modeled; layout ESL beyond the assumed ~1 nH; level-1 on-resistance and switching loss optimistic/pessimistic vs silicon; thermal rating of the damping resistor and snubbers (0.9 ohm at ~2 A RMS is ~3.5 W of dissipation — real parts and copper area needed); gate-drive power not counted in R7; solder and harness parasitics beyond the fixed 50 mohm/100 nH.

Milestones (if too big): 1. Damping-window selection at nominal corners: a design.json meeting R1/R7 at 5.0 MHz, 12 V — grader checks settling ≤ 60 cycles and efficiency ≥ 42 %. 2. Band-and-corner robustness with gate/mid tuning: same file extended to held-out frequencies and L/C ±3 %, R1–R5. 3. Rail bank sizing: R6/R7 with caps −30 % and rail 11/13 V. Each milestone is standalone only if measured per-run time forces a split; otherwise one run is plausible.

What to change (reshape): none required at Stage 1. If measured runtimes force it, split into the three milestones above; do not relax limits to obtain a passing design.

Evidence status: draft-only. All requirements, handbook values, reference outline, public-design failure claims and the 2.5–2.85 ohm window are stated requirement or author claim; the embedded fixed_parts.cir text establishes supplied text, not physical fidelity; no simulation has been run and no artifact has been inspected. The feasible window, the claimed failure modes of public designs, and two-hour fit are unverified hypotheses. My own arithmetic (tau = 2L/Rtotal = 3.55 us at Rtotal 2.65 ohm vs 60 cycles = 11.5 us at 5.2 MHz; 1.2/2.65 = 45 % nominal load share) supports plausibility only.

Checks before full-task readiness:
• Run one reference design through the full grader matrix and confirm it passes all of R1–R8; record actual margins on R1, R4, R7.
• Reproduce at least one claimed public-design failure (e.g. undamped tank missing settling) to validate the harness and metric extraction.
• Measure per-run ngspice wall time and total corner-matrix time; trim the agent's self-check set to fit ~2 hours.
• Characterize numerical noise between T/200 and T/400 and between trap/gear for a reference design; confirm R4's 1 % and R5's 3° are above the noise floor.
• Verify efficiency decomposition (load vs stack vs harness vs rail network vs switching) at the band edges to confirm R7 is achievable where the clock is most detuned.

Numbers to supply next:
• Requirement: number of random perturbed-start seeds per case and the sampling rule — e.g. 8 seeds, energy drawn uniform in [10 %, 50 %] of final peak stored energy, both polarities, fixed seed list for the grader.
• Requirement: envelope demodulation and settling edge conventions — e.g. per-cycle DFT of i(t) at the clock frequency, settling counted in whole cycles, first cycle whose envelope is within 5 % of the cycle-140–150 mean and stays there.
• Requirement: corner enumeration for the pass rule — e.g. all four combinations of L ±3 % and C ±3 % at each of 5 held-out frequencies, rail 11/12/13 V, rail caps at nominal and −30 %; state whether these are crossed or one-at-a-time.
• Requirement: tolerance of the added network parts — e.g. r_series, r_gate and snubber R/C treated as exact values as written in design.json (no tolerance).
• Requirement: clock convention — e.g. clk starts with a rising edge at t = 0, 50 % duty, 2 ns edges, and the R3 step occurs on a rising edge 150 cycles after the start.
• Interface: input files /app/input_assets/fixed_parts.cir (fixed) and /app/output/design.json (schema exactly as specified: rail_caps[{c_uF,esr_mohm,esl_nH}], snubbers[{node,r_ohm,c_nF}], r_series_ohm, r_gate_ohm, c_mid_nF); the grader-built netlist and per-case metrics JSON (settling cycles, orbit mismatch %, slips, periodicity %, phase spread deg, ripple mV, efficiency %) — e.g. {"case_id": "f5.043_L+3_C-3", "metrics": {...}, "pass": true}.
• Handbook data: capacitor part classes with typical ESR/ESL — e.g. 10 uF X7R 25 V, ESR 3–20 mohm, ESL 0.5–2 nH, as already stated; confirm whether DC-bias derating is applied (currently not).
• Verification still needed (not spec): reference-passing design through the full matrix, baseline-failure reproduction, per-run runtime measurement, integrator/step noise floor.
