I need a custom gate cell for a near-threshold sensor ASIC block. It computes Y = NOT((A AND B AND C) OR D) and drives a 6 fF load. The block runs at low supply with body bias applied to recover speed, and the three-high stack suffers body effect, so the cell has to work across the whole supply, bias and temperature band, not just at nominal.

Fixed conditions: supply 0.55 to 0.80 V; body bias Vb from -0.2 to +0.3 V (positive is forward; the surroundings drive NW = VDD - Vb and PW = VSS + Vb); temperature 0 to 85 C; input 10-90% edge times 80 to 400 ps; load 6 fF from Y to VSS. Devices use the cards in /app/input_assets/model.inc (NMOS nch, PMOS pch). Gate length 60 nm, each width 120 nm to 2 um, at most 14 devices, total width at most 5.0 um, no resistors or capacitors. Body terminals may go to rails, to NW/PW, or to local nodes.

Requirements:
R1: Static, all 16 input vectors held 20 ns, at every supply, bias and temperature point in the band: Y within 5% of VDD of the correct rail.
R2: Every single-input arc that toggles Y, at every supply, bias, temperature and edge time in range: 50%-to-50% delay at most 500 ps at 0.55 V, falling linearly in supply to at most 220 ps at 0.80 V.
R3: Every single-input arc that must not toggle Y, same conditions: Y excursion from its rail at most 20% of VDD.
R4: Back-to-back toggling of the worst arc, 4 ns period, 200 ps edges, 50 cycles, at every supply, bias and temperature point: in every cycle Y is within 5% of VDD of its final rail within 1.0 ns after the input 50% crossing, and each cycle's delay is within 3 ps of cycle 1's.
R5: Every arc that raises Y, 400 ps edges, every supply, bias and temperature point: (E_supply - C*VDD^2)/E_supply is at most 30%, where E_supply is the energy drawn from VDD from the start of the input edge to 3 ns later and C is 6 fF.
R6: Robustness, two separate checks. (a) Refining the time resolution (see handbook), or starting from different initial node voltages, changes any delay by at most 2 ps and any Y level by at most 1% of VDD. (b) With the threshold magnitude of every device independently shifted by up to 15 mV in either direction, R1, R2 and R3 still pass.
R7: Netlist structure: the stated port order, at most 14 devices, L = 60 nm, 120 nm <= W <= 2 um, total width at most 5.0 um.

Deliverables in /app/output/: cell.sp, a SPICE subcircuit named aoi31 with port order A B C D Y VDD VSS NW PW using models nch and pch; and design.json with fields devices (list of name, type, W_m, drain, gate, source, body) and total_width_m.
tasks.handbook:
Model and temperature. model.inc holds 25 C cards. Each temperature point is evaluated with a card at that temperature and no additional simulator temperature rescaling: |vto|(T) = |vto25| - 1.2 mV/K*(T-25); kp(T) = kp25*(T_K/298.15)^-1.5. So 0 C is the slowest corner (|vto| +30 mV) and 85 C the fastest (-72 mV). Threshold shifts in R6(b) are added to vto of each device (to its magnitude for PMOS).

Body effect: |Vth| = |VTO(T)| + GAMMA*(sqrt(PHI + Vsb) - sqrt(PHI)), with Vsb the source-to-body reverse voltage (for PMOS, body-to-source). Stacked upper devices have Vsb > 0 when bodies are tied to a rail, which raises their threshold by roughly 10 to 30 mV. Reverse bias (Vb < 0) raises thresholds of devices whose bodies follow NW/PW by about 25 mV at -0.2 V with these parameters; forward bias lowers them. Junction conduction at +0.3 V is negligible in this model. Tying a body to a rail ignores Vb.

Near threshold (0.55 V against |Vth| of roughly 0.40 to 0.45 V in the cold, reverse-bias corner), current scales roughly with overdrive squared or worse, so 15 mV shifts move drive by tens of percent and delay by comparable amounts. With slow input edges the output cannot start to move until the input passes the turn-on threshold of the active device, which adds a delay of a significant fraction of the edge time. Series devices share the same current, so an effective width of two series devices is about W1*W2/(W1+W2). Internal stack nodes that are discharged and then connected to Y share charge with the 6 fF load and cause Y excursions on non-toggling arcs; stack ordering and device size set their capacitance.

Definitions. Delay: input crossing 50% of VDD to Y crossing 50% of VDD; inputs are linear ramps whose 10-90% time is the stated edge time. Arcs that toggle Y are those where the single changed input changes the function value with the other three held; the others must not toggle Y. Excursion: maximum deviation of Y from its starting rail during a non-toggling arc. Static: all inputs at rails, 20 ns settled. Truth: Y = 0 whenever D = 1 or A = B = C = 1; otherwise Y = 1. The model cards include gate overlap capacitance; gate-oxide capacitance follows from tox. Ranges for typical level-1 cards: GAMMA 0.2 to 0.5 V^0.5, PHI 0.7 to 0.9 V.

Time resolution refinement (R6a) means halving the interval between successive time points in the transient simulation. Initial states are arbitrary node voltages between the rails.
tasks.review:
### 07 · Body-bias-tolerant AOI31 near-threshold cell — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — 'I need a custom gate cell ... It computes Y = NOT((A AND B AND C) OR D) and drives a 6 fF load' plus 'at most 14 devices, total width at most 5.0 um' and deliverables cell.sp / design.json. The agent must choose topology, device widths, stack ordering and body ties; that is a physical design decision, not a simulation study.

Forge task: Design and size a 60 nm, at most 14-device AOI31 standard cell (topology, widths, body ties) delivering Y = NOT((A·B·C) + D) into 6 fF, meeting R1–R7 across VDD 0.55–0.80 V, Vb −0.2 to +0.3 V (NW = VDD − Vb, PW = VSS + Vb), 0–85 °C, input edges 80–400 ps, with robustness to independent ±15 mV per-device threshold shifts, and outputting cell.sp plus design.json.

Why it fits:
• The deliverable is a design artifact (SPICE subcircuit + device table) that a headless simulator can grade end to end; every requirement maps to a scripted DC or transient measurement.
• The engineering difficulty is real and coupled: at 0.55 V with |Vth| ~0.40–0.45 V the three-high stack is body-effect and overdrive limited; tying bodies to rails versus NW/PW versus local nodes trades threshold lowering against glitch and internal-node charge sharing; R7 caps the trivial fix (upsizing).
• R3 (glitch excursion), R5 (short-circuit energy fraction) and R6(b) (margin under shifts) rule out a knife-edge optimum; several distinct topologies can pass, so this is design, not lookup.
• ngspice runs these level-1 cards headlessly: DC operating points (R1), transient arcs with linear ramps (R2/R3), supply-current integration (R5), 50-cycle transient (R4), reruns with halved timestep/initial states and shifted vto (R6), and a Python parse for R7.

What stops it:
• Structural objection: none blocking — the task as written is a design decision and is checkable in principle.
• Unresolved feasibility risk: sweep cost. R2/R3 alone are roughly 32 arc-and-held-state combinations × ~5 edge times × ~30 band points ≈ 4800 transients; R4 adds 200 ns transients per arc per point, R6(a) doubles runs, R6(b) multiplies them by the number of shift patterns. At 0.5–2 s per transient one full pass is plausibly 40 min–3 h, before any design iteration. Measured runtimes are needed; if the budget is exceeded, split rather than widen limits.
• Unresolved feasibility risk: physics oracle. model.inc is author-supplied text; it is uncalibrated for 60 nm devices near threshold, so 'passes the checker' does not imply 'works in silicon' (see simulation gaps).
• Unresolved feasibility risk: tolerances. R2 tolerance is 1 ps measurement resolution and R6(a) allows 2 ps change; the ngspice numerical noise floor for this netlist is unmeasured, so the tolerance may be at or below solver noise.

How to check it:
• ngspice: DC settled operating points for all 16 vectors at grid and interior (VDD, Vb, T) points (R1, Y within 5% of VDD of correct rail).
• ngspice transient, linear-ramp inputs, every single-input arc with the other three held: 50%-to-50% delay versus the linear-in-VDD limit (R2) and maximum Y excursion on non-toggling arcs (R3).
• ngspice transient with supply-current integration from input edge start to +3 ns for every rising-Y arc at 400 ps edges (R5).
• ngspice 50-cycle transient, 4 ns period, 200 ps edges (R4: Y within 5% VDD of rail 1.0 ns after each input 50% crossing, per-cycle delay drift within 3 ps).
• ngspice reruns: halved maximum timestep and alternative initial node voltages (R6a); independent per-device vto offsets up to ±15 mV with R1–R3 rerun (R6b).
• Python parse of cell.sp and design.json: port order aoi31 A B C D Y VDD VSS NW PW, device count, L, W range, total width, file consistency (R7).

Simulation gaps:
• Level-1 cards omit velocity saturation, DIBL, subthreshold conduction, mobility degradation and series resistance; current at 0.55 V/60 nm is therefore an approximation, and the handbook's overdrive-squared scaling is a model property, not measured silicon behaviour.
• Body effect uses a simple sqrt(PHI + Vsb) law; junction conduction at Vb = +0.3 V is asserted negligible in the model (author claim), whereas real forward-biased wells conduct.
• Temperature is a prescribed vto/kp rescale, not a physical temperature model; thermal self-heating and leakage are absent.
• Only model-card overlap and oxide capacitances appear; no routed interconnect R/C, no well tap resistance, no supply network. Glitch and delay would differ in a real layout.
• A finite grid plus undisclosed interior points can miss a failing corner; convergence settings, timestep control and measurement interpolation are not yet specified.

Why frontier models fail: hypothesis, not established. The plausible difficulty is that near-threshold sizing of a three-high stack under a 5.0 µm width cap requires reasoning about body-tie topology, stack ordering, series effective width W1·W2/(W1+W2), internal-node charge sharing and margin against ±15 mV shifts simultaneously; minimum-size AOI, uniform upsizing and knife-edge-optimum AOI each fail one of R2, R7 and R6(b) respectively (author claims, unverified). This needs baseline trials before it can be asserted.

Real-world risks:
• A cell passing the level-1 checker may fail in silicon (short-channel effects, parasitics, well proximity, IR drop); model.inc is uncalibrated text, and no silicon correlation is supplied.
• The 6 fF load, ideal ramp inputs and stylized width budget may not represent the sensor block's real drive and slew environment.
• Forward body bias up to +0.3 V is asserted harmless in this model; real devices would see junction injection and reliability limits.

Milestones (only if measured runtime exceeds one run):
1. Static + delay task: cell.sp meeting R1, R2, R7 on the stated grid; grader runs DC and R2 transients.
2. Glitch + energy + margin task: starting from a supplied baseline cell.sp, meet R3, R5, R6(b) with sizing refinement.
3. Dynamic + numerical task: meet R4 and R6(a) with a supplied cell.sp and harness.

What to change (reshape): nothing structural. Pin down the sweep grid, hidden interior point count, R4 arc definition, R6(a) base timestep and R6(b) pattern count, and solver options before release. If one full verification pass measurably exceeds the run budget, split at the milestones above; do not widen the limits.

Numbers to supply next:
• Requirement (grid, R1–R5): supply points e.g. {0.55, 0.625, 0.70, 0.775, 0.80} V; bias points e.g. {−0.2, −0.1, 0.0, +0.15, +0.3} V; temperature points e.g. {0, 25, 55, 85} °C — plus the number of undisclosed interior points (e.g. 3 random per axis) and the seed policy.
• Requirement (R2/R3): sampled edge times, e.g. {80, 160, 240, 320, 400} ps, and whether intermediates are interpolated or swept.
• Requirement (R4): define 'worst arc' — e.g. all toggling arcs, or the arc with the largest R2 delay at each corner; the stimulus pattern (which input toggles, the values the other three are held at), and that the 50 cycles use the stated 4 ns period and 200 ps edges.
• Requirement (R6a): base transient maximum timestep, e.g. 2 ps, halved to 1 ps; and the initial node voltage set, e.g. all-0 V, all-VDD, plus 5 random seeds in [0, VDD].
• Requirement (R6b): number and distribution of vto shift patterns, e.g. 20 random patterns with each device offset uniform in [−15, +15] mV, and the corner subset rerun (e.g. 6 of the grid points).
• Requirement (R5): confirm the 3 ns integration window and that E_supply is the integral of VDD-source current (as written).
• Interface: inputs /app/input_assets/model.inc; outputs /app/output/cell.sp (subcircuit aoi31, port order A B C D Y VDD VSS NW PW) and /app/output/design.json; state the design.json types/units (W_m float in metres, nodes as strings, total_width_m float, per-device L implied 60 nm) and where the checker harness and hidden points are injected (specification, not yet an inspected asset).
• Handbook data: model card parameters are given (nch vto 0.35 V, pch −0.37 V, gamma 0.25, phi 0.8, kp 400u/200u, tox 2n); add the input driver model for the ramps (e.g. ideal voltage ramp with 10 Ω series resistance), the 6 fF load's connection (Y to VSS, as stated), and ngspice version plus .options (method, reltol, gmin, max step) used for all acceptance runs.
• Verification still needed (not a missing specification): reproduce one claimed baseline failure (minimum-size AOI exceeding 500 ps at 0.55 V, 0 °C, Vb = −0.2 V) with the harness; demonstrate at least one reference cell passing R1–R7; measure per-transient wall time and total sweep cost against the run budget; measure the halved-step delay difference on a fixed netlist to confirm the 2 ps R6(a) tolerance sits above solver noise.

Evidence status: draft only. The model.inc card text, the reference outline (e.g. the 360 ps / 480 ps hand estimates), the public-design failure claims, and the stated margins are author claims in the supplied text; nothing has been simulated or inspected here. Named assets (/app/input_assets/model.inc) are specified dependencies, not verified files. The reference outline is a proposed solution outline, not a passing design. Claimed difficulty of public designs and predicted frontier-model failures are hypotheses pending trials.

Checks before full-task readiness:
1. Build the checker harness and reproduce at least one author-claimed baseline failure (R2 at 0.55 V, 0 °C, Vb = −0.2 V).
2. Demonstrate a passing reference netlist across the full grid plus held-out interior points (the author explicitly marks all thresholds provisional).
3. Measure ngspice runtimes per requirement class and total sweep cost; decide single-run versus milestone split from data.
4. Measure the numerical noise floor (halved-step and initial-state deltas on a fixed netlist) to validate the 2 ps / 1 ps tolerances.
5. Freeze the grid, edge-time set, R4 arc definition, R6 pattern counts and solver options in the task text.

tasks.brief:
We are adding an ultrasonic level sensor node to the product line and I need the drive stage values for its resonant piezo disc. A 3.0 V battery (3.6 V max) pings the disc once per second with a short burst from a full-bridge drive, then the stage sits in standby. The echo level has to be repeatable. The disc may still be ringing slightly when a burst starts, and its resonance and loss drift as it ages.

Transducer (motional branch plus clamped capacitance) and the bridge and leakage data are in /app/input_assets/input.json. Nominal values: Lm 50 mH, Cm 316.63 pF, Rm 209.44 ohm (series resonance 40.0 kHz, Q 60), C0 1.2 nF. Bridge series resistance is 10 ohm in total.

Requirements. Amplitude means the peak motional current in the last 4 drive cycles of the main burst (brake excluded). Ring-down means the peak motional current from 1.6 ms after the last drive edge to 20 ms after it.

R1: cold start, all states zero, 3.0 V, nominal transducer: amplitude 11.4 to 12.6 mA.
R2: same, but starting with residual free ringing of 0 to 3.6 mA at any phase: amplitude 11.4 to 12.6 mA.
R3: ring-down <= 0.3 mA for the R1 and R2 cases.
R4: at 3.0 V with the same residual ringing, for series resonance shifted by -0.4% and +0.4% and Rm scaled by 0.9 and 1.1 (all four combinations): amplitude 9.6 to 14.4 mA.
R5: ring-down <= 0.3 mA for the R4 cases and for the cold start at 3.6 V.
R6: cold start at 3.6 V, nominal transducer: amplitude 8.4 to 15.6 mA.
R7: the last drive edge (burst plus brake) occurs <= 2.0 ms after the wake edge, in every case above.
R8: standby power, drive idle, at 3.6 V and 85 C: <= 6.0 uW.
R9: average battery power over the 1 s frame, cold start, 3.0 V, 25 C: <= 20 uW.
R10: same frame average at 3.6 V, 85 C: <= 30 uW.

Fixed interfaces: full-bridge drive from the rail, no other rails, no energy recovery into the battery, maximum burst end 2.0 ms after wake. The open values are the drive frequency, the burst segments (cycles and pulse width), an optional brake (inverted-phase drive after an optional gap), and the gate-hold resistor, which sets both standby current and turn-on delay. The waveform conventions are in the handbook.

Deliver /app/output/design.json with these fields: f_drive_hz (36000 to 44000); segments (list of up to 6 objects, each with integer cycles 1 to 80 and pulse_width_frac 0.05 to 1.0 in steps of 0.05); brake (object with gap_cycles 0 to 5, cycles 0 to 10, both in steps of 0.5, and pulse_width_frac 0.05 to 1.0 in steps of 0.05); r_hold_ohm (1e5 to 2e7).
tasks.handbook:
Transducer model: motional Rm, Lm and Cm in series, in parallel with C0, all at the bridge output node. The bridge is an ideal source of +Vrail, 0 or -Vrail behind a total series resistance Rsw (10 ohm). Zero means both low-side switches on. States are i_m (motional current), v_cm and v_t (terminal voltage). The equations are L di/dt = v_t - Rm i - v_cm; Cm dv_cm/dt = i; C0 dv_t/dt = (Vs - v_t)/Rsw - i. Typical motional Z0 = sqrt(Lm/Cm) is about 12.6 kohm. The amplitude envelope time constant is 2L/R, about 0.48 ms at nominal. The half-bandwidth is fs/(2Q), about 0.83% of fs. Steady current at resonance for a fundamental drive amplitude Vf is about Vf/(Rm+Rsw).

Drive waveform. Drive cycles are numbered from 0, and each cycle has period T = 1/f_drive. The first half-cycle is positive and the second negative. In each half-cycle the bridge applies +Vrail (first half) or -Vrail (second half) for pulse_width_frac of the half-cycle, centred in that half-cycle, and is otherwise at zero. Segments run back to back, and cycle numbering is continuous across them. The fundamental amplitude is (4/pi)*Vrail*sin(w*pi/2). A brake starts gap_cycles after the last main-burst cycle. It uses the same waveform with the sign inverted (first half negative), so the brake acts as a half-cycle-continuing phase reversal. The last drive edge is the end of the brake, or of the burst if brake cycles is 0. Timing starts at the wake edge (t=0). The first drive edge occurs at td = 0.69*r_hold*Cg after t=0, with Cg = 200 pF. Edges are aligned to a grid of T/400.

Residual-ring initial state: i_m = A cos(phi), v_cm = -A sin(phi)*Z0, v_t = 0, with phi measured against the drive's cycle-0 start. A is 0 to 3.6 mA. The verifier picks phi and A inside the declared range and includes the extremes.

Offsets: a series-resonance shift s scales Cm by 1/(1+s)^2. An Rm scale multiplies Rm only. Lm and C0 are unchanged.

Amplitude window: the last 4 drive cycles of the main burst, taken as the maximum of |i_m| (the brake follows it).

Battery energy: the integral of Vrail*max(0, i_bat) dt, where i_bat = sign(Vs)*(Vs - v_t)/Rsw while Vs is nonzero. Reverse flow is not credited. Add Cg*Vrail^2 per drive pulse as gate energy. Frame average power = (burst energy + gate energy)/1 s + standby power.

Standby power = Vrail*(I_leak(T) + Vrail/r_hold). I_leak is 20 nA at 25 C, 150 nA at 55 C and 900 nA at 85 C (switch devices combined, independent of rail). During the burst, standby power is counted for the full 1 s frame.

Reality checks: piezo discs commonly have Q of 30 to 150 and a series-resonance drift of a few tenths of a percent over life. Free ringing decays as exp(-t/tau), and a residual left at burst start decays at the same rate no matter how the burst is driven. Antiphase drive removes motional current at a rate of about Vf/(2 Lm).
tasks.review:
### 13 · Piezo burst drive and standby stage — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "The open values are the drive frequency, the burst segments (cycles and pulse width), an optional brake ... and the gate-hold resistor, which sets both standby current and turn-on delay."

Forge task: Select f_drive_hz, up to 6 burst segments (cycles, pulse_width_frac), an optional antiphase brake and r_hold_ohm for a battery-powered full-bridge drive of a resonant piezo disc, such that burst amplitude is held in tight windows across cold/warm starts and ±0.4% fs / ±10% Rm corners, ring-down is suppressed below 0.3 mA by 1.6 ms after the last edge, the last edge lands within 2.0 ms of wake, and standby plus frame-average battery power stay under 6/20/30 µW limits.

Why it fits:
• It asks for a design (waveform schedule + a component value), not an analysis: the deliverable is a parameter set in /app/output/design.json that a physical drive stage would use.
• The full physics that matters (three-state linear RLC model, switching-level propagation, gate energy, leakage, battery rectification of current) is stated in the handbook and can be integrated exactly headlessly.
• The hard content is real engineering: a burst long enough to wash out a 3.6 mA arbitrary-phase residual must fit inside a window squeezed between standby-imposed minimum r_hold and the 2.0 ms last-edge deadline, while an antiphase brake must kill ring-down at four parameter corners and at two rails, and energy budgets forbid brute-force long bursts.

What stops it:
• Structural: none. The decision, the model, the acceptance limits and the output schema are all given.
• Unresolved feasibility risks: no passing reference exists yet — the draft's reference_outline is explicitly "provisional estimates ... not confirmed by a passing reference". Whether the stated windows (11.4–12.6 mA at nominal warm start, 0.3 mA ring-down at 1.6 ms, ≤20 µW frame) are jointly satisfiable at the corners is an open engineering question, not a demonstrated fact. The claimed failures of the four public designs are author claims with no supplied simulations.
• Fidelity risk: the task's ground truth is the supplied linear model; real piezo nonlinearity at drive level, temperature coefficient of Cm/Lm, and real MOSFET gate behavior are outside the model.

How to check it:
• Proposed checker (as specified in grader_plan): exact matrix-exponential propagation of the three-state ODE on a T/400 switching grid, from zero state (R1/R6), from verifier-chosen residual states (R2/R4), continuing undriven for ring-down (R3/R5), plus exact schedule arithmetic for R7 (G4) and analytic energy integration for R8–R10 (G5).
• ngspice: transient of the equivalent RLC + switch network cross-checks one case; the draft allows 0.5% slack for this cross-check only.
• Separately, in principle vs. implemented: the tools are suitable in principle; no implementation, no runtime measurement and no cross-check result has been inspected. Residual draws are held out from the solver (24 per corner per G2), which is specified but not yet demonstrated to be sufficient coverage of phase.

Simulation gaps:
• The model is linear and ideal: no piezo nonlinearity or drive-level dependence of Rm/Cm, no switch dead-time or body-diode conduction detail beyond i_bat = sign(Vs)(Vs−v_t)/Rsw, no EMI or supply-impedance effects, no self-heating.
• Numerical: a T/400 grid with T/800 halving and a 1% amplitude-change rule is specified but unproven; peak |i_m| between grid points could be missed, and the acceptable error at the ±20% R4 corners is not quantified beyond the grid rule.
• Ring-down measured from 1.6 ms onward is easy to game relative to real acoustic ringing; the model's exp(−t/τ) with τ ≈ 0.48 ms is an assumption.

Why frontier models fail:
• Hypothesis, not verified: a cold-start-tuned short burst passes a solver's own convergence checks while failing held-out warm-start phases and fs/Rm corners; the amplitude window (±5% nominal, ±20% corners) is narrow relative to residual-phase sensitivity.
• The r_hold trade-off is genuinely coupled: standby forces r_hold ≳ 4.7 MΩ at 3.6 V/85 °C while R7 then consumes ~0.65–0.8 ms of the 2.0 ms budget, so burst + brake must be built and validated inside ~1.2 ms — a packaging-style squeeze across four requirement families.

Real-world risks:
• A design passing the stated model may ring longer in hardware (acoustic loading, coupling to the liquid, housing) or drift further in fs over life than ±0.4%.
• Leaky real drivers at 85 °C and gate leakage may exceed the prescribed leakage table; r_hold temperature coefficients matter.
• Battery internal resistance and rail droop during the burst are not modeled; the rectified i_bat integration assumes a stiff rail.

Milestones (if too big): not needed — the parameter space and simulation cost are plausible within one ~2 h run, subject to a measured full-sweep runtime.

What to change (reshape): • Nothing structural. Keep the same device and the same core decision (drive schedule + r_hold); only pin down remaining conventions (below).

Numbers to supply next:
  • Verification (not spec): reproduce one baseline failure from public_designs (e.g. the fixed 2 ms constant-width burst should trip R7 and the energy limits) and demonstrate one passing schedule, with measured checker runtime and T/400 vs T/800 amplitude deltas — needed before full-task readiness.
  • Requirement: exact residual-draw policy — e.g. "24 draws per corner, seeded PRNG seed 0, always including A = 0 and A = 3.6 mA at phases 0, π/2, π, 3π/2".
  • Requirement: peak measurement convention — e.g. "peak of |i_m| evaluated on the T/400 grid, with a 0.1% relative tolerance on the window edges".
  • Requirement: whether an empty segments list is legal and whether any segment may have zero effective drive — e.g. "at least one segment required".
  • Interface: one example /app/output/design.json instance and one example /app/input_assets/input.json echo — e.g. {"f_drive_hz": 40000, "segments": [{"cycles": 20, "pulse_width_frac": 1.0}, {"cycles": 20, "pulse_width_frac": 0.35}], "brake": {"gap_cycles": 0.0, "cycles": 2.0, "pulse_width_frac": 0.25}, "r_hold_ohm": 5500000} (illustrative only, not a validated design).
  • Handbook data: already supplied (Lm 50 mH, Cm 316.63 pF, Rm 209.44 Ω, C0 1.2 nF, Rsw 10 Ω, Cg 200 pF, leakage table 20/150/900 nA) — confirm these are fixed constants for grading, and confirm the gate-energy term Cg·Vrail² per pulse is independent of r_hold.

tasks.brief:
Hi, I need a loop block for the timing card on our data-acquisition module. It is a charge-pump PLL with a passive loop filter, a 10 MHz reference and a divide-by-64 feedback path. The reference carries a 20 ps phase spur at 250 kHz offset, and the charge pump has mismatch, leakage and a dead zone that spread with temperature. Please size the loop and pick the compensation settings so it meets our datasheet numbers.

Fixed inputs are in /app/input_assets/plant_model.md (the behavioural plant, the loop-gain definition and the metric definitions) and /app/input_assets/input.json (ranges, three corner sets, windows, design bounds). Reference hop of 12 kHz at 400 us, cold start with a 2 MHz output frequency error.

Requirements. Everything must hold at the three corners in input.json and at any other point inside the declared ranges (kv, mismatch, leakage, dead zone):
1. Phase residual RMS <= 5.0 ps in window A (samples 2000-3999, 200 us), where the residual is the phase-error series e[k] (ps, one sample per reference cycle) minus its exact least-squares fit of a constant plus a sine and cosine at 250 kHz and nothing else.
2. The same residual, same limit, in window B (samples 6000-7999) after the hop.
3. Cold-start lock time <= 60 us.
4. Relock time after the hop <= 60 us.
5. Cycle slips (|e| crossing 50 ns) = 0 over the whole run.
6. |mean of e| <= 120 ps in each of windows A and B.
7. Unity-gain loop crossover <= 100 kHz at kv = 125 MHz/V, using the linearised loop gain defined in plant_model.md.
8. Phase margin >= 45 degrees at both kv = 75 MHz/V and 125 MHz/V.
9. Design values within the bounds in input.json: charge-pump current 10-100 uA, R 100 ohm-100 kohm, C1 100 pF-10 nF, C2 1-200 pF, bias current 0-50 nA, overlap 0-120 ps.

Deliverable: /app/output/design.json, a JSON object with numeric fields icp_uA, r_ohm, c1_pF, c2_pF, bias_nA, overlap_ps (SI-prefixed units as named).
tasks.handbook:
Background for the PLL loop block.

Loop practice. A type-II charge-pump loop has a series R-C1 branch (integrator plus zero) and a shunt C2 (ripple pole). Typical practice puts the zero a factor 3-5 below crossover and the C2 pole a factor 3-5 above. Phase margin of 50-60 degrees is common. Crossover scales with Icp*R*Kv at mid-band. With the stated Icp, R and Kv ranges, crossover from a few kHz to a few hundred kHz is reachable.

Charge-pump non-idealities. Up/down current mismatch of a few percent to 10 percent is common. Leakage of the loop-filter node is in the sub-nA to a few nA range and grows with temperature and control voltage. With a dead zone, small phase errors produce no correction. The leakage then acts uncorrected on the integrating capacitor and moves the VCO frequency. The phase error drifts until it leaves the dead zone and a correction pulse fires, so the locked phase can wander slowly. The time scale depends on leakage, dead-zone width, capacitor sizes and Kv, and can be comparable to a 200 us window.

Common countermeasures. Practice distinguishes two ways to keep the detector out of the dead zone. (a) Overlap (reset delay): both charge-pump switches are on for a short time every cycle. This shrinks the effective dead zone, and with mismatch it injects a net current of Icp*mismatch*overlap/T. (b) Static bias current: a deliberately injected DC current into the filter node forces a non-zero static pulse width. In the lock steady state the detector pulse supplies a charge that cancels all DC currents. The static pulse width u_ss is about I_net*T/Icp, where I_net = bias - leakage + Icp*mismatch*overlap/T. Different leakage and mismatch across the range change I_net, so a scheme tuned at one point can leave the detector inside or at the edge of its dead zone at another. The spur modulates the phase error by roughly the spur amplitude, about 20 ps, around the static point. A static error that is too large violates the offset limit.

Metric conventions. Residuals are RMS of the raw sample series after removal of exactly the named components, no others. Any extra basis function (a slope, a quadratic) can absorb slow phase wander and is not part of the definition used here. The 250 kHz tone has an integer number of cycles (50) in the 2000-sample window, so the fit basis is orthogonal to the constant over the window. The phase error e[k] is taken at the detector input, before the dead zone, so it contains the spur itself. Spur rejection by the loop is not scored separately because the fit removes the beat.

Loop-gain conventions. The linearised loop uses the average-current detector gain Icp/T. Mismatch, dead zone and leakage are ignored in the linear analysis. The crossover frequency is the highest frequency at which |L| = 1. Phase margin is 180 degrees plus the phase of L at crossover.

Units. Time in seconds in the plant equations, and ps in reported series. Kv is in Hz per volt at the 640 MHz output. Capacitors in farads, resistors in ohms.

Typical orders of magnitude. With Icp 30 uA, T 100 ns and Kv 100 MHz/V, the detector gain is 300 A/s and the VCO gain in time-error terms is 0.156 per volt. Static pulse widths of tens of ps correspond to currents of a few to tens of nA at Icp tens of uA.
tasks.review:
### 15 · Charge-pump PLL fixed-basis phase residual — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "Please size the loop and pick the compensation settings so it meets our datasheet numbers" / deliverable "design.json ... icp_uA, r_ohm, c1_pF, c2_pF, bias_nA, overlap_ps".

Forge task: Choose charge-pump current, R, C1, C2, bias current and overlap for a type-II charge-pump PLL with passive loop filter (10 MHz reference, N=64, 640 MHz output) so that the simulated fixed-basis phase residual is ≤5.0 ps RMS in windows A and B at three corners and held-out points inside the declared kv/mismatch/leakage/dead-zone ranges, cold-start and relock ≤60 µs, zero cycle slips, |mean e| ≤120 ps, crossover ≤100 kHz at kv=125 MHz/V and phase margin ≥45° at kv=75 and 125 MHz/V, with all six values inside the stated bounds.

Why it fits:
• A bounded configuration decision over six numeric design variables with a fully specified plant (state update, expm discretisation, voltage clipping) — no human judgement needed to score it.
• The whole verification stack is headless and open: numpy/scipy for the 8000-step discrete simulation and least-squares fit, and an analytic Bode computation of L(jω) for R7/R8.
• Difficulty comes from coupled nonlinear physics, not tolerance: the dead-zone nonlinearity plus uncorrected leakage produces a slow sawtooth drift in e[k] on the same 200 µs timescale as the scored window; overlap and bias pull in opposite directions (dz_eff = max(0, dz − ov) vs. the injected mismatch-overlap current and the 120 ps mean-error limit), so a feasible bias window of a few nA at Icp ~30 µA is plausible.
• The exact residual basis (constant + 250 kHz sin/cos only) is a genuine engineering trap: extra detrending terms (slope, quadratic) would absorb the slow wander and make an under-compensated design look passing. The brief states the basis explicitly, so a diligent solver sees the failure; a shortcut solver does not.
• Held-out points inside the ranges are part of the grading plan, so corner-tuned designs that fail at low-leak / negative-mismatch extremes are caught.

What stops it:
• Structural: none identified. The plant is specified equations, so every requirement R1–R9 is computable exactly as written.
• Unresolved feasibility risks (not structural objections): the draft asserts a narrow feasible bias window and that textbook designs fail by a large factor, but no simulation has been run — thresholds (5.0 ps, 120 ps, 60 µs) are the author's, and it is unverified that any design satisfies all of R1–R9 simultaneously. The 50 ns cycle-slip threshold plus the 2 MHz initial error also implies a capture transient whose time-to-lock under the dead zone is not yet demonstrated. Numerical conditioning of the expm update and the LS fit, and runtime of 11+ scenario simuations per candidate design within the ~2 h budget, are unmeasured.
• The provided `input.json` and `plant_model.md` are named specified dependencies; this review has not inspected the filesystem to confirm they exist or match the pasted text.

How to check it:
• numpy/scipy: integrate the per-reference-cycle plant (matrix exponential over T=100 ns, voltage clipping to 0.3–1.5 V) for all 3 corners plus 8 seeded held-out points in kv 75–125 MHz/V, mismatch ±0.10, leak 0.3–5.0 nA, dz 40–220 ps; extract e[k] in ps.
• numpy.linalg.lstsq on the fixed basis [1, sin(2πf_s kT), cos(2πf_s kT)]: residual RMS and mean of e in windows A [2000,4000) and B [6000,8000).
• Same simulation, definitions from plant_model.md: lock time vs. mean(e[3500:4000]), relock time vs. mean(e[7500:8000]), slip count at |e| crossing 50 ns.
• Analytic/computational Bode of L(s) = (Icp/T)(Kv/f0)Z(s)/s with Z(s) as given: crossover on a log grid refined to 0.1%, phase margin at kv=75 and 125 MHz/V.

Simulation gaps:
• The plant is behavioural: no VCO phase noise, no reference jitter beyond the deterministic 20 ps / 250 kHz spur, no charge-pump current noise, no supply/substrate coupling, no quantisation of the reset/overlap timing, no thermal drift within a run. Real silicon residual could exceed 5 ps RMS from noise sources absent here.
• The loop-gain model deliberately ignores mismatch, dead zone and leakage; PM/crossover computed there do not guarantee the nonlinear transient behaves.
• Held-out coverage is 8 seeded points — it samples, but does not prove, the whole 4-D range; worst case may sit between samples.
• Solver convergence of the LS fit and conditioning of expm(M·T) with extreme R·C products are unverified numerics.

Why frontier models fail:
• The metric basis is exactly three terms; a solver that adds a slope or quadratic to 'detrend' absorbs the dead-zone sawtooth and reports passing numbers for a design that fails R1/R2 — an honest-looking shortcut rather than a hidden rule, since the basis is stated.
• The bias current must satisfy conflicting inequalities across the leak/mismatch/dz range: keep |u_ss| above the ~20 ps spur swing at the low-leak, negative-mismatch corner while keeping dz_eff/2 + u_ss within 120 ps at dz=220 ps. Optimising only at the three nominal corners produces a design that fails held-out points.
• Coupled linear/nonlinear design: crossover, zero/pole placement and the dead-zone compensation interact through Icp (which sets both detector gain and the mismatch-overlap current and u_ss scaling), so the variables cannot be tuned independently.
• These are hypotheses consistent with the mechanism described in the draft; no model trials have been run.

Real-world risks:
• A design passing the behavioural checks would plausibly work on a real timing card only if the fabricated charge pump matches the model's dead-zone/leakage/mismatch parameterisation — model-to-hardware mismatch on the dead-zone shape and leakage temperature coefficient is the main gap.
• 5 ps RMS residual at 10 MHz reference is aggressive once reference jitter and VCO noise are included; a built loop could pass the model and still fail the datasheet number.
• The mean-error limit of 120 ps trades static phase offset against robustness; a real device needs guard band, which the bounds may not provide.

Milestones (if too big): not required — the full task plausibly fits one run (11+ scenarios × 8000 steps per candidate, trivially parallelised). If runtime proves excessive, split as: (1) static lock-point analysis (find bias/overlap satisfying u_ss and dz_eff constraints at all corners) graded by an analytic feasibility check; (2) linear filter sizing (R, C1, C2 for crossover/PM) graded by the Bode check; (3) full transient verification of all six values graded by the complete R1–R9 checker.

What to change (reshape): nothing structural.

Evidence status: author draft only. The plant equations, ranges, metric definitions and grader plan are supplied text, not executed artefacts. Claims that textbook designs fail R1/R2 by a large factor, that the feasible bias window is a few nA, and that 30–50 validation runs fit the budget are unverified author claims; no checker, reference design or runtime measurement has been inspected. Named files /app/input_assets/input.json and /app/input_assets/plant_model.md are specified dependencies, not confirmed assets.

Checks before full-task readiness:
• Confirm /app/input_assets/input.json and plant_model.md exist and match the quoted content, and that the checker implementation reproduces the stated metric definitions exactly.
• Produce a reference design that passes R1–R9 at all three corners and a large sweep (e.g. 200+ seeded points) of held-out points; if none exists, reassess the provisional thresholds rather than widening them without justification.
• Reproduce the claimed failures of at least the textbook (no bias, no overlap) and pure-overlap public designs under the exact basis, and demonstrate that adding a linear detrend term changes the residual as predicted.
• Measure wall-clock time of a full 3-corner + 8-held-out evaluation and of the candidate loop a solver would need (e.g. 30–50 evaluations), including float noise in the LS fit and expm update.

Numbers to supply next:
• Requirement: confirm the fixed limits (5.0 ps residual RMS, 120 ps |mean|, 60 µs lock/relock, 0 slips, 100 kHz crossover cap, 45° PM floor) as stated requirements and justify them against the timing-card datasheet — e.g. "phase residual ≤5 ps RMS at 250 kHz spur".
• Requirement: lock/relock band definition (already given as 150 ps about a specified mean window) and whether lock time is measured in µs from k=0 and k=4000 — e.g. "60 µs from t=0".
• Interface: input files /app/input_assets/input.json (as pasted) and /app/input_assets/plant_model.md (as pasted); output /app/output/design.json with schema {"icp_uA": number, "r_ohm": number, "c1_pF": number, "c2_pF": number, "bias_nA": number, "overlap_ps": number}; checker script path and its RNG seed for the 8 held-out points — e.g. seed 12345.
• Handbook data: charge-pump mismatch range ±10%, leakage 0.3–5.0 nA, dead zone 40–220 ps (already declared); additionally, the datasheet figures the 5 ps / 120 ps limits come from and any guard-band policy — e.g. "design target 3.5 ps to allow model error".
• Verification still needed: reference design simulation results, held-out sweep size and pass rate, and measured per-evaluation runtime — e.g. "reference design passes 200/200 random points, 40 s per full evaluation".

tasks.brief:
We are adding a battery-powered load-cell node and need the front end that excites a 350 ohm full bridge and reads it out as one single-ended voltage. The node sleeps most of the time and wakes for short bursts. The readout must therefore settle quickly after each wake, whatever charge its capacitors were left holding. It also has to behave the same for any clock the host happens to provide.

Fixed interfaces. Deliver one subcircuit named readout with ports: vdd gnd clk en xp xn sp sn out. Supply is 3.3 V on vdd. clk is a 3.3 V logic clock at 50 percent duty, at any frequency from 7.76 to 12.36 kHz. en is 3.3 V logic: high is measure, low is sleep. xp and xn are the two bridge excitation terminals your circuit drives. sp and sn are the bridge signal terminals your circuit senses. out is the single-ended output. out drives 1 Mohm in parallel with 100 pF to a 1.65 V reference. The bridge has four 350 ohm arms and 3 mV/V sensitivity. Its signal is Vex x 0.003 x s, where s is the strain fraction from -1 to +1 and Vex is the excitation across the bridge. Bridge, op-amp, switch and inverter models are in /app/input_assets/parts.lib. That file is supplied separately, so do not include it. Every op-amp instance has the same static input offset, anywhere within +/-300 uV.

Requirements. out must equal 1.65 V + 1.2 V x s. FS is the 2.4 V output span. The settling band is 0.05 percent FS, which is 1.2 mV around the output's final value.
R1. Wake from rest: en rises at t=0 with all capacitors at 0 V and s fixed anywhere in range. Out stays inside the settling band from 2.0 ms until the end of the 10 ms burst.
R2. Same limit as R1, but every capacitor starts at any voltage from 0 to 3.3 V.
R3. Strain step: s steps between any two values in range (up to 2 in size) during a burst. Out is inside the settling band within 2.0 ms of the step and overshoots the final value by at most 0.2 percent FS (4.8 mV).
R4. Ripple and periodicity: once settled, out peak-to-peak is at most 0.5 mV. The difference between out and out one clock period earlier is at most 0.15 mV.
R5. Accuracy: settled out is within 1 percent FS (24 mV) of the ideal line for every s in range and every offset in range.
R6. Power: average supply power over a settled measure interval, including the power delivered to the bridge, is at most 12 mW at every s.
R7. Sleep: with en low, the supply current is at most 5 uA and out is within 20 mV of 1.65 V.
R8. Numerical robustness: quartering the simulation step changes the settled mean by at most 0.2 mV and the settling time by at most 0.1 ms.
R9. Construction: use only resistors, capacitors, switches (model SW), oa and inv instances. No inductors, no other subcircuits, no sources. Values come from the E24 series. Total capacitance is at most 10 uF.

Deliverable: /app/output/readout.cir, a SPICE netlist containing only the readout subcircuit definition.
tasks.handbook:
Conventions and reference data.

Bridge. Differential signal sp minus sn equals Vex x 0.003 x s. It is proportional to the voltage across xp-xn, whichever polarity that has. Common mode is half the excitation. Bridge resistance seen by the drive is 350 ohm. Bridge dissipation is Vex^2/350 for a DC or square-wave drive of amplitude Vex, scaled by the fraction of time it is driven. The parts file supplies a bridge subcircuit that takes the strain through a control node ctl, where 1 V means s=+1.

Op-amp model (oa inp inn out vdd). Open-loop gain 1e5, a single pole giving GBW of 5 MHz, output limited to 0.1-3.2 V, 10 ohm output resistance, 150 uA quiescent current drawn from its vdd pin when that pin is above 2 V. When its vdd pin is below 2 V it draws nothing and its output is 0 V. Its input offset is the global parameter vosg, the same for every instance, within +/-300 uV. A real front end also has 8 nV/rtHz white noise and a 100 Hz 1/f corner. The parts file represents that low-frequency error only by the static offset. Noise is not graded.

Switch model SW. Ron 5 ohm, Roff 1e9 ohm, threshold 1.65 V with 0.2 V hysteresis. A switch closes when v(control+) minus v(control-) exceeds the threshold. The control voltage does not depend on the switch's own terminals, so any switch may be driven from clk, en or a node derived from them. Charge injection is ignored.

Inverter (inv a y vdd). Smooth logic inverter, 100 ohm output, y = vdd when a is low and 0 when a is high, with its threshold at vdd/2.

E24 series per decade: 10 11 12 13 15 16 18 20 22 24 27 30 33 36 39 43 47 51 56 62 68 75 82 91. Series and parallel combinations of E24 parts are allowed. Resistor thermal noise is 4kTR, about 1.29 nV/rtHz for 100 ohm at 300 K.

Measurement definitions.
- Final value of out is its mean over the last 2 ms of the interval in which s is constant, with a burst at least 10 ms long. In a burst containing a strain step, the final value is the mean over 18-20 ms.
- Settling time is the last time out is outside the 1.2 mV band around the final value.
- Overshoot is the peak excursion beyond the final value in the direction of the step.
- Ripple is the peak-to-peak value of out over the last 2 ms of the burst.
- Periodicity compares out at t and t+1/fclk over that same interval, where fclk is the actual clock frequency in use.
- Supply power is the mean of v(vdd) x supply current over the stated interval.
- Sleep current is the mean supply current with en low for 5 ms from rest.

Initial states. A charged start sets each capacitor's initial voltage between 0 and 3.3 V, measured from its first to its second listed node. The en rise time is about 1 us. The op-amp internal state starts at rest.

Typical practice. A single-pole filter's 0.05 percent settling takes about 7.6 time constants. A switch network's ripple depends on the clock frequency, so a design that is quiet at one frequency can show more at another inside the declared clock range. Gain from E24 values depends on the combinations used. Held-out points: the clock frequency, strain values, offset values and starting charges are chosen inside the declared ranges, not only at their corners.
tasks.review:
### 24 · Duty-cycled bridge readout front end — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "Deliver one subcircuit named readout with ports: vdd gnd clk en xp xn sp sn out" and "use only resistors, capacitors, switches (model SW), oa and inv instances", i.e. the agent chooses topology and E24 component values for a physical front end.

Forge task: Design a single-ended readout subcircuit (R, C, SW, oa, inv only) that excites a 350 ohm, 3 mV/V load-cell bridge from a 3.3 V rail and produces out = 1.65 V + 1.2 V x s, meeting bounded wake-from-arbitrary-charge settling (2 ms), strain-step settling/overshoot, ripple/periodicity at any 7.76-12.36 kHz clock, 24 mV accuracy over +/-300 uV offset, 12 mW measure power including bridge, and 5 uA sleep — as /app/output/readout.cir.

Why it fits:
- • It is a design decision, not an analysis: the deliverable is a netlist whose topology and values are chosen by the agent.
- • It is checkable without a human: ngspice transients with the supplied parts.lib plus a Python netlist parser cover function, accuracy, settling, ripple, power, sleep and construction rules.
- • The physics that matters (op-amp pole/GBW, output clamps, switch Ron/hysteresis, bridge resistance modulation, supply gating) is inside the supplied behavioral models, so the graded behaviour is the modelled behaviour.
- • The trade-off is real and coupled: 2 ms settling from any 0-3.3 V capacitor charge fights the 0.5 mV ripple limit at the lowest clock and the 4.8 mV overshoot limit, while offset and E24 gain quantisation eat the 24 mV accuracy window.

What stops it:
- • Structural objections: none. The task is a bounded design problem with a specified output file and modelled physics.
- • Unresolved feasibility risks (not blocking, but unverified): the reference outline is an unverified concept, explicitly labelled as such by the author; the claimed failures of the four public designs are hypotheses, not trial results. Whether a design exists that meets R1-R8 simultaneously across held-out clocks, offsets and random capacitor charges has not been demonstrated.
- • Runtime is unmeasured: a settling/ripple/step sweep over several clocks x s values x offsets x ic seeds, each repeated at two timesteps for R8, is on the order of 10^2 transient runs; at even 10-30 s per nonlinear transient this may be 15-90 minutes of grading and comparable iteration cost for the agent. Arithmetic on the stated timebases is fine (22 ms at max step 1/(400 x 10 kHz) is ~88k points), but wall-clock is unknown.
- • Numerical-convergence risk: the SW model uses Roff 1e9 and the oa model has discontinuous clamp expressions; large switch networks can produce timestep stalls or convergence warnings, and R8's 0.2 mV / 0.1 ms tolerances must exceed ngspice solver noise on this bench (unmeasured).

How to check it:
- • Static parser (Python): R9 — allowed element types (R, C, S, X oa/inv), subckt name/port order, E24 value or declared series/parallel combination, summed capacitance <= 10 uF.
- • ngspice transient (G2): wake from rest and from three random ic seeds (uniform 0-3.3 V on every C line), 12 ms run; departure of out from its 8-10 ms mean over 2.0-10 ms <= 1.2 mV + 0.05 mV allowance.
- • ngspice transient (G3): 22 ms run with a strain step at 10 ms; settling <= 2.0 ms to the 1.2 mV band and overshoot <= 4.8 mV.
- • Derived from the G3 waveforms (G4): pk-pk over 18-20 ms <= 0.5 mV and |out(t+T)-out(t)| <= 0.15 mV at T = 1/fclk.
- • Settled-mean comparison (G5): error to 1.65 + 1.2 s <= 24 mV across s and vosg sweep points.
- • Power integration (G6): mean of v(vdd) x supply current over 6-10 ms and 14-20 ms <= 12 mW, with an integrated-energy sanity check against bridge dissipation (Vex^2/350 scaled by drive duty; 3.3 V continuous excitation is ~31 mW, matching the author's figure).
- • Sleep bench (G7): en low 5 ms from rest, mean supply current over last 2 ms <= 5 uA and out within 20 mV of 1.65 V.
- • Step-quartering convergence (G8): max timestep 1/(400 fclk) vs 1/(1600 fclk); mean shift <= 0.2 mV, settling-time shift <= 0.1 ms.

Simulation gaps:
- • Noise is explicitly out of scope (8 nV/rtHz white, 100 Hz 1/f corner reduced to a static offset); a real build's noise and drift are not graded, so real ripple/settling will be worse than simulated.
- • Switch charge injection is ignored, so a real demodulator's pedestal and clock feedthrough are absent — this is the largest fidelity gap for a switched-capacitor/chopper design.
- • The oa model is a single-pole behavioural block with hard clamps and an ideal 1e12 ohm input; no input bias current, no CMRR/PSRR, no output current limit, no supply-dependent behaviour beyond the 2 V gate. Simulated settling under capacitive load or bridge imbalance may be optimistic.
- • Strain is applied as a control node with a 10 us ramp; real transducer dynamics and bridge thermal drift are not represented.
- • Unknown: ngspice convergence/stiffness behaviour for large switch matrices, and whether the R8 tolerance is larger than measured solver noise (needs a numerical-noise measurement on the reference bench).

Why frontier models fail:
- • The binding constraints pull in opposite directions: short time constants to erase arbitrary 0-3.3 V initial charges within 2 ms versus enough filtering/damping for 0.5 mV ripple at 7.76 kHz versus <= 4.8 mV overshoot versus 24 mV accuracy across +/-300 uV offset with E24-only gain parts. Tuning to a rest-start, nominal-clock response is the natural failure mode (author's hypothesis, to be confirmed in trials).
- • E24 gain quantisation plus offset means the accuracy budget must be closed analytically before simulation, not by trial-and-error sweeps.
- • Duty-cycled excitation must keep mean power (bridge + op-amp quiescent, 150 uA each at 3.3 V) under 12 mW while sleeping under 5 uA, i.e. supply gating has to be designed, not added later.
- • These are engineering-trade-off reasons, not hidden rules or pure tedium; the claim that frontier models fail here is a hypothesis until trial runs are done.

Real-world risks:
- • Charge injection, clock feedthrough, PCB parasitics and connector/lead resistance to a 350 ohm bridge are absent from the model and would eat the 0.5 mV ripple and 24 mV accuracy budgets on hardware.
- • 12 mW with a 3.3 V coin cell implies substantial duty cycling of the bridge; real excitation settling and thermoelectric offsets are unmodelled.
- • Common-mode half-excitation drive on sp/sn means the amplifier input range and CMRR (unmodelled) matter in a real build.
- • Noise is ungraded but real; a design that passes in simulation may not resolve fine strain in the field.

tasks.brief:
I need a floating supply for the high-side gate driver of a half-bridge in a motor drive. The only energy source is the 12 V low-side rail: no transformer, no isolated bias. The drive idles, then runs at any duty from 5% to 90% at 100 kHz and steps between duties. Sometimes it holds the high side on for many cycles. The driver rail Vb (VB relative to SW) must be right from a cold start, from a pre-charged state and after every such step. Undervoltage lockout and gate overstress are both unacceptable.

Deliver a netlist of a subcircuit GATE_SUPPLY with pins VIN SW VB GND, using only resistors, capacitors, and the diode and switch models in /app/input_assets/models.cir. One element per line, plain numeric values, no initial conditions on capacitors. Capacitors are listed as ideal; 50 mohm ESR is added in series with each one, and each is 25 V rated.

Fixed externals: the 12 V rail (+/-5%) reaches VIN through 0.5 ohm in series with a 20 nH (+/-20%) loop with 0.3 ohm. SW is forced from 0 to 400 V with 20 ns edges at 100 kHz (+/-3%), duty D 0.05 to 0.90, each period starting low. Capacitors are +/-10%. The driver load sits between VB and SW: 1.0 mA constant plus 20 nC drawn as a 0.2 A, 100 ns pulse at each SW rising edge.

Requirements. Each must hold at every tolerance, rail, frequency and loop-inductance value in the stated ranges, at any duty in range, and with every capacitor starting at 0 V, 6 V or 12 V:
1. Vb reaches 10.0 V within 200 us of the start of the first switching period.
2. After first reaching 10.0 V, Vb stays at or above 9.0 V at all times.
3. After a duty step in either direction between any two duties in range, Vb is back inside 10.0 to 13.0 V within 300 us and stays there.
4. Vb never exceeds 13.5 V.
5. At fixed duty, once settled, the Vb spectrum over 64 cycles has at most 60 mV amplitude at 100 kHz, at most 30 mV at each of the 2nd to 10th harmonics, and at most 10 mV at every other non-DC frequency bin.
6. At fixed duty, once settled, end-of-cycle Vb differs by at most 20 mV between consecutive cycles.
7. If SW is held at 400 V for up to 250 us, Vb stays at or above 9.0 V, and returns to 10.0 to 13.0 V within 5 cycles after SW falls.
8. Current drawn from the 12 V source (before the 0.5 ohm), averaged over 50 ns, never exceeds 0.2 A, including start-up.
9. At most 12 parts in total, at most 2 uF total nominal capacitance, and no capacitor voltage above 25 V.
10. Rerunning any scenario with half the integration step changes the minimum Vb, maximum Vb and settled spectral amplitudes by at most 20 mV.

Output: /app/output/gate_supply.cir, the netlist.
tasks.handbook:
Conventions. Vb = V(VB) - V(SW). Settled means at least 1 ms after the last state change. End-of-cycle Vb is sampled just before each SW rising edge. Spectrum: Vb over 64 consecutive periods, Hann-windowed, single-sided amplitude in volts. Bins are multiples of 100 kHz/64 (scaled with the actual frequency). Duty step: the SW pattern changes duty at a period boundary. High-side-on hold: SW stays at 400 V for the stated time, and the load keeps drawing 1 mA but no pulses occur because there are no rising edges.

Start states: each capacitor is given the same initial voltage across it (0, 6 or 12 V, in the n+ to n- order written in the netlist). Verification uses tolerances at corners and at interior values.

Parts. Diode model: forward drop about 0.7 V at 10 mA, series resistance 0.2 ohm, junction capacitance 5 pF, reverse rating 600 V. Switch model: voltage-controlled, 1 ohm on, 100 Mohm off, threshold 2.5 V with 0.5 V hysteresis. The control pair is two circuit nodes you choose. Capacitor ESR is 50 mohm, added by the checker in series with each capacitor line named C...; tolerance scales the value.

Physics worth knowing. A reservoir of C farads loses Q/C volts per charge draw Q. A 20 nC pulse plus 10 us of 1 mA is about 30 nC per cycle. Resistive limiting of a capacitor charged from 12 V gives time constant R*C. The source cannot supply more than 0.2 A, and an uncontrolled charge of a discharged capacitor through 0.8 ohm would draw about 15 A. The 20 nH loop with capacitors in the uF range resonates near 1 MHz and rings lightly with 0.8 ohm. Each rising SW edge at 20 V/ns injects C*dv/dt through any junction capacitance: 5 pF gives 0.1 A for 20 ns. A diode reverse-recovery effect is not modelled. Sinusoidal-equivalent fundamental of a sawtooth of peak-to-peak dV is about dV/pi. A capacitor's charge state after idle depends on its history, so start-state dependence is real.
tasks.review:
### 17 · Floating high-side gate supply from the 12 V low-side rail — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "Deliver a netlist of a subcircuit GATE_SUPPLY with pins VIN SW VB GND, using only resistors, capacitors, and the diode and switch models in /app/input_assets/models.cir"

Forge task: Design the topology and component values of a transformerless floating gate-driver supply subcircuit (VIN SW VB GND, R/C/D/S only, ≤12 parts, ≤2 uF) that regulates Vb = V(VB)−V(SW) to 10.0–13.0 V with bounded ripple, current draw ≤0.2 A and no UVLO or overstress, from any of the three capacitor start states, at any duty 0.05–0.90 at 100 kHz, across stated tolerances.

Why it fits:
• It asks for a physical design decision (a circuit topology with numeric part values), not an analysis of a fixed system; the deliverable is a netlist the agent must invent.
• The whole design is ≤12 elements, so the artifact is small while the design reasoning is not: start-up speed, current limiting, high-duty hold-off, ripple, and history dependence all bind at once.
• Every requirement is stated as a measurable quantity with a limit (time-to-10 V, min/max Vb, re-entry time, spectral bin amplitudes, end-of-cycle delta, source current, part/cap/voltage budgets, timestep convergence), so a script can grade it without a human.
• The harness conventions (Vb definition, settled definition, end-of-cycle sampling, Hann single-sided spectrum, ESR insertion, same-voltage start states) are given in the handbook.

What stops it:
• Structural: nothing structural blocks it — it is a bounded synthesis problem with a specified device set and a specified bench.
• Unresolved feasibility risk (not a structural objection): the numeric window is asserted, not demonstrated. The author's reference outline (30–50 ohm from VIN into ~0.5–1 uF) appears inconsistent with R8 at a 0 V start: 12 V / (30 + 0.5 + 0.3) ohm ≈ 0.39 A, above the 0.2 A limit, before any diode or switch is considered (my arithmetic on the author's stated numbers, not a simulation result). Pushing the resistor above ~60 ohm keeps start-up current under 0.2 A but makes the 200 us time-to-10 V and the 90%-duty hold harder; a current-limited charge path (as in the second listed design family) may be needed. Whether any topology in the permitted set meets R5/R6 (≤60/30/10 mV bins, ≤20 mV end-of-cycle) together with R1/R8 is unknown.
• Unresolved runtime risk: the grader grid (duty pairs both directions, three start states, tolerance corners plus interior points, rail 11.4/12/12.6 V, f 97/100/103 kHz, L 16/20/24 nH, 64-cycle FFT records, plus full re-runs at half step) is a large sweep; each 1 ms record at ≤5 ns sampling is on the order of 10^5–10^6 timepoints. Per-run and total wall time are not established.

How to check it:
• Netlist parse (Python): element types limited to R/C/D/S with the two named models, no IC=/.ic, ≤12 elements, ≤2 uF nominal, .subckt pin order — checks R9.
• ngspice transient: time-to-first-10 V, min/max Vb, 50 ns-averaged source current, capacitor voltages vs 25 V — checks R1, R2, R4, R8, R9.
gspice transient sweeps over duty steps both directions and the 250 us SW-high hold — checks R3, R7.
• ngspice transient records of ≥64 settled cycles fed to a Hann-windowed numpy FFT (single-sided, window-gain corrected) plus end-of-cycle deltas — checks R5, R6.
• Re-run every scenario with the integration step halved and compare min Vb, max Vb and bin amplitudes — checks R10.
Simulation gaps:
• The bench is the specified model, not hardware: diode reverse recovery is explicitly not modelled; the diode has fixed IS/RS/CJO and no leakage or temperature dependence; the switch is ideal RON/ROFF with a fixed threshold and hysteresis; ESR is a fixed 50 mohm per capacitor; the load is a fixed 1 mA plus a 0.2 A/100 ns pulse.
• The ≤10 mV "other bins" limit sits near the noise floor of a numerical FFT of a switched waveform; aliasing of 20 ns edges and solver ringing can move bin amplitudes, and R10's 20 mV timestep check is the intended guard but does not prove bin-level convergence.
• Real-layout parasitics beyond the stated 20 nH/0.3 ohm loop, gate-drive ground bounce, and diode recovery transients are outside the model; a passing netlist is validated against the model, not against hardware.
Why frontier models fail:
• The design is history-dependent: the same netlist must reach 10 V within 200 us from 0 V, and hold ≥9.0 V after a 250 us SW-high hold, and settle within 300 us after duty steps in both directions — a solution tuned to one natural start state fails the held-out states.
• Several constraints pull in opposite directions (R8 current limit wants a large series impedance; R1 start-up and R7 recovery want a small one; R5/R6 want large capacitance; R9 caps total C at 2 uF), and the duty range 0.05–0.90 plus the 20 nH resonance near 1 MHz add tolerance-corner behaviour that one nominal simulation will not reveal.
• The author's claimed failure mechanism (self-consistency-only verification, caught by R1/R3/R5/R6/R8) is a hypothesis about solver behaviour, not verified evidence; treat it as the design pressure to check, not as a proven property.
Real-world risks:
• Passing the model does not establish hardware behaviour: diode reverse recovery, real driver supply current vs. the 1 mA/20 nC abstraction, and temperature drift of the diode drop are unmodelled and can move Vb by more than the 9.0 V floor.
• The 25 V capacitor budget leaves headroom only under the modelled excitation; 20 V/ns edges plus loop overshoot could exceed it in hardware.
• Components at ±10% capacitance and ±5% rail must be sampled at corners in hardware too; a design that only passes at interior values is fragile.
Milestones (if too big): Not required — one netlist, one grader. If runtime proves too large, split the grader instead of the design task: (1) netlist parse + start-up/current/min-max checks; (2) duty-step and hold checks; (3) settled spectrum and periodicity; (4) halved-step convergence, each with a reduced representative scenario set as a development aid while the full held-out grid remains the acceptance run.
What to change (reshape): • Nothing structural; proceed as written. Keep the device set (R/C/D/S from models.cir) and the single netlist output. Do not widen any limit to make a passing design easier.
Numbers to supply next:
  • Requirement — clarify whether harmonics of 100 kHz above the 10th fall under the ≤10 mV "every other non-DC bin" limit (literal reading says yes; example: 11th harmonic of a 64 mV-pk-pk sawtooth ≈ 1.9 mV).
  • Requirement — R8 filter definition: 50 ns boxcar or moving average of the source current before the 0.5 ohm (example: boxcar, inclusive endpoints).
  • Requirement — the baseline integration step for G5 and its halved value (example: 2 ns → 1 ns), and whether edge-region step limiting is imposed.
  • Verification — the tolerance grid: which corners are mandatory and how many interior random points (example: 2^N corners for C, rail, f, L plus 5 seeded random interior points per scenario).
  • Verification — runtime budget: number of scenarios in the acceptance sweep and measured per-run wall time for one 1 ms record at the stated sampling (needs an actual timing measurement; the reference outline gives none).
  • Verification — reproduce a baseline failure of one public design (e.g. plain bootstrap diode + capacitor) and demonstrate one passing reference run, including a start from 0 V, to show the window is non-empty and the R8 arithmetic tension is resolved (e.g. by a current-limited charge path).
  • Interface — confirm /app/input_assets/models.cir exists on disk with exactly the quoted models (the embedded text establishes supplied text, not asset availability or validity); example output: /app/output/gate_supply.cir containing `.subckt GATE_SUPPLY VIN SW VB GND` with one element per line.
  • Interface — output schema is given; confirm that checker-side added series ESR counts toward the 12-part and 2 uF caps or not (example: excluded, since the checker inserts it).
  • Handbook data — device models (given: DBOOT, SWG); confirm no additional allowed parts (e.g. no dependent sources, no ideal transformers) and the diode polarity convention relative to the netlist node order.

All limits, tolerances and grader methods are stated requirements or author claims; no filesystem inspection, no ngspice execution and no passing design run are in evidence. The reference outline is a proposed solution that the author explicitly marks as unverified, and its 30–50 ohm resistor range appears to conflict with R8 at a 0 V start by simple arithmetic. Claimed public-design failures and the self-consistency failure mechanism are unverified hypotheses.
Checks before full-task readiness: 1) Confirm models.cir exists and matches the quoted content. 2) Reproduce at least one listed public-design failure under the harness. 3) Demonstrate one reference netlist passing at least R1/R2/R4/R8 from a 0 V start and one held-out duty, with measured runtime. 4) Measure per-scenario wall time and total acceptance-sweep time. 5) Resolve the R5 harmonic-bin ambiguity and the R8 filter convention. 6) Check timestep convergence at the proposed base step on one spectrum scenario before fixing the G5 numbers.

tasks.brief:
We need the input protection and bias stage for our battery-backed sensor board. The sense node is a 4.7 nF sensing capacitor plus 10 pF parasitic. It sits floating in standby for months, and clamp and board leakage slowly charge it. The reading has to stay stable over the 30-day calibration interval, and the stage has to survive one input surge at day 0.

Fixed environment: /app/input_assets/board_env.inc. It defines the 3.0 V rail (node vdd), the sense node sn, the input pin in, the temperature node tc, the surge generator, the board leakage, and two clamp parts DIODEA and DIODEB. Temperature is T(t) = 25 + 30 sin(2*pi*t/24 h) + 10 sin(2*pi*t/7 d) degC. Copy that file's contents unchanged into your netlist, including the lines `.param LK=1` and `.param THOLD=-999`. LK scales all leakage, and the stage must work for any LK from 0.5 to 4.

You may add only resistors and at most four clamp instances (DIODEA or DIODEB, any mix). One resistor must connect in to sn, at most 10 kOhm. No other parts and no analysis commands.

Requirements, each at every LK from 0.5 to 4 unless stated:
1. Peak sn voltage during the day-0 surge: <= 4.0 V.
2. sn voltage from day 0.5 to day 30: between 1.2 V and 1.8 V.
3. Residual of sn voltage over days 2 to 30, sampled every 10 min: RMS <= 2.0 mV. The residual is V(t) minus its least-squares fit to exactly two terms, a constant and a term proportional to (T(t) - 25).
4. Current delivered by the 3.0 V rail with the board held at constant temperature (THOLD) and no surge: <= 150 nA at 25 degC and <= 200 nA at 65 degC.
5. DC small-signal resistance seen at sn to ground at 25 degC: >= 40 MOhm.
6. Construction as stated above: fixed file unchanged, allowed parts only, series resistor <= 10 kOhm.
7. design.json values agree with the netlist to within 1 %.

Deliverables under /app/output/:
- stage.cir: SPICE netlist of the stage.
- design.json: {"series_resistor_ohm": number, "resistors": [{"name": string, "node1": string, "node2": string, "ohm": number}], "clamps": [{"instance": string, "model": "DIODEA"|"DIODEB", "anode": string, "cathode": string}]}.
tasks.handbook:
# Handbook

## Leakage physics
- Reverse leakage of a silicon junction at a few volts of reverse bias is roughly constant in voltage, once the bias is well beyond kT/q (about 26 mV). It rises steeply with temperature, typically 1.8 to 2.5 times per 10 degC for generation-dominated leakage.
- The clamp parts in the environment file are behavioural diodes, with Is(T) = Is0 * LK * (T/298.15)^(XTI/N) * exp(EG*(T/298.15 - 1)/(N*k*T/q)), N = 2, XTI = 3, EG = 1.11 eV. The series Rs and junction capacitance are lumped as stated in the file.
- Forward drop of a clamp grows logarithmically with current. It is about N*Vt*ln(I/Is) plus I*Rs. Paralleled devices share the current.
- The board surface leakage in the file is a current into sn that does not depend on temperature or node voltage and grows in time. It is scaled by LK.
- The node settles quasi-statically, because the node capacitance times the bias resistance is well under a few seconds. Net DC current into the node times the DC resistance to the bias point gives the voltage offset.

## Measurement definitions
- Temperature for the metric is T(t) from the formula, evaluated at the sample times t = 2 d, 2 d + 600 s, ..., 30 d.
- Residual: with the samples V_k, solve least squares for a and b in V_k ~ a + b*(T_k - 25). The residual is r_k = V_k - a - b*(T_k - 25). Report sqrt(mean(r_k^2)).
- Supply current is the current delivered by the 3.0 V source Vdd, at a constant board temperature set through THOLD.
- DC small-signal resistance at sn: ratio of a small voltage perturbation to the resulting current, at 1 mHz, at a constant board temperature of 25 degC, with all other sources quiescent. Reverse-biased clamp conductance counts.
- Surge: a 1 ms pulse of 8 V behind 100 Ohm is injected at the in pin at t = 0+, as defined in the file.

## Practice
- Resistors of 1 MOhm to 1 GOhm are commonly available at 1 % tolerance. Use ideal values in the netlist.
- Currents of a few picoamps are comparable to default simulator conductance and tolerance settings. Relax or tighten the simulator accordingly when verifying.
- A 30-day transient can be run with a large maximum timestep (minutes) away from the surge, since the node follows the slow inputs quasi-statically.
- Component names in the netlist are free. Node names sn, vdd, in, tc and 0 are fixed by the environment file.
tasks.review:
### 00 · Standby sense-node protection and bias stage — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "We need the input protection and bias stage for our battery-backed sensor board ... You may add only resistors and at most four clamp instances"; the deliverable is a netlist whose topology and component values are the agent's choice, subject to the stated requirements.

Forge task: Design the added resistor/clamp network for a floating 4.7 nF sense node (surge clamp ≤ 4.0 V peak, node held 1.2-1.8 V over 30 days, two-term-fit RMS residual ≤ 2.0 mV at every LK in [0.5, 4], rail current ≤ 150/200 nA, DC resistance to ground ≥ 40 MOhm), emitted as stage.cir plus design.json, checked by scripted ngspice runs.

Why it fits:
• It is a bounded analog design decision (part selection, topology and resistor values within a fixed part whitelist), not an analysis deliverable; the agent must choose values, not characterise a given circuit.
• Every requirement is a circuit quantity a headless ngspice run can evaluate: transient peak and window (R1, R2), sampled-and-fitted residual (R3), DC supply current (R4), small-signal input resistance (R5), and parseable construction rules (R6, R7).
• The constraints genuinely interact: raising bias resistance eases R4 and R5 but worsens the surface-leakage ramp in R3; clamp leakage must be balanced above and below sn to cancel the exponential temperature term; the surge requirement pushes Rs and clamp selection. That coupling, not hidden rules, is the difficulty.
• Held-out LK points inside the declared range and a fixed two-term basis make the pass/fail surface objective; the grader plan is explicit (append analysis to the submitted netlist).

What stops it:
• Structural: nothing. The idea is a design task with scriptable checks.
• Unresolved feasibility risks (author claims, not verified): the reference outline states the feasible bias window is "about 40 to 53 MOhm" and admits thresholds are provisional until a reference run is done. R5's 40 MOhm floor and R3's 2.0 mV ceiling leave a claimed ~15% margin at the worst corner (LK = 4), against a 2% integrator-difference allowance.
• Unverified: whether ngspice, with behavioural sources at 10-140 pA and 45 MOhm-1 GOhm resistances over a 30-day transient, reproduces the residual to better than the grader's tolerance; default reltol/gmin/vntol can put pA-scale node currents inside the numerical noise floor.
• Unverified: the claimed failures of the listed public designs (1 GOhm bias, single-sided clamp, electrometer buffer) are author assertions; no run is supplied.

How to check it:
• ngspice (transient, DC op, AC 1 mHz): surge peak of v(sn) and day 0.5-30 min/max at LK 0.5/1/4 plus held-out 0.7/2.5; 30-day v(sn) resampled at 600 s for the two-term numpy fit residual; Vdd current at THOLD 25 and 65 for LK 1/4 (+2.5); |V/I| at sn at 1 mHz for LK 0.5/1/4 (+1.8).
• Python parser: board_env.inc text verbatim in stage.cir, only resistors and ≤ 4 X-instances of DIODEA/DIODEB, in-to-sn resistor ≤ 10 kOhm, no analysis commands, design.json values within 1% of the netlist.
Simulation gaps:
• The behavioural clamp (exponential with min() limiting, pow() temperature term) is an idealised junction: no breakdown, no self-heating, no real-part tolerance, no PCB surface-leakage distribution beyond the linear ramp. Matching clamps cancels leakage only as well as the two behavioural instances match — real DIODEA/DIODEB spreads would not cancel this cleanly.
• Numerical accuracy of the 30-day transient at pA currents and minute-scale timesteps is uncharacterised; integrator and gmin choices can move the residual by more than the 2% allowance. This must be measured, not assumed.
• Surge behaviour is dominated by the ideal 8 V/100 Ohm behavioural generator and lumped Rs; real ESD waveforms and clamp tolerances are not modelled.
Why frontier models fail:
• Plausible, subject to trials: the pass/fail hinges on a nonstandard residual definition (exactly two basis terms, constant plus (T-25)); a solver that fits or inspects a linear-in-time term sees a clean proxy while the ramp-driven residual fails R3 at high LK. The feasible bias window is squeezed between R5's floor and R3's ceiling, and clamp leakage must be balanced across temperature, which requires reasoning about cancellation rather than a single worst-case number. All of this is a hypothesis until a model trial is run.
Real-world risks:
• Behavioural diodes and an idealised surface-leakage ramp are stand-ins for real parts; a built board's leakage spread, humidity dependence and part tolerance could blow the ~15% residual margin.
• 1% resistors in the 80-100 MOhm range exist but their voltage coefficient, board contamination and guard layout dominate the real node resistance; the model gives no credit or penalty for layout.
• The 30-day stability claim is inferred from a quasi-static model; no physical calibration-interval data corroborates it.
Milestones (if too big): not required as written; if runtime measurements show the 30-day transient is prohibitive, split into (1) surge + DC + AC checks and (2) long transient + residual fit as standalone tasks with their own graders.
What to change (reshape): none — pin down the items below rather than reshape.
