tasks.brief:
Hi, our system team needs a 3.3 V supply branch for the 10 MHz reference oscillator on a mixed-signal instrument board, fed from the 12 V board rail. The oscillator shares that rail with a pulsed digital load. The oscillator's supply-induced phase error must stay small in every operating state. The topology is yours.

Interface: deliver a subcircuit named pdn with ports feed, osc, dig, gnd. We attach the 12 V rail at feed (already behind 0.2 ohm + 1 uH, with 0.3 V pk-pk ripple at 31.25 kHz). We attach the oscillator load at osc (132 ohm in parallel with 10 nF) and the digital load current pulses (150 mA) at dig. Build it only from the cells REF, LREG, CAP and IND in /app/input_assets/models.lib plus plain resistors. Do not redefine those cells. Capacitors are 10 nF to 100 uF. Stimulus timing and ranges for every state are in /app/input_assets/input.json.

Phase error = 0.8 ps per mV of osc deviation from 3.3 V. The phase residual is the phase error minus a least-squares fit of a sinusoid at the stated beat frequency (free amplitude and phase) plus a constant, over the stated window. Residual RMS and peak-to-peak are measured at node osc.

Requirements, all with the reference offset anywhere in +/-3 mV:
1. State A (cold start, then steady 1 kHz, 20% duty pulses): residual RMS <= 2.0 ps and peak-to-peak <= 8.0 ps over 0.05 to 0.55 s.
2. State B (pulse load steps at 0.1 s from 1 kHz, 20% duty to 7 kHz, 40% duty): residual RMS <= 2.0 ps and peak-to-peak <= 8.0 ps over 0.2 to 0.7 s, beat 7 kHz.
3. State C (12 V feed dips to 9 V for 10 ms at 0.1 s): residual RMS <= 2.0 ps and peak-to-peak <= 8.0 ps over 0.2 to 0.7 s.
4. State D (feed sags linearly by 0.8 to 1.2 V from 0.1 to 0.7 s while the reference drifts down by 300 to 600 ppm over the same interval): residual RMS <= 2.0 ps and peak-to-peak <= 8.0 ps over 0.2 to 0.7 s.
5. State A: V(osc) within 3.3 V +/-1% from 20 ms to the end of the run.
6. State C: V(osc) within 3.3 V +/-2% from 0.1 s to the end of the run, including during the dip.
7. Node dig stays >= 3.0 V from 30 ms onward in every state.
8. At most 12 elements in pdn, counting each resistor, CAP, IND, LREG and REF instance. No sources or other elements, and no other model cells.

Deliverable: /app/output/pdn.cir, a SPICE netlist holding the pdn subcircuit.
tasks.handbook:
# Handbook: oscillator supply branch

## Conventions
- Phase error phi(t) = 800 ps/V x (V(osc) - 3.3 V), sampled at 100 kHz by linear interpolation of the transient output. The sample grid starts at t = 0.
- Residual: over the stated window, solve the least-squares problem phi = a sin(2 pi f_b t) + b cos(2 pi f_b t) + c with f_b fixed by the state. The residual is phi minus that fit. The fit has exactly three coefficients. It has no slope or other terms. Report RMS (zero-mean over the window) and max minus min.
- A linear ramp of total height H over the window has RMS H/sqrt(12) = 0.29 H and peak-to-peak H. At 0.8 ps/mV, 1 mV of ramp is 0.8 ps pk-pk and 0.23 ps RMS.
- A sinusoid of peak-to-peak P has RMS P/(2 sqrt 2) = 0.35 P. A 2.0 ps RMS tone is 5.7 ps pk-pk, which is 7.1 mV pk-pk at osc.
- Harmonics of the pulse repetition rate other than the fundamental are not removed by the fit.

## Library cells (/app/input_assets/models.lib)
- LREG vin vout fb gnd refin: behavioural linear regulator. The error amplifier has DC gain 100 and a pole near 3 kHz. A fixed fraction 0.5 of vin feeds through to the pass node without that pole. Dropout is 0.3 V. Output resistance is 0.3 ohm. It needs a feedback divider from vout to fb, and its output voltage obeys vout = (100 (V(refin) - V(fb)) + 0.5 V(vin)) / (1 + 100 beta) for a divider ratio beta. Line sensitivity and PSRR therefore follow from loop gain, which falls with frequency. It has no current limit.
- REF out gnd: 1.25 V reference behind 10 kohm. It carries a 1 mV peak tone at 4.7 kHz, an initial offset (+/-3 mV) and a slow downward drift in state D.
- CAP a b C=value: capacitor with ESL 1 nH and ESR = 0.015 + 0.1 sqrt(1e-6/C) ohm.
- IND a b L=value: inductor with series DCR = 0.02 sqrt(L/1e-6) ohm. Use 100 nH to 100 uH.
- Plain resistors are ideal, 0.1 ohm to 1 Mohm.
- The feed source, the loads and the stimulus are attached externally. REF reads the globals refofs (V) and refdrift (ppm), which are set per state. Defaults are 0.

## Practice and checking notes
- Closed-loop regulators set the output from the feedback divider ratio. The reference offset and the feedthrough term shift the DC level. Settling bands are measured on the actual simulated node voltage.
- Capacitive loading on a regulator output with finite output resistance adds a pole. Check ringing across the full 10 nF to 100 uF decoupling range with the ESR and ESL given.
- A series resistor in a filter drops I x R at DC. The branch carries 25 mA plus the digital load pulses (150 mA peak) if that load is connected downstream.
- The 31.25 kHz ripple is well inside the 100 kHz sampling Nyquist band. It is not a pulse harmonic, so it remains in the residual.
- Simulate with a maximum timestep of about 2 us or less and ideal-stimulus edges as in input.json.
- Windows are in seconds from the start of the run. All states begin with the feed ramping 0 to 12 V in 5 ms.
- Held-out corners: reference offset in [-3, +3] mV, sag in [0.8, 1.2] V, and drift in [300, 600] ppm.
tasks.review:
### 02-osc-supply-phase-residual-pdn · Regulated 3.3 V oscillator supply branch with bounded phase residual — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "The topology is yours." / "Build it only from the cells REF, LREG, CAP and IND in /app/input_assets/models.lib plus plain resistors." / "deliver a subcircuit named pdn with ports feed, osc, dig, gnd."

Forge task: Design a <=12-element PDN subcircuit (topology free: LREG stages, REF, CAP, IND, resistors) that derives 3.3 V from the 12 V feed and holds supply-induced phase residual at osc under 2.0 ps RMS / 8.0 ps pk-pk in four states (pulse load, load-rate step, feed dip, feed sag + reference drift) with the digital node held >= 3.0 V.

Why it fits:
• A design decision (topology, stage count, filter placement, component values, divider ratios) that a headless script can fully exercise: ngspice transient runs per state per corner, plus netlist parsing for R8.
• The trade-offs are physically coupled and genuinely hard: the LREG's un-poled 0.5·V(vin) feedthrough and ~3 kHz loop pole mean the 31.25 kHz feed ripple (not removed by the fit) drives AC rejection, while the state-D sag drives DC line rejection; added stages and filters consume the 12-element budget and add poles that must not ring into the 10 nF–100 uF load range.
• All limits, windows, fit basis (exactly sin + cos + constant), stimulus and library models are already specified in the payload, so a full task can be written from it.

What stops it:
• Structural objections: none. It is a design task, not analysis or tooling.
• Unresolved feasibility risks (author claims, unverified): the claim that single-stage designs fail R4 by 1.2–1.8x and R1 from 31 kHz feedthrough is stated in the draft but not demonstrated; a two-stage cascade plus reference RC is asserted to fit within 12 elements, which has not been counted or simulated. The mechanism note (a solver's own metric with a slope term masks the sag ramp) is a plausible hazard, not a tested one.
• Whether a passing design exists at every held-out corner is unknown until a reference design is simulated.

How to check it:
• ngspice: transient per state at max step <= 2 us, refofs in {-3, 0, +3} mV plus held-out offsets; read V(osc), V(dig); resample at 100 kHz; phi = 800 ps/V x (V(osc) - 3.3); three-term least-squares fit at the state's beat frequency; residual RMS (zero-mean) and max-minus-min against R1–R4; band checks R5–R6; dig minimum R7.
• A netlist parser: .subckt pdn feed osc dig gnd header, element count <= 12, only R / CAP / IND / LREG / REF instances, no sources or undefined cells (R8).
• Runtime is unmeasured: 0.55–0.7 s at 2 us is 2.75e5–3.5e5 steps per run, ~16–20 runs per design evaluation; small circuit, so plausible but needs measurement.

Simulation gaps:
• LREG is behavioural: B-source with min/max clamp, one pole, fixed 0.3 ohm Rout, no current limit, no thermal, no startup/soft-start dynamics, no PSRR data beyond the stated formula. A real LDO's PSRR, stability and dropout behaviour will differ.
• CAP ESR/ESL and IND DCR are idealised formulas with no tolerance, ageing, DC-bias derating or temperature dependence; no PCB layout parasitics or mutual coupling between the osc and dig branches is modelled.
• The 100 kHz resampled phase metric and linear interpolation are a modelling convention; sub-sample ripple and simulator timestep/noise sensitivity (2x timestep variation is accepted) are not characterised.
• Whether the grader sweeps component tolerances is unspecified; without it, nominal-only passing says little about a buildable board.

Why frontier models fail: hypotheses, not trials. The three-term fit deliberately refuses to absorb a slope, so a design that looks fine under a self-written sloped fit fails R4/R2/R3 tails; simultaneously the 31.25 kHz ripple sits inside the sampled band and is not fitted out, the 7 kHz pulse harmonics are not fitted out, and the element cap plus stability across the decoupling range constrains the obvious fix. Getting DC rejection, AC rejection, ringing margin and 12 elements right at once is a real multi-objective problem.

Real-world risks:
• Passing the behavioural bench does not establish a working board: real LDO loop gain/PSRR, real capacitor ESR/ESL spread and inductance of the layout can dominate the 1 mV-scale budgets being held.
• Reference drift/offset modelling is simplified (linear drift ramp, one tone); a real reference has noise and drift spectra the model omits.
• dig load return path and shared ground impedance are ideal here; on hardware they couple pulse noise into osc.

Milestones: not required on the evidence available — the task plausibly fits one run, subject to a measured per-run simulation time. If runtime or iteration count proves excessive, split as: (1) DC/AC line-rejection architecture sized against R3/R4 at a fixed topology; (2) stability and ripple across the decoupling range (R1/R2) and element-budget-legal netlist.

What to change (reshape): none — advance as written once the numbers below are supplied.

Numbers to supply next:
• Missing specification — tolerance policy: whether the grader sweeps CAP/IND/resistor tolerance or nominal values only; e.g. caps ±20%, inductors ±10%, resistors ±1%, swept at the corners.
• Missing specification — dig load waveform definition: 0 to 150 mA square pulses with 1 us edges, or symmetric ±150 mA; e.g. 0/150 mA, edge 1 us, start 0.02 s.
• Missing specification — simulator and options: ngspice version, .options (reltol, method, maxstep 2 us), and whether a solver's transient may be run longer than sim_end_s; e.g. ngspice 42, trap, maxstep 2e-6.
• Missing specification — netlist legality details: whether .param/.include lines are permitted in pdn.cir and whether the element count includes anything outside the .subckt body; e.g. .include forbidden, count instances inside .subckt only.
• Interface — checker bench asset: the wrapping bench netlist (source, 0.2 ohm + 1 uH feed, ripple, loads, state stimulus) as a concrete file, e.g. /app/input_assets/bench_<state>.cir; plus confirmation that models.lib and input.json exist and match the embedded text.
• Output schema — confirm: single file /app/output/pdn.cir containing exactly one .subckt pdn feed osc dig gnd with no internal .subckt definitions; output metrics reported where, if anywhere (e.g. a metrics.json, or checker-only).
• Verification still needed (not spec gaps) — reproduce the claimed single-stage failure at R4/R1 to confirm the difficulty premise; produce one passing reference design across G2–G5 including held-out points; measure per-run runtime and convergence with the B-source clamps at 2 us step; confirm the metric implementation matches the handbook exactly (three terms, zero-mean RMS, pk-pk = max - min).
• Handbook data already present (no action): ESR = 0.015 + 0.1·sqrt(1e-6/C) ohm, ESL 1 nH, DCR = 0.02·sqrt(L/1e-6) ohm, LREG gain 100 / pole ~3 kHz / dropout 0.3 V / Rout 0.3 ohm, 0.8 ps per mV; restate component ranges: caps 10 nF–100 uF, inductors 100 nH–100 uH, resistors 0.1 ohm–1 Mohm.

Evidence status: draft-only payload. The library models and input.json establish supplied text only; I have not inspected /app/input_assets or run any simulation. The reference outline, distinct-design list, public-design failure claims (e.g. 'single LDO fails R4 by 1.2–1.8x'), stated margins and the mechanism_survival claim are unverified author claims. My ripple/feedthrough and drift arithmetic above is engineering inference from the supplied model text, not measured. No design is validated; 'advance' means worth developing.

Checks before full-task readiness: 1) simulate the named public designs to reproduce their claimed R1/R4 failures; 2) build and simulate one candidate reference netlist across all G2–G5 corners plus held-out points to show a passing design exists within 12 elements; 3) implement and cross-check the residual metric independently (three-term fit only) against the handbook; 4) measure transient runtime and timestep sensitivity (1 us vs 2 us) and confirm convergence with the LREG clamps; 5) decide and record the component-tolerance policy before freezing limits.

tasks.brief:
I need a one-bit retention storage cell for an always-on sensor hub. In standby the cell sits on a slowly modulated supply, and our power firmware infers cell health from the supply-current trace. The trace must be a constant level plus a supply-synchronous ripple and must not creep as the devices age, and the bit must survive standby and read correctly on wake. I need a transistor-level cell.

Fixed interface: subcircuit RETCELL with ports VDD VSS BN BP D WE Q, in that order. Every NMOS bulk goes to BN and every PMOS bulk to BP. D is data in, WE is write enable (active high), Q is the read output, loaded with 10 fF to VSS. Use only the models in /app/input_assets/models.lib (nmos_g, pmos_g, nmos_hv, pmos_hv), referenced by name, and do not include the library in your file. Allowed elements: at most 14 MOSFETs (L >= 60 nm, 120 nm <= W <= 2 um) and at most 2 ideal resistors (100 Mohm to 20 Gohm). No sources, capacitors, diodes or behavioural elements. Temperature is 27 C. Logic levels for D and WE are 0 and 1.0 V.

Operating conditions: Active supply is 1.0 V. Standby supply is V(VDD) = 0.60 V + 0.100 V * sin(2*pi*t/100 us + phi), with phi anywhere in 0 to 2*pi, so 200 mV peak to peak. The window is 2000 modulation periods (200 ms) and starts after the supply has sat at 0.60 V for 5 ms. Ageing over the window is a linear ramp of forward body bias on BN (relative to VSS) and on BP (below VDD), from 0 up to a final value between 0.05 and 0.07 V; I will also check with no ramp. The wake-up is a linear supply ramp from the standby level to 1.0 V in 200 ns.

Requirements (D and WE held low in standby; each holds for a stored 0 and a stored 1):
R1. Write: with WE high for 10 ns at 1.0 V, Q is within 0.1 V of the written level 20 ns after WE rises.
R2. Residual: fit the raw VDD supply current (positive into VDD) over the full window with exactly a constant plus one sinusoid at the modulation frequency (amplitude and phase free, no other terms). RMS residual divided by the constant is <= 0.05, with and without ageing.
R3. The fitted constant is between 40 pA and 150 pA.
R4. Fitted sinusoid amplitude divided by the constant is between 0.05 and 0.50.
R5. Retention: at the lowest-supply instant in the last modulation period, Q is >= 0.7*V(VDD) for a 1 and <= 0.3*V(VDD) for a 0.
R6. Wake read: 20 ns after the wake ramp ends, Q is >= 0.9 V for a 1 and <= 0.1 V for a 0.
R7. Peak current into VDD during the wake ramp and the 50 ns after it is <= 150 uA.
R8. Netlist obeys the element, size, bulk and port rules above.

Deliver /app/output/cell.sp: a SPICE netlist containing the RETCELL subcircuit and nothing else.
tasks.handbook:
Model library: /app/input_assets/models.lib holds four BSIM3v3-type cards (nominal Vth about 0.32 V NMOS and -0.34 V PMOS for the _g models; about 0.42 V and -0.44 V for the _hv models). Subthreshold swing is about 75-85 mV/decade at 27 C. DIBL: Vth falls roughly 5-8 mV per 100 mV of drain-source voltage at minimum length. Gate and junction tunnelling leakage are not modelled, so all leakage is subthreshold channel leakage.

Ageing emulation: forward body bias lowers Vth through the body effect. For these cards a body-bias ramp of 0.05-0.07 V gives a Vth reduction of about 13-20 mV on each device type. Subthreshold current rises by exp(dVth/(n*kT/q)), with n*kT/q about 33-37 mV, so an unprotected leaking device gains roughly 1.4-1.8x over the window. Stacking devices does not remove this relative sensitivity; the stack node voltages move with the shift. Series stacks lower mean leakage per device but gain sensitivity.

Metric definition. Let i(t) be the current delivered by the VDD source into the VDD port, sampled uniformly at 20 us or finer over the 200 ms window. Least-squares fit i(t) = c + a*sin(w*t) + b*cos(w*t), with w = 2*pi/100 us. A = sqrt(a^2+b^2) is the fitted amplitude. Residual r(t) = i(t) - fit; RMS = sqrt(mean(r^2)). Reported ratios are RMS/c and A/c. For scale: a pure linear drift covering a fractional change D of the mean over the window gives an RMS residual near 0.29*D times the mean, because the ripple basis hardly removes it. Harmonics of the modulation frequency and any slow relaxation of internal nodes also count as residual.

Supply-current content: besides leakage, i(t) contains displacement current C*dV/dt from the modulated supply charging the cell's capacitances. It is sinusoidal at the modulation frequency and quadrature-phased; for 1-5 fF of node capacitance at this frequency it is roughly 6-30 pA of amplitude. Floating nodes with pA-level currents have settling times of tens to hundreds of microseconds (C*dV/I), comparable to the modulation period.

Ideal resistors: a resistor between VDD and VSS carries 0.6 V/R at the mean level and is linear in supply and independent of ageing, giving 60 pA at 10 Gohm. Resistor values are free within the stated range.

Retention: a cross-coupled inverter pair needs loop gain above 1, which at 0.5 V supply with high-Vth devices is marginal for small devices. Bit flips under supply dips are a real risk for weakly driven storage nodes at 0.5 V. Asymmetry between the two storage nodes' leakage changes the retained state's leakage by a factor of a few.

Write: logic levels on D and WE are 0 and 1.0 V; the write pulse is 10 ns; the 10 fF load on Q applies in all states. Wake: the ramp starts at the standby supply value at the end of the window. Simulation practice: leakage-level simulations need tight absolute current tolerances (sub-fA) and minimum conductance tied down, and long windows need a limited maximum step. Provisional note: the numeric limits are estimates to be calibrated against a passing reference.

### 07 · Drift-free standby retention cell — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "I need a transistor-level cell" / "Deliver /app/output/cell.sp: a SPICE netlist containing the RETCELL subcircuit and nothing else."

Forge task: Design a <=14-MOSFET (+<=2 ideal Gohm resistors) one-bit retention cell as a SPICE subcircuit RETCELL VDD VSS BN BP D WE Q, using only nmos_g/pmos_g/nmos_hv/pmos_hv, that writes at 1.0 V, holds both bits through a 200 ms supply-modulated (0.60 V + 0.100 V sin, 10 kHz) standby window with a 0-0.07 V body-bias ageing ramp, reads back after a 200 ns wake ramp, and whose raw VDD current over the window fits constant + one sinusoid at the modulation frequency within RMS/c <= 0.05, c in 40-150 pA, A/c in 0.05-0.50, wake peak <= 150 uA.

Why it fits:
• It is a physical design decision (transistor sizing and topology) whose every stated requirement is checked by scripted transient simulation: write/read levels (R1, R6), spectral fit of the supply trace (R2-R4), retention margin at the lowest supply instant (R5), wake inrush (R7) and netlist rules (R8).
• The difficulty is real engineering, not hidden rules: sub-pA leakage budgeting against ageing-driven Vth shift, resistive-bleed dominance versus ripple band, loop gain of a cross-coupled pair at 0.5 V, and displacement current from a nonlinear-C node — a multi-constraint analog trade-off frontier models typically get wrong.
• Bounded output: one netlist file; topology freedom is preserved (grader accepts any compliant topology).

What stops it:
• Structural: none — no analysis-only or out-of-scope-tool element.
• Unresolved feasibility risks (not structural objections): (a) no passing reference exists yet — the reference_outline is a proposed solution, not a passing design, and the limits are explicitly "provisional to be calibrated"; (b) runtime of a 200 ms transient at sub-fA abstol with a bounded max step is unmeasured — if one run takes >10 min, the iterative design loop inside ~2 h is at risk; (c) the 0.05 RMS/c band against a 1.4-1.8x drift is only plausibly reachable via resistor-dominated offset, which then pressures R3/R4 — the working window is asserted narrow but never demonstrated.

• ngspice (headless, BSIM3v3 level=8 from /app/input_assets/models.lib): transient of write, 5 ms settle, 200 ms modulated standby with body-bias ramp, 200 ns wake ramp; samples i(VDD) and Q at the stated instants.
• Python/numpy: least-squares fit of i(t) to constant + a*sin + b*cos at the modulation frequency over the full window; RMS/c, c, A/c; peak wake current — matching the grader plan (G1-G5), which is a plan, not implemented evidence.
• Static parse (Python): R8 element counts, model names, L/W ranges, bulk nodes, port order, forbidden elements.
• What a simulation would get wrong: BSIM3v3 here omits gate/junction tunnelling and all mismatch/variation, so the absolute pA floor and its bit-to-bit asymmetry are optimistic versus silicon; the fit's numerical noise floor (must sit well below 0.05*c, i.e. a few pA RMS) is uncharacterised; angular discretisation and max-step choice can alias harmonics into or out of the residual.

• Numerical: need abstol/gmin/max-step settings that reproduce a sub-pA noise floor below ~1 pA RMS on a known-current test case; current tolerances in the plan ("1%") are tight relative to a 40 pA floor and may be dominated by solver noise.
• Physical: single temperature (27 C), no process corners, no device mismatch, ideal zero-TC resistors; 100 MOhm-20 Gohm on-chip resistors are area-impractical in a real 65 nm flow — the scenario is a modelling abstraction.
• Behaviour through the cycle is checked at four instants (write, min-supply, post-wake, wake peak); slow internal-node relaxation between instants enters the fit but is not separately bounded.

• Author hypothesis (mechanism_survival), unverified: a solver fitting its own basis can absorb secular drift with an extra linear term and see a clean trace while the grader's fixed two-term basis does not — self-checking masks the failure.

• Ideal Gohm resistors and tunnelling-free models make absolute pA currents a simulation artefact rather than a silicon-realistic target; a fabricated cell would show gate leakage dominating and different ageing behaviour (NBTI/HCI, not a body-bias ramp).

tasks.brief:
I need the input sample-and-hold drive for a 12-bit SAR converter in a multi-channel logger. The sample clock comes from a drifting source, so the rate wanders anywhere from 20 to 30 MS/s. The sampling switch is closed for the first 45% of every period, and the held sample must be accurate at the instant it opens. I want a drive that settles cleanly at every rate in the band without ringing.

Fixed parts: a unity-gain buffer drives an output node. That node carries 3 pF of parasitic capacitance to ground, plus your added bypass capacitor. A series damping resistor then connects to the sampling switch, and the switch connects to an 8 pF sampling capacitor to ground. Switch on-resistance is 40 ohm. The buffer is described in full in /app/input_assets/buffer_models.sp. Its gain-bandwidth is set by its bias current. The full-scale input is 1 V, taken as a step from -0.5 V to +0.5 V or the reverse at the start of each window. One LSB is 1 V / 4096.

You choose three values: the series damping resistor (0 to 500 ohm), the bypass capacitor (0 to 50 pF) and the buffer bias current (50 to 400 uA).

Requirements, all measured on the sampling-capacitor voltage. They must hold at every sample rate from 20 to 30 MS/s and in every combination of these corners: buffer gain-bandwidth -25%/+25%, output-node parasitic capacitance -20%/+20%, sampling capacitor -10%/+10%, switch on-resistance -20%/+20%.

1. Error at the instant the switch opens, in each of 20 consecutive windows of alternating full-scale steps, starting with the capacitor and buffer at the opposite polarity: at most 122 uV (0.5 LSB).
2. Same error limit in each of the first 3 windows after power-up, with the capacitor at 0 V and the first input step 0 V to +0.5 V.
3. Overshoot beyond the final value, in any window: at most 5% of the step size (50 mV).
4. Buffer bias current: at most 400 uA.
5. Numerical robustness: the window-end error must be computed accurately enough that refining the numerical resolution of the simulation by a factor of two changes it by at most 25 uV.

Deliver /app/output/design.json with these numeric fields: "rs_ohm", "cb_pf", "ibias_ua".
tasks.handbook:
Conventions and background.

LSB and error: for 12 bits and 1 V full scale, 1 LSB = 244.1 uV and 0.5 LSB = 122.1 uV. Window-end error is |Vcap(t) - Vin| at t = 0.45 x T, where T is the sample period. The window start is the instant the input steps and the switch begins to close. Overshoot is max(Vcap - Vfinal) in the step direction, divided by the 1 V step, over the window.

Stimulus convention: the input alternates between -0.5 V and +0.5 V, changing at the start of each window. Before each step the buffer has been settled for the whole hold phase, and the sampling capacitor holds the previous input. For the power-up case the capacitor and buffer start at 0 V. For the opposite-polarity start, the capacitor and buffer start at -0.5 V and the input steps to +0.5 V. The switch is modelled as a voltage-controlled resistor, ideal in the closed state with the stated on-resistance and 1 Gohm when open, with an edge time of roughly 0.1 to 0.3 ns. Results should not depend materially on the edge time within that range.

The buffer model is a follower. Open-loop DC gain is 70 dB (3162 V/V). The dominant pole sits at GBW/3162. The non-dominant pole is fixed at 400 MHz. The output resistance of 40 ohm lies between the internal amplifier and the output node. Feedback is taken from the output node, so the bypass capacitor and parasitic capacitance are inside the loop. GBW scales linearly with bias current: 120 MHz at 200 uA. The corner percentages scale GBW directly.

Useful practice, as ranges. For a follower with a 400 MHz second pole, loop phase margin typically falls by roughly 10 to 20 degrees as GBW rises from 100 to 250 MHz. Added output-node capacitance lowers phase margin further, because it forms a pole with the 40 ohm output resistance. A series resistor of tens of ohms between the node and a capacitive load usually restores some phase margin. It adds an RC time constant of (Rs + Ron) x Cs, which is about 0.4 to 1.5 ns for these values. Settling a 1 V step to 122 uV needs about 9 time constants, since ln(8192) is about 9. A closed-loop response with phase margin below about 60 degrees shows a visible ringing envelope. The ringing phase relative to the window end shifts with sample rate, so window-end error can vary by an order of magnitude across the band. Linear time-invariant circuits show the same error magnitude for either step polarity once the initial state is the same size.

Band and corner evaluation: rate dependence of the error is not monotonic. Error should be checked at many rates across the band, not only at its ends. Corners combine freely, so 16 extreme combinations plus nominal exist for the four tolerance parameters. Numerical results can differ with the integration method and accuracy settings. Reasonable numerics should agree to within a few uV on a well-damped design.

Design parameter bounds are in the brief. Supply 1.8 V, no slew or headroom limits are modelled, and all elements are linear except the switch timing.
tasks.review:
### 12 · SAR sample-and-hold buffer rate-band settling — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "You choose three values: the series damping resistor (0 to 500 ohm), the bypass capacitor (0 to 50 pF) and the buffer bias current (50 to 400 uA)"

Forge task: Design a unity-gain SAR input drive (select Rs in 0–500 Ω, Cb in 0–50 pF, Ibias in 50–400 µA for a fixed buffer subcircuit) so the 8 pF sampling capacitor settles to ≤122 µV error at the switch-opening instant with ≤5% overshoot across 20–30 MS/s and all 16 combinations of GBW ±25%, Cpar ±20%, Cs ±10%, Ron ±20%, delivered as `/app/output/design.json` with numeric fields rs_ohm, cb_pf, ibias_ua.

Why it fits:
• It is a physical design decision (component value selection in a real mixed-signal network), not analysis of a fixed system.
• ngspice runs headless and can rebuild the circuit from the supplied `.subckt` and check every stated requirement: transient window-end error, overshoot, power-up first-3-window error, and time-step refinement (R5).
• The core difficulty is engineering-real: loop phase margin (fixed 400 MHz second pole, Rout=40 Ω driving node capacitance) trades against RC settling of (Rs+Ron)·Cs, and ringing phase relative to window end shifts non-monotonically across the rate band — exactly the coupled behaviour a knob-turning model gets wrong.
• Bounded parameter space (3 continuous knobs) and one small output file fit a single agent run; no human judgement is needed in grading.

What stops it:
• Structural: none. The task is a bounded parameter-selection problem over a specified, reproducible network.
• Unresolved feasibility risk (not a reason to drop): no passing design is demonstrated — the draft states "no passing reference demonstrated yet" and that its thresholds are provisional estimates (author claim, unverified). Whether a single (Rs, Cb, Ibias) point satisfies R1–R3 at all 17 corner/rate cases simultaneously is an open question until a reference sweep runs.
• Unresolved coverage risk: the brief requires "every sample rate from 20 to 30 MS/s", but the grader samples discrete rates (20, 30 and ≥8 undisclosed). A design failing at an unchecked intermediate rate would pass the grader yet fail the stated requirement.
• Unresolved definition risk: R5 constrains simulation numerics (change ≤25 µV on halving max time step), which is a grader-consistency property rather than a built hardware property; the max-step reference value and integration method are not fixed in the text.
• Runtime risk is unquantified: 17 corner/rate cases × 20 windows × (design sweep + a halved-step re-run) — an author claim of feasibility, with no measured runtime supplied.

How to check it:
• ngspice: rebuild BUF + SWM network from `/app/input_assets/buffer_models.sp`; transient-run 20 alternating ±0.5 V windows per rate/corner, measure |Vcap(0.45T) − Vin| and step-direction overshoot; separately run the 0 V power-up case for 3 windows (G2).
• ngspice (second pass, different integration method/tolerances and switch edge 0.1–0.3 ns): re-run with max time step halved and compare max window-end error (G3).
• A JSON schema check validates rs_ohm/cb_pf/ibias_ua numeric fields and bounds (G1's first step).

Simulation gaps:
• The supplied subcircuit is idealised: no slew rate, no headroom/supply limits (1.8 V stated but not modelled), no noise, no switch charge injection/clock feedthrough, no buffer input capacitance or PSRR — so a passing simulation does not establish silicon behaviour.
• The switch is a behavioural SW model with a 0.05 V hysteresis window and an edge time whose effect is asserted to be immaterial (author claim); edge-time sensitivity at fast ringing rates is unverified.
• GBW corner scaling is assumed to scale the dominant pole linearly; real buffers vary offset, output impedance and second-pole position with bias too.
• Numerical accuracy near 122 µV on a 1 V step (~7e-5 relative) is close to what transient tolerances reliably resolve; R5 partially guards this but the reference step size, method and ngspice version are unspecified.
• Discrete rate grid can alias with ringing zero-crossings; a finite grid cannot prove the continuous-band claim.

Why frontier models fail:
• The bias/settling/damping trade is coupled: raising Ibias helps the slow corner (GBW −25% at 30 MS/s) but erodes phase margin and raises overshoot at GBW +25%, while Rs and the Rout–Cb pole interact inside the loop. Naive "max bandwidth" or "big reservoir" intuitions fail one side of the trade.
• Error vs sample rate is non-monotonic because ringing phase relative to the window end moves; a model that checks only 20 and 30 MS/s or only nominal corners will pick a knife-edge point that fails at held-out rates and corners.
• Robust designs need deliberate margin, not threshold-hugging — a systematic sweep plus margin discipline, which is tedious and easy to shortcut. (Predicted failure is a hypothesis here; no trials are supplied.)

Real-world risks:
• Simulated pass still leaves unmodelled charge injection, switch leakage, clock jitter at the 0.45T aperture instant, resistor tolerance/tempco, PCB parasitics beyond the 3 pF, and buffer noise/offset — none are in the checker.
• The 20 MS/s lower rate is generous in time but the 30 MS/s corner with GBW −25% is the binding constraint; if the true buffer's second pole is below 400 MHz, real settling would be worse than simulated.

Milestones (if too big): not required — one run suffices if the sweep is scripted. If measured sweep runtime exceeds budget, split into: 1. Nominal + slow-corner feasibility sweep (grader: max window-end error ≤122 µV and overshoot ≤5% at 20/30 MS/s, corners GBW ×0.75 and RC-high). 2. Full 17-case verification with halved-step robustness (grader: R1–R5 over all corners and the undisclosed rate set).

What to change (reshape): none required — same device and same core decision. If the SME wants tighter scope, restrict the claim to a specified rate grid rather than the continuous band, or state R5's reference numerics explicitly; these are pinning-down changes, not reshapes.

Numbers to supply next:
• Requirement: rate sampling rule for "every rate in the band" — e.g. verify at 0.25 MS/s steps plus ≥10 uniform-random undisclosed rates in 20–30 MS/s (example).
• Requirement: R5 reference numerics — e.g. max time step 5 ps → 2.5 ps, trap + gear comparison, ngspice 42, reltol 1e-6, and acceptance of ≤25 µV change (example).
• Requirement: overshoot reference for the power-up case — e.g. fraction of the 0.5 V first step vs the 1 V full-scale step (state which).
• Requirement: measured runtime budget for a full corner×rate sweep — e.g. per-case transient ≤2 s wall clock on one core (example; to be measured, not estimated).
• Interface: input `/app/input_assets/buffer_models.sp` (fixed, as embedded); output `/app/output/design.json` schema — {"rs_ohm": number 0–500, "cb_pf": number 0–50, "ibias_ua": number 50–400}; checker rebuilds the network itself.
• Handbook data: corner application table — e.g. GBW ×{0.75, 1.0, 1.25}, Cpar ×{0.8, 1.0, 1.2} on 3 pF, Cs ×{0.9, 1.0, 1.1} on 8 pF, Ron ×{0.8, 1.0, 1.2} on 40 Ω (16 extreme combos + nominal).
• Handbook data: switch model parameters — e.g. SWM(ron=40 roff=1e9 vt=0.5 vh=0.05), edge time sampled in 0.1–0.3 ns.
• Verification still needed: run one reference sweep to demonstrate at least one passing (Rs, Cb, Ibias) point with margin at the slow-GBW/high-RC corner at 30 MS/s and at the +25% GBW corner; reproduce at least one listed public-design failure to calibrate the claimed narrow feasible band; measure sweep runtime and numerical noise floor (uV-level agreement between two integration methods).

Evidence status: draft-only. The buffer/switch netlist is supplied text (establishes the specified dependency, not validated model fidelity); the reference outline, budget fit, public-design failure claims, mechanism-survival narrative and threshold margins are author claims and remain unverified — no simulation output, passing design or runtime measurement is attached. Checkability in principle (ngspice, headless) is assessed from the text; implemented and validated coverage is not established.

Checks before full-task readiness: (1) reproduce a baseline failure of one listed public design to confirm the checks discriminate; (2) demonstrate a passing design with stated margin across all 17 cases and the halved-step re-run; (3) fix the rate-sampling rule, R5 numerics definition and power-up overshoot basis; (4) measure per-case and total sweep runtime and the uV-level numerical agreement between two integration methods; (5) confirm the switch edge-time insensitivity claim empirically in 0.1–0.3 ns.

tasks.brief:
I need the analog sampling stage for our precision acquisition board. It tracks a +/-1.0 V sensor step through a switch, then the switch opens and the held value is read. The board runs unattended in an 85 C chamber for hours, alternating between idle and bursts, so the held value has to be right from the first sample after a transition and every sample after it, anywhere in the clock band.

Fixed inputs are in /app/input_assets/frontend_spec.json: circuit topology, parasitics, switch law, tolerances, and bounds on every design value. In short: clock 67.5 to 82.5 MHz, 50 % duty, switch closed during the first half period and the hold edge at its end. Source resistance 20 ohm. Sample-path loop inductance 18 nH nominal, +/-20 %. Resistors +/-1 %, capacitors +/-5 %.

You choose: sampling capacitor, an optional series R-C damping branch from the sample node to return, a series damping resistor in the signal path, the switch on-resistance setting, and the return-path split fraction (0 to 1; the spec file says what it does).

Definitions. LSB = 2 V / 65536. Held value = sample-node voltage at the hold edge. Held-value error = |held value - input level applied in that cycle|. The input sequence is 40 idle cycles at 0 V, then a 200-cycle burst alternating +1 V / -1 V every cycle (starting at +1 V), then 40 idle cycles at 0 V. At the start of the sequence the capacitors may hold any uniform charge voltage within +/-1 V.

Requirements. Each holds at every clock frequency in the band and across the stated tolerance and inductance ranges.
1. Burst: held-value error <= 0.5 LSB (15.3 uV) in burst cycles 21 to 200.
2. Transitions and idle: held-value error <= 0.5 LSB in the first burst cycle, the first idle cycle after the burst, and idle cycles 21 to 40 of each idle block.
3. Hold-edge timing: requirements 1 and 2 still hold when the hold edge arrives anywhere from 150 ps early to 150 ps late.
4. Noise: sampled kT/C noise at 85 C, computed on the total sample-node capacitance (sampling capacitor at its -5 % corner, parasitic, buffer, switch and split capacitance; damping-branch capacitor excluded), <= 22 uV rms.
5. Capacitor budget: sampling capacitor plus damping-branch capacitor <= 8 pF.
6. Every design value lies inside the bounds given in the spec file.

Deliverable: /app/output/design.json, a JSON object with numeric fields cs_pf, cz_pf (0 if no damping branch), rz_ohm (damping-branch resistor), rd_ohm (series damping resistor in the signal path), ron_ohm (switch on-resistance setting) and split_fraction, in the units named in the spec file.
tasks.handbook:
# Handbook

## Constants and conventions
- Boltzmann constant 1.380649e-23 J/K. At 85 C (358.15 K), kT = 4.94e-21 J.
- Sampled thermal noise on a capacitor C: v_rms = sqrt(kT/C). Resistance does not change the integrated value. 22 uV rms corresponds to a total node capacitance of about 10.2 pF at 358 K.
- LSB = 2 V / 65536 = 30.52 uV. Half an LSB is 15.26 uV. A 2 V step settled to 0.5 LSB needs a residual below about 7.6e-6 of the step, i.e. roughly 11.8 time constants of a single-pole decay.
- Half period: 7.41 ns at 67.5 MHz, 6.06 ns at 82.5 MHz. The shortest acquisition window is at the top of the band.

## Second-order sample node
A series resistance R, inductance L and node capacitance C form a second-order network. Natural frequency w0 = 1/sqrt(LC), damping ratio zeta = (R/2)*sqrt(C/L). A step residual decays as exp(-zeta*w0*t) when under-damped. The ring phase at a fixed time depends on the damped frequency, which moves with L and C. When over-damped, the slow pole is approximately 1/(R*C) and settling becomes slow. The settling error at a fixed hold time therefore depends on both the decay rate and the oscillation phase. Component tolerances, the signal-dependent switch resistance and the clock period all shift these quantities. Series resistance in the loop includes the source resistance, any series damping resistor, the switch on-resistance and the added return-path resistance.

## Memory mechanisms in sampled stages
- Incomplete settling: charge from the previous sample remains on the node capacitances. The fraction left equals the settling residual.
- Dielectric absorption: a small fraction of capacitance sits behind a long time constant. The spec file gives this branch (0.1 % of the sampling capacitor, 5 us). It holds a slow average of past samples and leaks it back.
- Initial charge: with the settling times involved, its influence has decayed by cycle 21.

## Reading the spec file
- Switch resistance is a function of the node voltage v in volts: ron_ohm*(1 + 0.2 v + 0.1 v^2). It runs from about 0.9 to 1.3 times the setting over +/-1 V.
- The split fraction f scales the loop inductance to L*(1 - 0.5 f), adds 3f ohm to the series resistance and adds 0.3f pF at the sample node.
- Charge injection from the switch is not modelled. The buffer input is a pure capacitance, and the buffer is not part of the held-value measurement.
- Resistor tolerance applies to rd, rz, ron and the 20 ohm source. Capacitor tolerance applies to cs, cz and the fixed capacitances. Inductance tolerance applies to the 18 nH. Every tolerance is taken as a uniform range, and the corners are the extremes.
- The clock band is continuous, so intermediate frequencies matter, not only the band edges.
tasks.review:
### 30 · Sampled-data input stage clock-band settling — advance, rank 8
Design decision as written: yes — "You choose: sampling capacitor, an optional series R-C damping branch from the sample node to return, a series damping resistor in the signal path, the switch on-resistance setting, and the return-path split fraction (0 to 1)"
Forge task: Choose the six design values (cs_pf, cz_pf, rz_ohm, rd_ohm, ron_ohm, split_fraction) of a switched-capacitor sample stage so the held value at the hold edge is within 0.5 LSB of the applied level in the first burst cycle, all later burst cycles, the first idle cycle after the burst and idle cycles 21-40, at every clock frequency in 67.5-82.5 MHz, across resistor/capacitor/inductance tolerances, any uniform initial charge within +/-1 V, and a hold edge anywhere in -150 ps to +150 ps, while sampled kT/C noise at 85 C is <= 22 uV rms and cs+cz <= 8 pF.
Why it fits:
  • Design decision as written: the agent selects six physical component/setting values inside given bounds; the deliverable is a design, not an analysis or a tool.
  • Checkable in full within the stated model: ngspice (or another SPICE-class engine) can build the RLC sample node with the specified Ron(v) law, DA branch and split-fraction parameterisation, run the 40/200/40 sequence, and read the sample-node voltage at the hold edge; an independent Python state-space integration with different switch discretisation cross-checks the same metric. G3 is closed-form arithmetic (kT/C and cs+cz).
  • The physics that decides the design is genuinely coupled: settling envelope (zeta*w0) and ring phase (damped frequency moving with L and C) both determine the residual at a fixed hold time, while Ron varies with node voltage, the clock period varies across the band, and the noise/capacitance budget caps how small cs can be. Rough sizing shows the space is non-empty: noise needs total node capacitance >= ~10.2 pF, fixed node capacitance is 6.5 pF + 0.3f pF, so cs at its -5% corner must be >= ~3.4-3.6 pF, inside the 1.0-8.0 pF bound; settling to 0.5 LSB on a 2 V step needs roughly 11.8 time constants inside a 6.06 ns window at 82.5 MHz, which forces near-critical damping rather than either extreme of the resistor range.
  • Robustness, not nominal optimisation, is the core requirement: held-out in-band frequencies, random in-draw tolerances, initial charges and +/-150 ps edge shifts punish knife-edge ring-phase designs, so the agent must trade noise and capacitance headroom for damping margin — a real engineering trade-off.
What stops it:
  • Structural objections: none identified. The idea asks for a design decision, the model is closed and specified, and a reference solution is plausible within the stated bounds.
  • Unresolved feasibility risks (not structural): (a) no passing reference design has been demonstrated — the reference_outline and the public_designs failure claims are author assertions, unverified here; (b) the pass criterion over "randomised tolerance draws" is not numerically defined (how many draws, which corners, whether worst-of-random or worst-of-corners is binding), so a design could pass one grader instantiation and fail another; (c) runtime is unmeasured: 280-cycle transients at ~1.9 us of simulated time, refined enough to resolve a 150 ps edge shift (timestep on the order of a few ps), repeated over 12+ frequencies, tolerance draws, offsets and two implementations, is plausibly tens of seconds to minutes per candidate in SPICE — a full search must lean on the fast state-space model, with SPICE reserved for verification; (d) the initial-condition statement (all capacitors may hold a uniform charge within +/-1 V) appears to conflict with the DA branch "starting discharged" and needs one sentence of clarification.
How to check it:
  • ngspice (or xyce): transient of the specified RLC node with the Ron(v) = ron*(1+0.2v+0.1v^2) law, DA branch (Cda = 0.001*cs, Rda = 5e-6/Cda), split-fraction L/R/C modification; reads sample-node voltage at the hold edge for every cycle of the 40/200/40 sequence at held-out clock frequencies, tolerance draws, inductance values, initial charges and hold-edge shifts.
  • Independent Python state-space integrator (different switch discretisation and timestep): same per-cycle held values; agreement of both implementations is the pass criterion for R1-R3.
  • Arithmetic script for R4/R5/R6: total node capacitance at cs -5% corner plus 4 pF + 2 pF + 0.5 pF + 0.3f, kT/C at 358.15 K; cs+cz sum; bounds check against frontend_spec.json.
Simulation gaps:
  • The model omits charge injection, buffer input current/nonlinearity, switch leakage and charge sharing with the buffer beyond a pure capacitance, so passing simulations do not establish a passing board.
  • Dielectric absorption is a single 0.1 % / 5 us branch; real C0G/NP0 or film capacitors have multi-time-constant absorption spectra that a single branch under-represents.
  • Ron(v) is an analytic law, not a device model; real MOS switch resistance also depends on temperature, supply, body effect and process spread beyond the stated +/-1 % resistor tolerance.
  • Jitter is only the stated +/-150 ps edge offset; edge slew rate and clock phase noise are not modelled.
  • Numerical accuracy at the 15 uV level over a 2 V step requires roughly 1e-7 relative accuracy in a 1.9 us transient; both implementations need an explicit timestep-convergence demonstration (halving the step changes held error by < 1 uV), otherwise solver noise can masquerade as settling error or hide it.
  • The two implementations share the same analytic spec, so cross-agreement validates numerics, not physics.
Why frontier models fail:
  • Hypothesis, not demonstrated by trials: the trap is a design that clears the agent's own nominal/corner sweep but sits at a lightly damped ring whose residual at the hold edge swings by an order of magnitude with a few percent change in L, R, or clock frequency — moving the ring phase moves the residual at a fixed hold time, so a thin-margin optimum fails at some held-out point. Choosing near-critical damping deliberately costs noise and capacitance headroom (R4, R5), and accepting that cost is the engineering judgement required. A model that optimises point-wise instead of worst-case, or that treats the clock band as its two edges only, is likely to fail; so is one that over-damps into the slow pole and misses the 6.06 ns window.
Real-world risks:
  • Charge injection and pedestal error are unmodelled and can exceed 0.5 LSB (15.3 uV) at these levels; buffer bias current and leakage add drift over hours at 85 C.
  • PCB layout parasitics (via/trace inductance, ground return geometry behind the split fraction) are lumped into one L and one f; the realised loop inductance and the meaning of f are layout-dependent.
  • Component drift at 85 C over hours, self-heating during bursts, and 1/f noise are outside the kT/C-only noise budget; total noise will exceed the 22 uV figure.
  • Long-run DA memory of the burst edge into the first idle cycles is modelled by one branch only; real absorption tails could bias the first idle cycles specified in R2.
Milestones (if too big): none required — the six-value configuration search with a fast state-space evaluator plus SPICE verification plausibly fits one run, subject to the runtime check below. If measurement shows otherwise, split as: 1. analytic sizing + fast-model sweep: grader checks noise/budget arithmetic and a nominal-temperature state-space pass at band edges; 2. full robust verification across held-out frequencies, tolerances, initial charges and edge shifts with the two implementations.
What to change (reshape): nothing; advance as written once the numbers below are supplied.
Numbers to supply next:

Also state whether the agent is told the seed count.
  • Requirement (missing spec): hold-edge shift coverage and timestep — e.g. "grader evaluates shifts {-150, -75, 0, +75, +150} ps plus held-out shifts; solver timestep <= 5 ps, converged to < 1 uV in held error under halving".
  • Requirement (clarify): initial condition — e.g. "all node capacitances including the DA branch start at one uniform voltage in [-1, 1] V", resolving the conflict with "Cda ... starting discharged".
  • Requirement (verification still needed): a demonstrated passing reference design with its worst-case margins, and reproduction of at least one claimed public-design failure (e.g. the f=0, small-rd ring) as a baseline sanity check.
  • Interface: input /app/input_assets/frontend_spec.json (as supplied); output /app/output/design.json with exactly the six numeric fields cs_pf, cz_pf, rz_ohm, rd_ohm, ron_ohm, split_fraction in pF/ohm/ohm/ohm/ohm/fraction, plus a machine-readable copy of the R1-R6 limits so the agent can self-check.

tasks.brief:
Conditioning block for a 16-bit multiplexed data-acquisition card, shared by all channels, one sample per 1 us slot. No memory of the previous slot; clean start without warm-up samples.

Interface: subcircuit BLOCK, ports inp inn phi1 phi2 vdd vref out gnd.
- inp/inn: differential inputs behind 1 kOhm source resistance per leg; common mode 1.45 to 1.85 V.
- phi1/phi2: 1.000 MHz (+/-2 %) two-phase non-overlapping clock, 0 to VDD, 5 ns non-overlap.
- VDD 3.0 to 3.6 V; vref is an ideal VDD/2.
- out: single-ended, loaded by 10 pF in parallel with 100 kOhm to gnd, sampled 5 ns before end of phase 2 each period.

Allowed parts: resistors 100 Ohm to 1 MOhm; capacitors; switches of model SWM (on-resistance 200 Ohm to 5 kOhm); instances of subcircuit OPAMP (open-loop gain 60 to 80 dB, GBW 1 to 40 MHz, supply current 0.4 mA per 20 MHz of GBW), from models.spice; ideal logic sources driving only switch controls.

Each capacitor has 0.1 % (1 sigma) random error plus a parasitic of 5 % of its value from its second-listed node to gnd. Put no analysis commands, initial conditions or model definitions in the netlist.

Each requirement holds over all stated ranges and start states.

R1. Gain, differential input to (out - vref) at 10 kHz: 1.88 to 2.12 V/V.
R2. SNDR, 10 kHz 1.0 Vpp differential tone, 2048 consecutive slots after 20 settling slots: at least 60 dB.
R3. Input +1 V differential for 40 slots, then 0 V: first output sample at 0 V, relative to the settled zero-input output, at most 0.3 % of the settled +1 V output.
R4. Input held at 0 V or +0.8 V differential: every output sample from slot 20 to 40 within 1 mV of the value after 300 slots.
R5. 1.0 Vpp differential tone from 960 kHz to 1.04 MHz: sampled output component at the alias frequency at least 20 dB below 1.0 Vpp times the 10 kHz gain.
R6. Average vdd current during the tone test at most 1.2 mA.
R7. Total capacitance at most 60 pF.
R8. Numerical consistency: gain, SNDR and memory error must be insensitive to simulation resolution, within the limits in the handbook.
R9. Construction: only the allowed parts above.

Deliverable: /app/output/block.cir containing BLOCK; conventions in the handbook.
tasks.handbook:
# Handbook: conditioning block

## Supplied models (models.spice)
The file defines:
- global parameters RON and A0DB (defaults 1000 Ohm and 70 dB);
- switch model SWM, a voltage-controlled switch with Roff = 1e12 Ohm, threshold 1.65 V and hysteresis 0.05 V;
- subcircuit OPAMP with ports inp inn out vdd gnd and parameter GBW.

OPAMP is a single-pole transconductance stage with DC gain 10^(A0DB/20). Its output is clamped to 0.1 V above gnd and 0.1 V below vdd, with 100 Ohm of series output resistance. It draws a constant 0.4 mA x GBW/20 MHz from vdd. Your netlist must not redefine SWM, OPAMP, RON or A0DB.

The checker substitutes RON anywhere from 200 Ohm to 5 kOhm and A0DB anywhere from 60 to 80 dB. Switches close when their control exceeds about 1.65 V. Charge injection and leakage are not modelled.

## Environment seen by BLOCK
- Each input leg is driven through exactly 1 kOhm from an ideal source. The differential voltage vd = V(inp) - V(inn), and the common mode is the mean of the two legs.
- The clock has 1 ns edges. Each phase is high for half a period minus 5 ns, and phi1 is high first.
- The differential input changes only at the start of a period (phi1 rising edge) for step and DC tests. The tone is a continuous sinusoid. The input is constant within each slot.
- The sampling instant is 5 ns before the falling edge of phi2. Every metric uses the output sampled once per period at that instant. The clock period for each run is 1/f_clk, with f_clk anywhere from 0.98 to 1.02 MHz.
- Capacitor handling: each capacitor C n1 n2 value is multiplied by (1 + 0.001 g), with g a Gaussian draw, independently per capacitor and per run. A parasitic capacitor of 0.05 x value is then added from n2 to gnd.
- Initial state: every node touching a capacitor is initialised to a random voltage between 0 V and VDD, set by the checker.

## Metric definitions
- **Gain (R1):** amplitude of the output component at 10 kHz, divided by the 10 kHz input amplitude, with a 1.0 Vpp differential tone. It is found by least-squares fit after 20 settling slots.
- **SNDR (R2):** the 2048 samples are windowed with a 4-term Blackman-Harris window. Tone power is taken in the 9 bins around the tone. Error power is all remaining bins from bin 3 to the Nyquist bin, which excludes DC and offset; everything except the tone and DC counts as error. Noise is not simulated. SNDR = 10 log10(tone/error).
- **Memory (R3):** y0 is the first output sample after the input changes from +1 V to 0 V at a period boundary. yss0 is the settled zero-input output, taken after 40 further slots. yss1 is the settled output with +1 V input. Memory error = |y0 - yss0| / |yss1 - yss0| x 100 %.
- **State return (R4):** the reference value is the mean of samples 290 to 300 of the same run. Samples 20 to 40 are compared with it, for every random start and for the zero start.
- **Rejection (R5):** the output sequence (sampled at f_clk) is fitted by least squares with a sinusoid at |f - f_clk|, plus a constant, over 1024 slots after 20 settling slots. Tones within 3 kHz of f_clk are not used for the alias fit. The rejection is 20 log10( G10k x 1.0 V / alias amplitude ), with G10k from the same corner.
- **Current (R6):** the mean of the current out of the vdd source over the whole tone-test window.
- **Capacitance (R7):** the sum of all capacitor values written in the netlist before the checker's modifications.
- **Numerical consistency (R8):** the checker re-runs each case with the simulation timestep halved and compares the metrics. The gain must change by at most 0.2 %, the SNDR by at most 0.5 dB, and the memory error by at most 0.05 percentage points.

## Ranges used for checking
The checker draws start states, corner values and seeds inside the declared ranges, including values between the extremes. Do not rely on the extremes alone.
- f_clk: 0.98 to 1.02 MHz
- VDD: 3.0 to 3.6 V
- common mode: 1.45 to 1.85 V
- RON: 200 to 5000 Ohm
- A0DB: 60 to 80 dB

## Background
- An ideal sampled output of a signal with energy near f_clk folds to |f - f_clk|.
- A switch with on-resistance Ron discharging a capacitor C leaves a fraction exp(-t/(Ron C)) of the initial voltage after time t.
- Capacitor mismatch between parallel signal paths shows up as spurs at multiples of f_clk/2 plus or minus the tone frequency.
- An op-amp integrator or switched-capacitor stage with finite gain A transfers charge with a relative error of about 1/A.
- kT/C noise and thermal noise are not part of any metric.
tasks.review:
### 14-mux-daq-conditioning-block-no-memory · Shared-channel differential-to-single-ended conditioning block — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "Conditioning block for a 16-bit multiplexed data-acquisition card, shared by all channels, one sample per 1 us slot" with "Deliverable: /app/output/block.cir containing BLOCK"; the agent chooses the topology and sizes every resistor, capacitor, switch and OPAMP instance.

Forge task: Design a differential-to-single-ended conditioning subcircuit BLOCK (ports inp inn phi1 phi2 vdd vref out gnd) from R, C, SWM switches and OPAMP instances that meets R1 gain 1.88–2.12 V/V at 10 kHz, R2 SNDR ≥ 60 dB over 2048 slots, R3 slot memory ≤ 0.3%, R4 start-state return ≤ 1 mV by slot 20, R5 ≥ 20 dB rejection of 960–1040 kHz tones at the alias, R6 ≤ 1.2 mA average vdd current, R7 ≤ 60 pF total capacitance, R8 timestep insensitivity, over f_clk 0.98–1.02 MHz, VDD 3.0–3.6 V, vcm 1.45–1.85 V, RON 200–5000 Ohm, A0 60–80 dB, random capacitor errors/parasitics and random start states.

Why it fits:
• The deliverable is a design artifact (netlist topology and component values in a fixed part library), not a measurement, analysis or tool.
• ngspice runs headless and reproduces every stated metric: transient of the checker bench with 1 ns clock edges and the defined sampling instant; numpy then does the least-squares 10 kHz gain, the 4-term Blackman-Harris SNDR with the fixed bin convention, the alias sinusoid-plus-constant fit, memory/state-return errors and mean vdd current; a static Python parse covers R7 and R9.
• The constraints are coupled through mechanisms the supplied models do capture (sinc/alias null placement vs clock spread, dump completeness vs RON and C, finite-gain charge transfer vs memory, GBW vs current, two-path mismatch vs SNDR spurs), so this is genuine mixed-signal trade-off work rather than hidden-rule tedium.
• The brief already fixes ports, environment, metric definitions and ranges, so the design problem is well posed as written.

What stops it:
• Structural: nothing in the idea requires physics that a headless tool cannot check, since the model world is explicitly self-consistent and noise/charge injection are declared out of scope.
• Unresolved feasibility risk: no passing design has been shown. The reference outline is labelled untested with provisional thresholds, and the stated margins are narrow (author-estimated ~24 dB worst-case alias rejection against a 20 dB limit; R3 memory 0.3% against finite-gain charge error ~1/A ≈ 0.1% at 60 dB and dump residual exp(-t/(RON*C)) at RON 5 kOhm; R2 60 dB against 0.1% capacitor mismatch spurs). If no configuration satisfies R1–R8 at once, the task has no solution and would need re-scoping.
• Unresolved runtime risk: the grading suite runs 20+2048 slot transients plus 1024-slot alias runs across corners, starts and seeds and repeats at a halved timestep; measured ngspice runtime is unknown and could break the one-run budget.

How to check it:
• ngspice: wrap block.cir in the checker bench (models.spice with RON/A0DB overridden, 1 kOhm source legs, two-phase 1 ns-edge clock, 10 pF || 100 kOhm load, per-run 0.1% Gaussian capacitor error plus 5% bottom-plate parasitic, checker-supplied .ic), transient across the declared ranges, sample 5 ns before the phi2 falling edge.
• Python/numpy: gain fit, Blackman-Harris SNDR per the handbook bins, alias fit at |f - f_clk| excluding tones within 3 kHz of f_clk, memory error and state-return error, mean vdd source current.
• Static parse: element whitelist, logic sources feeding only switch controls, no .tran/.ic/.model/.param lines, capacitance sum with 0.5% allowance; timestep-halved repeats for R8.

Simulation gaps:
• Charge injection and leakage are not modelled (stated in the handbook), yet they are exactly the effects that set real slot-to-slot memory.
• Noise (kT/C, thermal) is not simulated, so R2's 60 dB SNDR is a distortion/spur limit only; a 60 pF budget with 1 kOhm sources sits near the real thermal floor.
• The OPAMP macro has no slew rate, no input common-mode limit, no output current limit (only a clamped behavioural output and 100 Ohm Ro), no PSRR/CMRR; the switch has no parasitic capacitance.
• Real capacitor voltage/temperature coefficients, layout parasitics and component matching are absent; only a 0.1% Gaussian plus a fixed 5% parasitic is applied.

Why frontier models fail:
• Hypothesis, not evidenced by trials: one set of values must satisfy alias rejection, complete slot reset, current and capacitance simultaneously over RON 200–5000 Ohm, A0 60–80 dB, f_clk ±2% and random starts/mismatch.
• Ordinary continuous-time filters and naive track-and-hold fail R3 or R5 (author's claimed public-design failures, unverified); a single-path integrate-and-dump over phase 2 gives only a few dB of alias rejection; two-path ping-pong trades mismatch spurs against reset completeness.
• Expect nominal-corner designs to look clean and then fail on held-out seeds and interior corner points; only solver-run trials would confirm this.

Real-world risks:
• A passing netlist is validated only inside the declared model world; a build would face charge injection, kT/C noise, real amplifier settling/slew and capacitor matching, plus PCB/layout parasitics.
• The constant 0.4 mA per 20 MHz GBW bias model understates real amplifier current under a 10 pF load, so R6 is a proxy rather than a real power spec.

Milestones (if too big):
1. Short-window design: topology and sizing validated on 64–128 slot runs; grader checks R1, R3, R4, R6, R7, R9 on those windows.
2. Full-length validation: 2048-slot SNDR (R2), 1024-slot alias rejection (R5) across corners and seeds, plus the timestep-halved repeat (R8).
Keep the split only if measured full-length runtime breaks the one-run budget.

What to change (reshape):
• None as written. Only if the reference simulations show the R1–R8 window is empty should the vendor reconsider a limit or the allowed part set; that would be a spec change to propose, not one to make at this stage.

• Requirement (missing specification): corner and seed sampling plan per grader case — e.g. zero start plus 3 seeded random starts x 5 interior corners (f_clk 1.013 MHz, RON 3.3 kOhm, A0 66 dB, VDD 3.17 V, vcm 1.80 V).
• Interface (missing specification): the checker bench as an input asset — e.g. /app/input_assets/bench.cir including models.spice plus the measurement script, so the agent can reproduce the metrics.
• Interface (missing specification): netlist scope — state whether BLOCK may contain helper .subckt lines and whether any OPAMP instance count is capped (e.g. helper subcircuits allowed, no instance cap).
• Handbook data (missing specification): ngspice version and .tran options used by the checker — e.g. ngspice 42, transient run without uic, .ic supplied by the checker.

tasks.brief:
I need the input stage for a field sensor board: a regulator that turns the 24 V harness feed into a 5 V rail for a switching-load sensor module. The board hangs off a long cable and the ceramic input capacitor cannot be removed. Sometimes the board powers up from rest, sometimes after a brownout with its capacitors still charged. Both cases must end at the same rail with no lingering oscillation.

Fixed interfaces:
- Harness: ideal source anywhere from 18 to 32 V, through 8 uH series inductance (tolerance +/-30%) and 0.35 ohm to board node vin.
- Input ceramic at vin: 4.7 uF nominal (+/-20%), 5 mohm ESR, fixed. Its capacitance falls with DC bias (handbook, model in file).
- Load on vout: current sink alternating between 40 mA and 600 mA, 50% duty, 2 us linear edges, repetition rate anywhere from 1 to 50 kHz.
- /app/input_assets/fixed_parts.cir holds the pass element, error amplifier, reference and ceramic-capacitor models. Use them by name and do not redefine them. Exactly one pass element, one error amplifier and one reference block are used. Everything else is resistors, inductors, diodes (model dgen) and the supplied ceramic-capacitor model. All capacitors, including compensation, use that model.

Requirements. Each must hold at nominal and at corners: cable inductance +/-30%, capacitor values +/-20%, resistors +/-1%, inductors +/-20%, harness voltage anywhere in 18 to 32 V.
1. Cold start: all nodes at 0 V, harness ramps 0 to its value in 50 us. Vout peak is at most 5.5 V. With a constant 40 mA or 600 mA load, vout is 4.90 to 5.10 V at 5 ms and later.
2. Warm start: harness already at its value, vout pre-charged anywhere in 0 to 5.5 V, input ceramic pre-charged anywhere in 0 to 32 V. Vout never exceeds 5.5 V. The settled DC rail (mean over 0.5 ms after 5 ms, constant load) is within 20 mV of the cold-start value for the same harness voltage, load and corner.
3. Toggling load, 1 to 50 kHz, from either start: rail ripple at most 150 mV peak to peak over the last 5 cycles after 4 ms.
4. Same condition: cycle-to-cycle variation of the rail's maximum and of its minimum over those 5 cycles is at most 3 mV each.
5. Harness step 18 to 32 V and 32 to 18 V (10 us linear), constant 40 mA or 600 mA load: vout returns to within 50 mV of its pre-step value within 200 us and stays there.
6. The measured ripple and recovery time must not depend on time resolution: with the time resolution of the simulation doubled, the ripple changes by at most 3 mV and the recovery time by at most 10 us.
7. Parts: at most 25 resistors, inductors, diodes and capacitors in total, excluding the three supplied blocks. Total nominal capacitance of the added capacitors is at most 22 uF.

Deliverable: /app/output/regulator.cir, a SPICE netlist containing one subcircuit named reg with ports vin vout gnd (gnd is ground), one component per line. Capacitor, resistor and inductor values are written as plain numbers or parameters.
tasks.handbook:
# Handbook

## Supplied models (fixed_parts.cir)
- pass d g s: n-channel square-law device, threshold 2 V, transconductance 2 A/V^2 (device W/L = 1), small channel-length modulation, gate capacitances 300 pF (g-s) and 50 pF (g-d). Connect drain to vin, source to vout, gate to the error amplifier output.
- ea ref fb g: transconductance amplifier injecting current into g when ref exceeds fb. Small-signal gm 10 mS, output current limited to +/-2 mA (tanh law), output resistance 5 Mohm, soft clamp keeping g between 0 and 12 V. Input pins are high impedance. Compensation components go on g.
- vrefblk vin ref: 1.25 V reference that follows vin during power-up (full value once vin is about 6 V or more) through a 10 kohm internal output resistance.
- cdr a b c0= esr=: ceramic capacitor. Effective capacitance = c0 * (1 - 0.6 * (min(max(Vdc,0),32)/32)^1.2), in series with esr. Vdc is the voltage across the capacitor. Tolerance applies to c0.
- dgen: generic silicon junction diode (Is 1e-12 A, N 1, Rs 0.1 ohm).

## Derating table (capacitance fraction of nominal vs DC bias)
0 V: 1.00; 8 V: 0.89; 16 V: 0.74; 24 V: 0.58; 32 V: 0.40. Above 32 V the fraction stays at 0.40. This applies to every cdr instance, input and added alike.

## Tolerance corners
Cable inductance 5.6 to 10.4 uH. Capacitor c0 within +/-20%. Resistors +/-1%. Added inductors +/-20%. Corners are applied to the delivered netlist's values and may be combined.

## Measurement definitions
- Rail ripple: maximum minus minimum of v(vout) over the stated window.
- Cycle-to-cycle variation: within the last 5 load cycles, the spread (max minus min) of the 5 per-cycle maxima, and separately of the 5 per-cycle minima.
- Cold-start reference value: mean of v(vout) over 0.5 ms after 5 ms, same harness voltage, constant load, same corner.
- Recovery time: time from the start of the harness step until v(vout) enters and stays within 50 mV of its pre-step mean.
- Part count: lines starting with R, L, D, or X (capacitor model instances) inside reg, excluding pass, ea and vrefblk.
- Pre-charge states are applied as initial conditions on the input-capacitor node and on vout. Remaining nodes start at 0 V (cold) or settle from there. The inductor current starts at 0.
- Load toggling starts at t = 0 with the heavy-current level, so it overlaps the start-up in the toggling runs.

## General engineering background
- Multilayer ceramic capacitors have ESR roughly 2 to 10 mohm at 10 to 100 kHz. Class-II dielectrics lose capacitance with DC bias and the loss depends on voltage rating and case size. They have negligible dielectric damping.
- A cable inductance in series with a low-ESR ceramic forms an LC resonance whose characteristic impedance and Q follow from L, C and the series resistance.
- Capacitors on the error-amplifier output integrate; its current limit makes large-signal behaviour (start-up, steps) differ from small-signal behaviour. Integrator charge accumulated while the amplifier is saturated can persist after the rail reaches regulation.
- Resistor values in practice come from E96 series; film resistors 1%, ceramic NP0/X7R capacitors 5 to 20%.
- Simulation conventions: the harness source and the load are ideal. The output ripple is measured at the vout node, not at the load terminals through any extra trace.
tasks.review:
### 00-harness-fed-5v-regulator-stage · Start-state-independent 5 V regulator stage — advance, rank 8

Design decision as written: yes — "a regulator that turns the 24 V harness feed into a 5 V rail ... Deliverable: /app/output/regulator.cir, a SPICE netlist containing one subcircuit named reg with ports vin vout gnd". The agent chooses the loop topology, compensation, input damping, soft-start and all added R/L/D/cdr values.

Forge task: Design a 24 V-harness-fed 5 V linear regulator input stage (one supplied pass element, one error amplifier, one reference block, plus at most 25 R/L/dgen/cdr parts and at most 22 uF total added nominal capacitance) whose cold-start peak, warm-start peak and warm-vs-cold settled-rail difference, load-toggle ripple and cycle-to-cycle spread, harness-step recovery and timestep-insensitivity all hold at nominal and at declared tolerance corners. Output is /app/output/regulator.cir.

Why it fits:
• It is a configuration design task: a netlist with chosen topology and values, not an analysis or measurement exercise.
• Every requirement row maps to a scripted ngspice bench plus Python metric extraction (peak, settled mean, ripple, per-cycle maxima/minima spread, settling time, timestep-difference deltas) and static netlist parsing for R7.
• Difficulty is engineering-real: coupled input LC resonance, class-II capacitance derating with DC bias, transconductance-amplifier integrator saturation/windup, and identical end state from cold and warm starts across corners — a genuine trade-off space, not hidden rules.
• Bounded deliverable (one netlist, one subckt) fits a single agent run of design + local sweeps.

What stops it:
• Structural: none identified. The device and core decision (topology + compensation + damping + values for a harness-fed 5 V regulator) stay intact.
• Unresolved feasibility risks (author claims, unverified): the joint R3 150 mV ripple and R4 3 mV cycle-to-cycle spread at 560 mA steps over 1-50 kHz, with only 22 uF added capacitance and 200 us recovery, may be simultaneously unreachable; the draft itself states "No passing reference has been demonstrated" and its claimed public-design failures are hypotheses, not evidence.
• Unresolved checkability risks: the supplied behavioural models use max/min/pow/tanh expressions; discontinuous derivative behaviour at clamp edges may make R6 (timestep and integrator-method independence) a numerical artefact rather than a design property, and may force timestep-independent results regardless of design — needs demonstration in ngspice before the row is trusted.
• Unresolved runtime: the corner x Vin x load x pre-charge x toggle-frequency matrix is verifier-side and unstated; measured wall time is unknown.

How to check it:
• Python netlist parser (G1): counts R/L/D/X lines in reg excluding pass, ea, vrefblk, sums cdr c0, rejects other element types or redefinitions, verifies exactly one of each supplied block.
• ngspice (G2-G5, G7): cold-start ramp, warm-start initial-condition grid and random points, toggling load at held-out frequencies, harness 18<->32 V steps, run at nominal and at mixed-sign corners (cable L x0.7/x1.3, c0 x0.8/x1.2, R +/-1%, added L +/-20%) applied to the delivered netlist text; Python extracts the stated metrics.
• ngspice (G6): rerun with maximum timestep halved and with a different integration method; compare ripple and recovery deltas.
• Note: these are the proposed checks; none has been executed or validated here.

Simulation gaps:
• LEVEL=1 square-law pass device and tanh transconductance amplifier are idealised: no mobility/temperature effects, no real error-amplifier supply rejection, no MOSFET SOA, self-heating or package parasitics.
• The ceramic model derates only with DC bias per a fixed law; no temperature, ageing, tolerance-of-ESR, or piezoelectric effects; added capacitors are all forced to this one model.
• Harness and load are ideal; no cable resistance tolerance (0.35 ohm fixed), no harness capacitance, no PCB trace/loop parasitics, no conducted-EMI or stability with a real sensor module beyond the stated current sink.
• Real silicon loop stability (phase margin with device capacitance variation, PCB layout coupling) is not covered by a netlist-only check.

Why frontier models fail:
• A plausible hypothesis (the draft states it, unverified): a model that tunes from rest at nominal and checks its own timestep sees a clean 5 V rail, while the hard rows sit at derated 32 V bias, +30% cable L, toggle rates near the ~40 kHz input resonance, and pre-charged warm starts where error-amplifier integrator windup persists.
• Meeting R4 (3 mV cycle-to-cycle) and R6 together demands deliberate damping plus a loop that is both fast (R5) and periodic at 50 kHz; this is a coupled trade-off, not a single analytic fix.

Real-world risks:
• A design that passes the behavioural benches may still ring or overheat with real component spread, real ESR/ESL and real load transients; netlist-level success does not establish manufacturability or EMC.
• Passing R2 only at the sampled pre-charge grid does not prove start-state independence everywhere in the continuous 0-5.5 V x 0-32 V box.

Milestones (if too big): not required; the deliverable is one netlist and one agent run is plausible, subject to the runtime question above. If corner runtime proves excessive, split as: 1. nominal cold/warm/toggle/step benches: passes R1-R5 at nominal; 2. full corner + held-out frequency + timestep sweep: passes R1-R6 at corners.

What to change (reshape): nothing structural. Pin down the open items listed below.

Numbers to supply next:
  • Requirement: base maximum timestep and integration methods for R6 — e.g. default .tran with max step 5 ns, comparison runs at 2.5 ns, methods trap and gear; state whether absolute tolerances (reltol/vntol) are fixed too.
  • Requirement: simulation horizon and window anchors — e.g. run to 10 ms; settled mean over [5.0 ms, 5.5 ms]; toggle metric window "last 5 load cycles after 4 ms" anchored at verifier-chosen cycle boundaries.
  • Requirement: minimum corner sampling policy for G7 — e.g. at least 12 mixed-sign corner combinations plus the extremes, and at least 3 held-out toggle frequencies per bench.
  • Requirement: whether added resistor/capacitor values must be E96/E24 series values or may be any number — e.g. E96 for R, any value for cdr c0/esr; state the allowed esr range for added cdr instances (currently only 5 mohm shown).
  • Interface: exact bench netlist snippets (harness source with 50 us ramp, 8 uH/0.35 ohm cable, load current sink 40/600 mA with 2 us edges at verifier-chosen 1-50 kHz, and how .ic pre-charges are applied to vout and the input-ceramic node) so the agent can reproduce the checker benches locally.
  • Interface: confirm /app/input_assets/fixed_parts.cir is delivered byte-identical to the embedded text and that it parses in the pinned ngspice version; output schema as stated (one component per line, plain numbers/parameters).
  • Handbook data: pinned ngspice version and behavioural-expression support (pow, max, min, tanh in B-sources); whether diode dgen may be used unlimited within the 25-part cap; tolerance application convention (all corners combined simultaneously as stated in G7).
  • Verification still needed (not missing specifications): demonstrate in ngspice that the supplied models converge and that R6 metrics are numerically meaningful (repeat a known netlist at 2x/0.5x step and two integrators and confirm deltas are dominated by design, not solver noise); demonstrate at least one netlist meeting R1-R5 at nominal before treating feasibility as established; measure verifier-side runtime of the full corner matrix.

Evidence status: draft-only input. The reference outline, distinct_valid_designs, public-design failure claims, mechanism-survival narrative and provisional thresholds are author claims, unverified. The fixed_parts.cir content is supplied text establishing what models are specified, not proof the file exists on disk or that it has been simulated. No simulation, corner sweep, passing design, runtime measurement or numerical-noise study has been inspected.
